Context
The Customer Support (CS) organization is responsible for the installations, qualification, repair and maintenance of the ASML systems at customer sites and is responsible for the necessary transfer of know-how to the customer. Local site Customer Support branches perform these tasks for the customer within the specific region.

Anticipates, analyzes and solves complex technical problems escalated from first line support or the customer including in-fab support as needed. Conducts diagnostics and troubleshooting with a higher degree of independency and under limited supervision within primary competency.

Has more specialized knowledge of one competency or broader knowledge of multiple competencies. Has knowledge of and experience with the different components of the machine. Focuses on acquiring more knowledge.
Requirements
BS degree in relevant Technical Field (Electrical Technology, Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, etc.) with thorough experience, or comparable thinking and working level. Experience in semiconductor industry required.
Specialized knowledge in the area of pneumatics, hydraulics or electronics, and semiconductor processes, and relevant software.
Experience in using computer applications, including data analysis tools, word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation software.
Has specialized knowledge of competency/subsystem, product functionality.
Responsibilities
Problem analysis and approach
Gather all information relevant for the problem, analyze using available means, gather additional diagnostic info if needed, decide on initial approach to solve problem, assess new information and adapt approach if necessary under limited supervision.

Issues require basic understanding of primary competency relation to elements of the Service Level Agreement (SLA) including availability/uptime, MTBI, throughput/productivity, and yield.
Problem handovers and routing
Handover problem or problem aspects to others (Sr. TSEs or 3rd line support), document, package and deliver all data relevant for problem resolution (e.g. pass-downs, work orders, field service reports, system problem reports, technical reports).
Repairs
Advise customer technical personnel and 1st line support in dealing with complex problems, use tools, replace parts, improve settings, to execute repairs including supporting non-routine service actions. Able to resolve unexpected disturbances and provide countermeasures for primary competency with high degree of independence.
Procedures
Arrange with customer machine time window to execute procedure, plan procedure, arrange for all (possible) parts, tools, equipment and information / knowledge to be available at start of procedure, execute complex procedure, make necessary decisions / adaptations during procedure and to realize optimal results.

Define and explain appropriate actions to first line engineers to correct malfunctions, train customers in routine and non-routine maintenance of equipment, recommend changes in user procedures when needed.

Provide input for improvement proposals.

Maintain and broaden own knowledge (incl NPI), shares best known methods within the work group (site/cluster).
Coaching
Delivers advanced technical knowledge and skills transfers on primary competency to first-line field engineers, peers and junior TSE colleagues.

These applications are used by the Customer Support (CS) work force while performing their job in serving our customer’s needs.
Our mission is to facilitate and improve the productivity of the users of these applications and capabilities in order to meet ASML’s obligations.
We offer CS users functional support, process escalations and will drive issues to closure, freeing the CS engineer to perform the invaluable task of solving our customer’s issues.
Responsibilities:
As an CS Capability Expert you are the point of contact for the ASML Customer Support organization and application user community when the knowledge base and key users cannot support them, acting as a 3rd line support of off-system applications.
Your role is a mix of Run the Business (RtB) - by solving escalations within your expert area and being a single point of contact for one or more local sites - and Change the Business (CtB), by bringing real life examples, field requirements, and input into the design of new applications.
For this position, you will be the machine data expert to support world wide machine data authorization admin work as well as troubleshooting the machine data issues.
Your main responsibilities are to ensure that issues are picked up and handled to the satisfaction of our end-users and within given SLA’s, to maintain frequent communication with the local sites assigned to you, to participate in user acceptance tests and to participate in projects as expert for your domain, including the support of deployments.
To successfully do so you build and maintain strong relationships with the local sites and users as well with the development teams.
You also maintain documentation like knowledge bases and internal procedures and train key users.
You are involve in non-PGP projects and responsible to drive the progress and coordinate internal and external customer to ensure the delivery on time.

Context
The Customer Support (CS) organization is responsible for the installations, qualification, repair and maintenance of the ASML systems at customer sites and is responsible for the necessary transfer of know-how to the customer. Local site Customer Support branches perform these tasks for the customer within the specific region.

Anticipates, analyzes and solves complex technical problems escalated from first line support or the customer including in-fab support as needed. Also responsible for building the problem-solving capacity, developing capabilities for new product launches, and predictive diagnostics. Conducts diagnostics and troubleshooting cross-competencies independently.

Provides input for new products. Works with other engineers in the field launching new products. Develops competencies before a new product is launched (KD11) to bring it up to the desired level.
Takes a leading role in resolving 'unsolvable' problems with machines. Has more in-depth knowledge of competencies or develops broader competencies. Provides training and plays a role in releases while actively optimizing processes. Acts as a mentor to colleagues JG5/JG6/JG7. Supports the development of training material. Drives and develops training plans for new engineers.
Is able to theorize based on fully mastering own competencies.
Requirements
MS degree in relevant Technical Field (Electrical Technology, Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, etc.) with thorough experience, or comparable thinking and working level. Experience in semiconductor industry required.
Specialized knowledge in the area of pneumatics, hydraulics or electronics, and semiconductor processes, and relevant software.
Experience in using computer applications, including data analysis tools, word processing, spreadsheet, and presentation software. Has expert knowledge of primary competency and advanced cross-competency knowledge of main/sub modules, product functionality.

Experienced and proven track record in strong stakeholder management, and high influence in multidisciplinary environment. Requires deep and specialized knowledge in primary competency.
Responsibilities
Problem analysis and approach
Gather all information relevant for the problem, analyze using available means, gather additional diagnostic info if needed, decide on initial approach to solve complex and multi module related problems within primary competency, assess new information and adapt approach, establish it as new process if necessary.

Advises on strategies for UnScheduled Down (USD) & Scheduled Down (SD) within competency to influence the SLA: availability/uptime, MTBI, throughput/productivity and yield.
Problem handovers and routing
Drives problem or problem aspects with others (GSC/D&E) including proposals for containments/solutions, document and package all data relevant for problem resolution (e.g. pass-downs, work orders, field service reports, system problem reports, technical reports), ensure problem ownership is clear and is responsible for follow-up.
Repairs
Advise customer technical personnel and 1st line support in dealing with complex problems, use tools, replace parts, improve settings, to execute repairs including leading non-routine service actions. Able to independantly resolve unexpected disturbances and provide countermeasures and define the fundemantal improvements to increase efficiency and servicability relative to multiple competencies.
Procedures
Negotiate with customer on machine time window based on own risk assessment to develop procedure (if none exists), execute procedure, plan procedure, arrange for all (possible) parts, tools, equipment and information / knowledge to be available at start of procedure, execute procedure, make necessary decisions / adaptations during procedure to realize optimal results.
Training / advice
Persuade appropriate actions to first line engineers and customer to correct malfunctions, train first line engineers and customers in routine and non-routine maintenance of equipment, recommend changes in user procedures when needed, based on the functional theory, design rules and know-how. Capable to (co)develop internal training syllabus.
Process Optimization
Initiate new processes, checks and revises the existing procedures using expertise. Takes charge of ‘technically correct or infallible cure’ to machine problems by exercising ‘beyond-procedure’ creativity if needed.

Provide structural and strategic solutions towards issues or problems during process execution to optimize at a regional level.
Knowledge build-up and transfer
Establishes good ways of working for efficient knowledge exchange across geographical scope.
Coaching
Teaches and educates engineers, reviews and helps them making progress including advising on performance capabilities of junior engineers. Ability to handle oversight and coaching on multiple competencies and advise others on diagnostic best known methods.

Introduction to the job
Within ASML, the Customer Support (CS) organization is responsible for the maintenance, repair, upgrade, relocation, and continuous improvement of ASML systems, as well as the customer interface at customer locations. One of the departments within CS focuses on DUV UIR (Upgrades, Installs & Relocations). This organization prepares and executes complex UIR activities on DUV systems in a customer production environment worldwide. In this role, you will manage resources from the DUV UIR team and supporting organizations, while driving team development, strong collaboration, and people care, and contributing to the long-term ambition of ONE UIR.
Role and responsibilities
As CS DUV UIR Group Leader, you are responsible for the operational management of DUV Upgrade, Install, and Relocation activities at customer sites around the world. These activities are executed in live production environments and require strong alignment across teams, functions, and regions. Your mission is to develop capable and mature engineers, ensure stable and predictable execution, and support UIR operations to guarantee safe, efficient, and high-quality outcomes, while progressing toward a unified ONE UIR way of working.
Team & People Development
· Build, develop, and lead a high-performing DUV UIR team, fostering teamwork and shared accountability.
· Organize staffing according to the UIR blueprint, ensuring the right competencies are available at the right time.
· Define training plans and development targets to support multi-skill capability across Upgrades, Installs, and Relocations.
· Hire, onboard, train, and coach new team members toward operational and advanced/expert levels.
· Drive team engagement, collaboration, and people care, ensuring a safe and inclusive working environment.
KPI & Performance Management
· Define, align, and deploy Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across UIR activities, including safety, quality, delivery, efficiency, and cost.
· Monitor team and project performance using KPIs to identify gaps, risks, and Improvement Opportunities.
· Provide clear performance feedback to line management and stakeholders.
· Use KPI insights to support decision-making and continuous improvement toward ONE UIR performance alignment.
Execution & Operational Excellence
· Ensure UIR activities are executed safely and in alignment with agreed targets and customer commitments.
· Assign projects and lead planning and execution of DUV Upgrades, Installs, and Relocations.
· Support day-to-day UIR operation handling and issue resolution in customer fabs.
· Drive continuous improvement in safety, quality, cycle time, efficiency, and cost, leveraging lessons learned and best practices.
· Ensure effective skill management and knowledge sharing within the team and across UIR scopes.
Education and experience
Education :
MSc or BSc technical degree such as Mathematics, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electronics, (Applied) Physics, or a comparable discipline.
Experience :
· Experience in a challenging, high-tech environment with complex production processes.
· At least 6 years of relevant experience as a People Manager, Team Leader, Project Manager, or Project Leader.
· Experience with EUV systems and ASML products is strongly preferred.
· Proven experience working in cross-functional and multicultural environments.
Skills
· Strong ability to motivate, steer, and develop people at different levels of the organization.
· Capable of maintaining a global overview of operational and strategically important topics.
· Able to define and execute strategies for process and performance improvement.
· Excellent communication skills for internal and external stakeholders across different organizational levels.
· Strong technical foundation and a solution-oriented mindset.
· Customer-focused with strong planning and organizational skills.
· Open to cultural diversity and international collaboration.
· Good command of English, both verbal and written.
Other information
1. Willingness and flexibility to travel internationally (e.g., Taiwan, Korea, USA, and other regions) when required.
2. This role plays a key part in the evolution toward ONE UIR, driving:
· Unified processes and KPIs across Upgrade, Install, and Relocation scopes
· Stronger teamwork and resource flexibility across regions
· Standardized execution models and shared best practices
· A single, aligned UIR team mindset focused on customer success

ASML is dedicated to enabling long‑term customer success by delivering world‑class lithography solutions and services. We are looking for a DUV Equipment Instructor to join the CS Global Training Center in Linkou, Taiwan. In this role, you will design and deliver technical training that equips engineers with the knowledge and skills required to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot DUV scanner systems safely and effectively in real fab environments.
This position follows a 4‑days‑on / 3‑days‑off working schedule, designed to support sustainable workload while enabling global training operations.

Deliver technical training sessions on DUV lithography equipment for Customer Support engineers and selected customer engineers.
Develop, review, and continuously improve high‑quality training programs using a blended learning approach, including: Instructor‑Led Training (ILT)/Web‑Based Training (WBT) /Case‑Based Learning (CBL)
Animations and technical reference materials
Maintain training machines, tools, and related equipment to ensure safe, reliable, and effective training conditions.
Ensure all training activities comply with safety regulations and operational standards.

Support global training initiatives, including international training delivery and cross‑site collaboration.

Experience in technical training delivery, knowledge transfer, or structured technical instruction.
Strong interest and aptitude in teaching, coaching, and developing others.
Ability to communicate technical topics clearly in spoken and written English.
Willingness to work in a shift‑based operating model and travel as required.

Hands‑on experience in semiconductor equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, or Customer Support.
Background in lithography equipment (DUV experience is a strong plus).
Proven experience with instructional design, didactics, or adult learning methodologies.
Comfortable working in classroom, laboratory, and cleanroom environments.
Experience working in a global or cross‑cultural environment.

ASML is the world’s leading supplier of photolithography systems for the semiconductor industry, manufacturing machines used for the production of integrated circuits. The company heavily relies on information, making the protection of confidential data critical and requiring continuous improvement.
At ASML, the Three Lines of Responsibility model is applied, with security capabilities organized centrally (second line) and security risk management embedded within each sector (first line).
To support several sectors in Taiwan, we are looking for a Security Risk Manager to ensure that information security risks remain within the organization’s risk appetite.
You will be part of a global Security Risk Management (SRM) team that:
Identifies and assesses information security risks in processes and applications
Recommends mitigations to reduce risk to acceptable levels
Supports risk owners in implementing mitigation actions
Monitors and reports progress to stakeholders
The team is involved in programs, projects, and changes, assessing risks related to new or modified assets by defining security requirements and validating their implementation.
Creating awareness and educating stakeholders at all levels is a key responsibility. In addition, the team drives company-wide initiatives to strengthen and mature information security capabilities.
Role and Responsibilities
As a Security Risk Manager, you will be the first point of contact in Taiwan for assigned sectors on security-related topics. Your main responsibilities include:
Handle local security incidents
Provide security awareness training
Execute application risk assessments
Support new initiatives through risk scoping
Define security requirements and validate proper implementation
Create visibility into the local risk landscape of supported sectors
Evaluate risks against the organization’s risk appetite
Recommend, support, and guide risk owners in implementing mitigation actions
Report to local and central stakeholders
Actively participate in programs, projects, and changes
Support the business during internal and external audits
By driving initiatives, identifying gaps, and supporting continuous improvement efforts, you will contribute to strengthening and maturing ASML’s security capabilities.
Education and Experience
To be successful in this role, you bring strong expertise in security risk management and experience working in complex environments, along with:
Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field
Minimum of 10 years’ experience in information security risk management
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or CRISC (strongly preferred)
Experience with risk assessment, risk treatment, and control design
Knowledge of information security standards and risk frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001, NIST)
Experience protecting confidential information and intellectual property
Familiarity with identity and access management and secure collaboration practices
Experience working with stakeholders at different organizational levels and in cross-functional teams
Ability to translate policies and procedures into operational activities
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of technology means continuously solving new challenges. You will collaborate across teams and functions in a dynamic environment. To be successful in this role, you bring:
Strong communication and influencing skills
Ability to analyze risks and translate them into business impact
Ownership and ability to drive results in a complex environment
Strong relationship-building skills and ability to influence without authority
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
Ability to collaborate effectively across diverse teams
Proactive mindset with a focus on continuous improvement
Strategic thinking and strong risk prioritization skills
Flexibility to adapt to changing priorities and organizational needs
Passion for improving security awareness and maturity
Strong verbal and written communication skills in English
Confidence to speak up when risks, opportunities, or concerns are identified
Other Information
This position is based in Taiwan. You will be part of the Security Risk Management team within the Infrastructure, Architecture & Security department of the Customer Solutions & Support (CS&S) sector.
You will report to the Regional Group Lead based in Veldhoven. In addition to supporting CS&S, you will also support other global sectors such as IT, Corporate Real Estate, and several Corporate functions.
You will collaborate with the broader ASML security community across business sectors. ASML supports your professional growth through continuous learning opportunities and exposure to international teams and projects.
The position offers competitive compensation. Job grade will be determined based on qualifications, experience, and competencies.

A unique opportunity to focus on cyber security while experiencing ASMLs business and way of working.
Role and responsibilities
Your task as CS &S Security Architect is to provide architecture-level security direction and assurance across applications, AI solutions, products and services. In close collaboration with Capability Architects, Solution and Infrastructure Architects, product and service teams, security experts and IT, you will evaluate solution designs, identify technical risks and security gaps, define appropriate controls, and align security improvements with business and IAS technology roadmaps. This means:
Architecture-level technical risk assessments, including defining proportionate controls for new applications, AI solutions, products and services.
Secure solution design assurance, covering data flows, trust boundaries, integrations, identity, operational dependencies and residual risks.
Strong architectural understanding of secure SDLC, application security, cloud security, AI security and product security.
The ability to translate technical findings into business exposure, delivery choices, remediation priorities and investment decisions.
Development of security capability and service roadmaps aligned with product portfolios, infrastructure roadmaps and IT operations.
Engagement with CS&S infrastructure, solutions, product and operations architects to embed security consistently across their roadmaps.
Support for both IAS product teams releasing solutions to the field and service teams operating business-critical capabilities.
Interpretation of penetration-test, vulnerability, threat-model, code-review and compliance assessment findings into an actionable remediation plan.
Contribution to broader operational security decisions, architecture deviations and recurring security improvement initiatives.
Conduct Security Control Gap Assessments (Risk Scoping) for new and existing solutions to identify control deficiencies, evaluate associated risks, and ensure alignment with enterprise governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) requirements.
Education and experience
Master's degree in information security, cyber security or equivalent.
You prove to have at least 10+ years’ experience in security architecture, design and requirements collection.
Worked in multi-disciplinary projects; Dealt with customers.
Deep knowledge of security technologies, architecture principles, risk management practices and industry best practices.
Experience with security assessments and assessing security implications; Affinity with various security frameworks and current EU legislations, including CRA and NIS 2.0.
Experience coordinating and managing information security risks in partnership with business and technology stakeholders.
Strong ability to communicate technical risks and security requirements in business language and influence decision-making at all levels.
Proven track record of creating, managing and delivering security roadmaps and step-ups in infrastructure, products and services.
Experience within a high-tech, engineering or semiconductor environment is considered a strong advantage.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, ISSAP, SABSA, TOGAF or equivalent are required; however, demonstrated practical experience, architectural judgement and delivery of security outcomes are valued more highly than certifications alone.
Skills
Strong communication and listening skills
Strong problem solving capabilities
Ability to influence and manage different stakeholders on multiple levels
Strong motivation on finding creative solutions for complex multi system, multiple customers problems.
Translate security requirements and business goals into detailed specifications and designs that are accepted by stakeholders at many levels in the organizations.
Other information
As a CS&S Security Architect, you are part of the CS&S Security & Risk Management department positioned within Customer Solutions & Support and will report to the CS&S Security Lead.
You will be based in Veldhoven, the Netherlands. You will be a member of the ASML Security community; working closely together with the security risk management teams in other sectors and the central security competence teams.

Introduction to the Job
As a Customs Manager, you will play a critical role in enabling ASML’s global business while ensuring compliance with customs regulations. Your work will help support the movement of advanced technology across international borders, allowing ASML to continue driving innovation in the semiconductor industry.
In this Customs Manager role, you will develop, implement, and govern ASML’s global customs strategy with a strong focus on U.S. customs compliance. You will oversee customs-related activities, manage risk, and guide the organization through an evolving regulatory landscape. By partnering with business leaders and cross-functional teams, you will help support business growth while maintaining compliance across customs-related processes, systems, and decisions.
This position may require access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require the Company to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.
Role and Responsibilities
As a Customs Manager, you will serve as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert, helping ASML navigate complex customs requirements while supporting business objectives. You will collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to strengthen compliance programs, manage risk, and drive continuous improvement.
You will:
Monitor customs laws and regulations and assess their impact on ASML’s business operations.
Advise leaders and stakeholders on customs implications related to business decisions and strategic initiatives.
Partner with finance, legal, compliance, and other business functions to provide integrated customs guidance.
Develop, implement, and continuously improve customs compliance policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.
Maintain and enhance customs control frameworks, with a strong focus on U.S. customs compliance and risk mitigation.
Lead or support business improvement projects as the customs subject matter expert.
Represent ASML in interactions with customs authorities, including audits, rulings, agreements, and regulatory discussions.
Education and Experience
To be successful as a Customs Manager, you should have:
Bachelor’s degree in business, international trade, supply chain management, law, finance, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum of 8 years of experience in customs compliance, international trade, or related regulatory disciplines.
Experience managing customs compliance programs within the United States.
Experience leading customs initiatives in a complex, matrixed organization.
Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and drive compliance across multiple business functions.
Master’s degree in a related field preferred.
Licensed Customs Broker certification preferred.
Experience within the semiconductor, technology, manufacturing, or machinery industries preferred.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Analyze complex customs and business requirements and translate them into practical solutions.
Build trusted relationships and influence stakeholders across multiple functions and levels.
Communicate clearly and effectively in both written and verbal settings.
Demonstrate ownership and accountability from issue identification through resolution.
Prioritize competing demands and manage deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Adapt to changing regulations, priorities, and business needs.
Apply strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Collaborate effectively within global and multicultural teams.
Evaluate risk and make sound, compliance-focused decisions.
Leverage knowledge of customs regulations, trade compliance, and related tax concepts.

This role operates at the intersection of cyber resilience, enterprise risk management, and business continuity, with a strong focus on governance, standardization, and cross-sector alignment. You are also responsible for developing and maintaining enterprise-wide, cross-sector cyber resilience and recovery artefacts, such as recovery blueprints, strategies, and standardized recovery approaches, to ensure a coherent and scalable recovery capability across ASML.

Introduction
ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
As a Field Service Engineer - Cymer at ASML you will be part of a team of engineers who help our organization install, repair and maintain Cymer laser equipment at customer sites. You ensure that our systems work as they should – and be part of the technology innovation that’s moving the world forward. You’ll be a technical expert who will work with coworkers, customer & field support in isolating and solving problems to maintain and optimize equipment on a daily basis enhancing functionality and prevent problems. You will act as a resource for users on routine malfunctions and will be responsible for the necessary transfer of know-how to the customer.
Role and Responsibilities

Introduction to the job
ASML /Cymer is one of the world’s leading manufacturers of lithography systems that help enable Moore’s Law and the creation of increasingly powerful and capable electronic devices. Our San Diego-based light source division, Cymer, is renowned for developing both deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography light sources and next generation extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light sources. As the world’s leading semiconductor equipment manufacturer, ASML enables chipmakers to produce cheaper, speedier chips – and to produce them faster – thereby enabling all the technology you use today. The systems we produce integrate several large and sophisticated machines, themselves each a feat of engineering innovation, precision, and speed.
We are a multinational company with over 70 locations in 16 countries, headquartered in Veldhoven, the Netherlands. We have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA (EUV laser source creation).
In the Cymer Light Source (CLS) division in San Diego, we design and manufacture Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) lasers, used directly in the chipmaking process. Far from a basic “consumer” laser, these machines are complex, powerful, and flexible. As a Design and Engineering (D&E) Lab Technician, this role will support product development by performing hands-on build, prototyping, proof-of-concept, diagnostic and troubleshooting testing, of electrical and mechanical systems, in a consistent, repeatable, safe and efficient manner. Another key responsibility is to support at least one of ASML’s development labs which includes maintaining testing equipment, instrumentation, and tooling in a ready state, including but not limited to calibration tracking, configuration management of test stands and test equipment, and safety monitoring as well as other tasks in support of projects and production operations. The third primary responsibility is ownership, planning, and scheduling activities within the lab, and maintaining the lab with a 5S environment. Basic computer skills are required for test stand operation, as well as for scheduling and communicating with customers.

As a Design Engineer: Optical Sensor System - Integrated Optics, you will help develop advanced optical technologies used in ASML lithography systems. These systems enable the production of faster, more powerful, and more energy-efficient microchips that power everyday technologies around the world.
Based in Wilton, Connecticut, this role combines optical design, photonic integration, simulation, testing, and system validation. As a Design Engineer: Optical Sensor System - Integrated Optics, you will contribute to the design, analysis, testing, and validation of advanced optical sensing technologies. Introduction to the job
Engineering Simulation plays an increasingly important role in how engineers design, test and optimize products. Behind it sits a complex landscape of simulation applications, engineering workplaces and high-performance computing capabilities.
As Domain Owner Engineering Simulation, you will lead the (IT) domain that provides these capabilities. You will set the direction, build the roadmap, lead the organization and ensure successful delivery of the IT platforms and IT services that engineers rely on every day.
This is a significant leadership role covering strategy, delivery, people and organizational development. You will report directly to the Head of Electrical Engineering & Machine Conditioning and lead 11 direct reports, supported by a broader group of internal and external specialists.
Role and responsibilities
You are the end-to-end owner of the Engineering Simulation domain.
You will translate business priorities into a clear strategy, multi-year roadmap and delivery plan. You will make choices about priorities, investments and capacity and ensure execution against agreed quality, timing and cost objectives.
At the same time, you will help build the organization needed for the future. You will strengthen capabilities, develop talent and create an environment in which teams can perform, grow and take ownership.
A key part of the role is your close partnership with the Domain Architect. Together, you connect business priorities, technical direction and delivery. You will also work closely with Product Owners, engineers, domain experts, suppliers and other stakeholders to achieve coherent outcomes across the domain.
What you will do:
Strategy and value realization
You will define and drive the domain strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligned with broader business and technology priorities. The role goes beyond setting direction. You will translate that direction into executable plans and measurable outcomes.
You will:
Define and maintain the domain strategy and roadmap.
Translate business priorities into domain plans, work packages, scope and dependencies.
Maintain the rolling six-quarter plan and adapt scope and capacity when priorities or circumstances change.
Create clarity around priorities and investment choices.
Track value realization through improvements in productivity, quality, cost, innovation and people development.
Align teams and stakeholders around the agreed direction.
Delivery and platform ownership
You will be accountable for delivery across the Engineering Simulation domain.
You will manage risks, dependencies, governance and critical decisions, while ensuring that commitments are delivered against agreed scope, quality, timing and cost.
You will also act as IT owner of the Engineering Simulation application landscape, the Engineering Simulation Workplace and the High-Performance Computing platform. Your ownership covers the full lifecycle, from design and delivery through operations and continuous improvement.
You will:
Manage delivery risks, dependencies, governance and critical decisions.
Ensure successful delivery against agreed commitments.
Own the Engineering Simulation application landscape, Engineering Simulation Workplace and HPC platform.
Ensure effective integration with related engineering, tooling and data domains.
Continuously improve the platforms, services and ways of working so that they remain aligned with changing engineering needs.
Stakeholder and supplier leadership
The Engineering Simulation domain operates at the intersection of engineering, IT and external technology partners. Success depends on clear priorities, strong partnerships and the ability to resolve dependencies before they affect delivery.
You will act as a strategic partner to engineering and IT stakeholders. You will translate business needs into concrete plans, align priorities across teams and ensure that ownership is clear.
You will also manage suppliers and external resources, including onboarding and offboarding, and hold partners accountable for their commitments and performance.
Build and lead the organization
This is a substantial people leadership role.
You will lead and develop the teams within the domain and build the capabilities required for the future. Beyond delivering the roadmap, you will strengthen the organization itself.
This means creating clarity around roles, responsibilities and accountability. You will assign leadership roles within teams where needed, develop talent and help people take on broader ownership. You will coach teams and leaders, strengthen collaboration and improve how work flows through the organization.
You will create an environment in which people can perform, learn and grow. You will also use relevant metrics to assess team and partner performance, improve delivery predictability and follow through on improvement actions.
Education and experience
You combine technical leadership, delivery management and people leadership. You are comfortable working in a complex environment, making priorities explicit and balancing long-term direction with day-to-day execution.
You bring:
A bachelor’s or master’s degree in a technical field, or equivalent professional experience.
Approximately 7 to 10 years of experience in product, platform, program or delivery leadership within complex technical environments.
Proven experience in end-to-end product or platform ownership, delivery leadership, people leadership and supplier management.
Experience managing stakeholders, suppliers and cross-functional teams in large organizations.
Experience working across cultures, locations and time zones.
Exposure to large-scale engineering or R&D environments.
Experience with Engineering Simulation, High-Performance Computing, scientific computing, simulation applications or data-intensive engineering workflows would help you get up to speed quickly.
Deep domain experience is valuable, but it is not the only route into this role. You may instead bring a strong technical foundation, proven leadership experience and the curiosity and learning agility to build credibility quickly. Your ability to ask the right questions and use the expertise around you is as important as your previous domain experience.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
You combine strategic thinking with a strong delivery mindset. You create clarity, make decisions and turn direction into tangible results.
You develop people, build trust and create accountability without micromanaging.
Most importantly, you enjoy building: building teams, strengthening organizational capability and developing a domain that enables engineers to do their best work.

Introduction
The Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) team at ASML in Veldhoven supports the reliable operation of advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment. As systems become larger and more complex, assessing compliance with low-frequency radiated emission requirements can be challenging in practical measurement environments. During this internship, you will help bridge the gap between regulatory requirements and real-world qualification conditions. Your work will contribute to the development of practical EMC assessment methods for next-generation semiconductor manufacturing systems. This internship offers a unique opportunity to combine scientific research with an industrial engineering challenge.
Your assignment
In this internship, you will investigate how radiated emission limits below 150 kHz can be translated into a practical evaluation method for large semiconductor manufacturing equipment. You will combine electromagnetic theory, modeling, simulation, and measurement analysis to develop a technically substantiated assessment approach. Working closely with EMC specialists, you will contribute to improving future compliance assessment strategies.

Your main responsibilities will be:
Review relevant low-frequency electromagnetic compatibility regulations and standards
Analyze the assumptions behind existing radiated emission limits and prescribed measurement distances
Investigate near-field and far-field electromagnetic behavior below 150 kHz
Develop analytical models and simulations to translate regulatory limits to practical measurement distances
Identify gaps between regulatory requirements and current qualification practices
Propose and validate a practical radiated emission assessment methodology
Document findings and present recommendations to technical stakeholders
This is a master's thesis internship for minimum 3-6 months, minimum 4 days per week (minimum 2 days on-site). The start date of this internship is as of February or as soon as possible.
Your profile
To be suitable for the internship, you:
Are enrolled in a master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Electromagnetics, RF Engineering, Applied Electromagnetics, or a related technical field
Are looking for a master's thesis internship
Have strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Are proactive and collaborative when working with technical experts and stakeholders
Have knowledge of electromagnetic field theory and an interest in electromagnetic compatibility
Have experience with, or strong interest in, modeling, simulation, and data analysis
Communicate clearly in English, both verbally and in writing
This internship is based at the ASML campus in Veldhoven. Throughout the project, you will gain experience applying advanced engineering theory to real-world semiconductor manufacturing challenges. You will work alongside experienced specialists and contribute to the development of practical EMC qualification methods. The internship provides an opportunity to create tangible impact while completing your thesis research. If you enjoy combining scientific analysis with practical engineering applications, this internship could be an excellent next step in your academic journey.

Introduction to the job
As Electrical installation manager (low voltage), you help protect people, infrastructure, and business operations across ASML in the Netherlands. Reliable electrical installations are essential for developing and manufacturing the advanced technology that enables ASML’s customers to produce microchips.
You will be the formally appointed Electrical Responsible Person, known in the Netherlands as the Installatieverantwoordelijke. You will ensure that ASML’s low-voltage infrastructure operates safely, reliably, and in accordance with applicable standards. Specialized contractors perform daily operational activities, while you provide governance, oversight, and technical leadership.
Role and responsibilities
As Electrical installation manager (low voltage), you have overall accountability for low-voltage electrical safety and compliance. You establish clear requirements, oversee delegated responsibilities, and intervene when safety or business continuity is at risk.
You will:
Act as the appointed Installation Manager under NEN 3140 for assigned low-voltage installations.
Own and continuously improve ASML’s electrical safety management program, policies, procedures, and governance framework.
Oversee authorized contractor organizations performing maintenance, inspections, switching activities, testing, and operational installation management.
Safeguard infrastructure reliability through lifecycle planning, risk mitigation, redundancy strategies, and modernization programs.
Review and approve high-risk activities, technical deviations, risk assessments, competencies, and electrical safety authorizations.
Lead electrical incident investigations, identify root causes, and ensure effective corrective and preventive measures.

A bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering or a related technical discipline.
At least 10 years of relevant experience in industrial, utility, semiconductor, high-tech, or mission-critical environments.
Extensive experience with electrical safety governance, asset management, and infrastructure risk management.
Demonstrated experience overseeing contractors and managing formally delegated electrical safety responsibilities.
Strong knowledge of NEN 3140, NEN 3840, NEN 1010, NTA 8220, IEC 60364, IEC 60204-1, NEN-EN-IEC 61936, and IEEE 1584.

As Enterprise risk expert, you will enable ASML to achieve its business objectives in a responsible way, by providing deep risk expertise, cross-sector insights, and independent challenge. Role and responsibilities
As Enterprise risk expert, you contribute to the maturity of ASML’s risk management processes, enhancing transparency, alignment with strategic priorities, and consistent application of risk principles across ASML. Your role strengthens organizational resilience and long-term value creation by embedding enterprise risk thinking in strategy and execution; anticipating emerging risks through scenario planning and systems thinking; providing clear, decision-oriented risk insights to senior stakeholders; shaping risk culture and fostering mature, open dialogue on uncertainty.
In this role, you will:

Introduction to the job
ASML is a global leader in the high-tech semiconductor equipment manufacturing industry. We are seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Mechanical Engineer to support the operation, maintenance, and optimization of our facilities infrastructure. This role is critical to ensuring the reliability, efficiency, and safety of our complex mechanical systems, which enable the success of our manufacturing operations.
The Mechanical Engineer – Facilities will be responsible for designing, analyzing, and supporting the operation of major facilities systems such as HVAC, DI water, process water, chillers, boilers, pumps, exhaust systems, heat exchangers and roofing systems. This role also involves overseeing the distribution of process gases and liquids critical to manufacturing processes. The ideal candidate has deep technical knowledge of mechanical systems and experience in facilities engineering within a high-tech or manufacturing environment.

Design, analyze, and improve mechanical systems to enhance efficiency, reliability, and performance.

Conduct risk assessments and implement mitigation strategies to address potential system failures.

Prepare reports and presentations for management, highlighting system performance and improvement opportunities.

Introduction to the job
Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers fibers are critical components to enable ASML's advanced light sources, which in turn power our metrology systems. Fabrication of these fibers need state-of-the art glass manufacturing technologies in highly specialized clean facilities. Technical challenges are manifold including control of hydrodynamic effects during many stages of the fiber draw, advanced qualification and data analysis, correct pre-fiber process design, advanced problem solving and more. And organizationally, we need to secure safe work environments, structured planning & reporting to our stakeholders, managing suppliers as well as dealing with unique blend between academic and industrial environment in a remote location.
Role and responsibilities
As fiber drawing engineer, you work partially in a clean room based, high-tech fiber manufacturing facility as well as in advanced optical laboratories, where you take end-to-end ownership of (part)the fiber development and production process. This includes identifying and understanding problems, proposing and engineering solution directions, sourcing in material, implementing and testing.
Together with the team you also contribute to other stages of the fiber drawing process, starting from raw material characterization, preform assembly, drawing fibers, to their qualifications, and eventual shipping.
Dealing with suppliers as well as our academic partner who provides clean room facilities, of will be part of your role. This includes aspects of technical supply/academic management. Integrating submodules in the tower line requires you to have basic mechanical, software and electronics experience.
You timely flag problems as well improvements ideas for production output and yield to colleagues management.
You use your experience in the fiber domain to propose advanced manufacturing and diagnostic technologies, that may help in improving yield and performance of the fibers.
You work closely with a specialized team of fiber drawing experts and ourtechnology partner.
You report within your team, to management in Erlangen and Veldhoven and should be comfortable working in a small and remote team.
Critical deliverables of this position include timely providing sufficient fiber material of the right quality, reporting and planning, technical documentation, successful troubleshooting and solution implementation.
Education and experience
You have a Master or Ph.D. (degree in the technical areas of Material Science, Fiber Optics or a similar technical field) with 3-5 years relevant work experience.
Affinity towards fine mechanical work and craftsmanship with glass is essential.
Skills
Hands-on experience with optical fibers, specialty fibers or hollow-core fibers manufacturing.
Experience with quality control of processes as well as advanced troubleshooting.
Deep theoretical knowledge of the (hollow-core)fiber process and helicopter view on the landscape of HC-PCFs.
Works independently after onboarding & training is completed
Affinity with stock management, statistical/data analysis, and logistics to deliver the fibers to different locations.
First line leadership experience is preferred
Excellent communication skills to explain complex technical problems to stakeholders
Basic planning skills are needed to contribute to a reliable way forward
Work in clean rooms areas and high-tech facilities
Integration of submodules: basic mechanical design, software (MATLAB, Python, LabVIEW) and electronics knowledge
Able to work in multi-disciplinary teams within a high-tech environment.
Embrace the international and diverse environment of the company.
Focused on quality and continuous improvement.
Able to fluently speak, write and understand English. German language is a plus.
Being comfortable working in small & remote team
Having potential to look outside your box and be interested to learn other skills, such as leadership, project planning or more
Other information
You report to a group leader. The primary location of work is in Erlangen, Germany. Occasional business trips to ASML headquarters in the Netherlands may be required. For more information on ASML, visit our website: http://www.asml.com

1 資産形成サポート・手当
社員の将来設計から日々の生活まで、安心して働き続けられるよう、資産形成と生活支援の両面をサポートする制度を充実させています。

-フレキシブル・ベネフィット：年に一回ポイントが付与され、旅行・レストラン・日用品など幅広いサービスに利用可能

-寒冷地手当：積雪地帯等で必要となるコスト等の負担を軽減するための手当を支給

-社内メンター制度：社員がキャリアやスキル開発を目的に社内の経験豊富なメンターとつながれる機会を提供

industrialization deliverables.

Introduction to the job
As Manager Financial Planning Systems & Analytics at ASML, you play a key role in shaping the future of financial planning and performance management across a global high-tech organization. Your work enables financial transparency and strong decision-making that supports ASML’s long-term strategy and operational excellence.
In this role, you operate at the intersection of Corporate FP&A, Finance transformation and technology, combining strong financial expertise with advanced planning capabilities to improve how ASML forecasts, plans and translates performance into management insights.
You will take business ownership of SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) for financial planning while playing an active role in ASML’s forecasting, budgeting, long-term planning and management reporting cycles. Working closely with senior Finance stakeholders, business teams and IT, you will turn complex planning requirements into scalable solutions and actionable financial insights.
This role sits at the heart of ASML Finance and provides the opportunity to influence how financial information is structured, automated and used to support decision-making across the company.
Role and responsibilities
In this senior individual contributor role, you act as a trusted partner across Finance, business teams and IT, with significant cross-functional influence and exposure to senior stakeholders. You drive key financial planning and performance management activities while continuously improving the systems and processes that enable them
You will:
Act as the functional product owner and subject-matter expert for SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) planning and reporting
Own and manage the SAC roadmap by defining user requirements, prioritizing enhancements, and partnering with IT on implementation.
Design and maintain SAC data models, workflows, templates, and logic, including integration with SAP/HANA/BW.
Ensure high-quality planning information for forecasting, long-term financial plan, corporate budgeting, and Monthly Operating Reviews (MOR).
Developing performance insights, financial narratives and scenario analysis for senior management forums in close collaboration with business and finance stakeholders
Translate financial and non-financial KPI definitions into scalable planning logic with clear governance
Identify opportunities to simplify manual planning and reporting activities and drive automation through integrated planning and analytics capabilities.
Collaborate across Finance, IT and business teams to ensure end-to-end consistency, adoption and continuous improvement of financial planning processes.
Contribute to the continued development of ASML’s FP&A capabilities by bringing together financial expertise, technology and data-driven insights.
Education and experience
Master’s degree in business economics, finance, accounting, or a related discipline
10+ years of relevant experience in FP&A, financial planning, business control or related Finance roles.
Strong experience with enterprise planning and reporting systems, including SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC)
Experience working with ERP or business intelligence platforms such as SAP BW or SAP HANA
Proven involvement in corporate budgeting, forecasting, and financial performance cycles
Strong background in financial modeling, management reporting, performance analysis and scenario analysis.
Experience working in a complex, international, technology-driven environment
Experience partnering with senior Finance and business stakeholders in a cross-functional environment.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Strong understanding of financial planning, forecasting and performance management.
Good understanding of SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC)
Analyze complex financial data and translate it into clear insights
Communicate effectively with stakeholders at different organizational levels
Collaborate proactively across Finance, IT, and business teams
Translate Finance requirements into practical and scalable planning solutions.
Structure and prioritize work across multiple planning cycles
Drive improvement through a hands-on and solution-oriented mindset
Maintain accuracy, reliability, and transparency in financial information
Influence change through expertise rather than formal authority
Other information
This Manager Financial Planning Systems & Analytics position reports into the Finance organization at ASML in Veldhoven, the Netherlands. The role operates in a day-shift environment and may require alignment with global stakeholders across time zones.
The position provides broad exposure across Corporate FP&A, business Finance and IT and offers the opportunity to influence the continued development of ASML’s financial planning and performance management capabilities.
ASML invests strongly in employee growth through structured development programs, international exposure, and opportunities to deepen both technical and leadership expertise. Introduction of the job
As an FPGA Design and Verification Engineer, you will specify, design, develop, realize, integrate, and test modules and tools in a multi-disciplined team, collaborating closely with cross-functional partners and suppliers. You will deliver within system specifications, cost targets, and project schedules, ensuring timely realization of solutions that contribute to competitive, achievable, and serviceable products. The FPGA Firmware Engineer provides discipline specific expertise throughout the entire product life cycle. This Includes concept feasibility, new product introduction, existing product sustainment and customer facing problem resolution. The position requires highly motivated, extremely organized, and self-driven individuals.
The FPGA Design and Verification Engineer will be responsible for definition, design, verification, and documentation for Field Programmable Gate Arrays. They will provide RTL design, simulation, physical implementation and verification of complex FPGA modules comprising a mix of custom RTL with hard and soft vendor IP cores within a larger architecture.
Role and responsibilities
In this role, you will contribute to engineering deliverables that scale with job grade, from executing defined tasks and supporting senior engineers to owning complex technical scope, coordinating cross-functional work, and leading program-level outcomes.
Identify, analyze, document, and manage requirements with traceability, and coordinate verification criteria to confirm deliverables meet intent.
Conduct research and feasibility studies, document findings, and translate results into recommendations, tradeoffs, and decision inputs.
Develop engineering concepts and solutions, make technical choices, and resolve issues to meet functionality, performance, cost, and compliance needs.
Define and communicate specifications and high-level designs, align interfaces, and support reviews and approvals to enable quality execution.
Support system or product integration by coordinating dependencies, applying configuration management, and enabling smooth project execution.
Define and execute validation and test approaches, improve methods and procedures, and ensure qualification evidence supports release readiness.
Estimate effort, plan and track work, manage risks and dependencies, and deliver assigned work packages or projects to agreed quality and timelines.
Maintain accurate technical documentation, share knowledge through coaching and mentoring as applicable, and follow EHS policies while identifying and mitigating safety risks.
Education & experience
Bachelors degree in Electrical Engineering required.
Masters Degree or PhD preferred.
Minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience required.
Design:
Determine architecture and detailed system design approach for the FPGA
Define module interfaces and all aspects of device design coordinated with the Printed Circuit Board Designers
Evaluate the process flow including but not limited to high level design, synthesis, place and route, timing constraints and power utilization
Support the generation of technical engineering products by using the appropriate standards, processes, procedures, and tools throughout the FPGA development life cycle
Independently determine approach to solutions and get alignment from System Engineers and Printed Circuit Board developers
Contribute to design and development of FPGA hardware for control, communications systems and digital signal processing (DSP) platforms.
Technical Writing: Define and Document Specifications and Design Decisions
Test, Verification & Integration:
Develop and Implement the Product Validation and Verification (V&V) Strategy for FPGA
Determine system verification approach for the FPGA, ensuring proper test coverage
Develop, implement and supervise design verification test plans at system level.
Design, Develop and Build Product Specific Test Tooling
Includes: Simulation, Emulation, and Hardware Test Tools.
Test Validation and Verification (V&V) of Product Requirements
- Plan and Execute Component Level Testing & Sub-module Integration
Plan and Execute Module Level and System Level Integration
Bridge the gap between Electrical Systems and System Software
Technical Writing: Define and Document Test Procedures, and Test Reports
Skills
Technical & functional skills
Requirements, Interfaces & Technical Specification Management: Ability to identify, analyze, document, and manage requirements with traceability, translate them into clear specifications, and align interfaces so engineering deliverables meet intent and enable reliable downstream design, integration, and verification
Engineering Solution Development (Electrical): Ability to develop engineering concepts and solutions, make sound technical tradeoffs, resolve issues, and realize designs that meet functionality, performance, cost, compliance, and schedule constraints within system/module specifications.
Preferred Skills in Embedded Logic and Firmware Design and Verification includes:
- Highly proficient use and understanding of FPGA engineering concepts, principles, and theories
Highly proficient in FPGA design languages and tools including VHDL and UVM or OSVVM (Altera High Level Synthesis is preferred)
Experience with FPGA development software - (Modelsim, Quartus, Mentor CDC is preferred)
Highly proficient in Microsoft Office applications
Experience with FPGA SoC, including Avalon and AXI architectures
Experience with architecting and implementing embedded processors including NIOS
Proficient in implementing IP blocks based on interface requirements and designing the required interface logic to overall FPGA architecture
Expertise using VHDL for implementation and verification of FPGA designs
Basic knowledge of signal algorithms
Preferred knowledge and experience using design software and technical tools includes:
- VHDL, System Verilog, UVM
Questa Sim, Modelsim, Quartus
GIT, JIRA
MATLAB and SimuLink
Electronic Laboratory Equipment
LabVIEW
Python
Integration, Verification & Validation (V&V) Execution: Ability to plan and execute verification and validation, ensure qualification evidence supports release readiness, and support system/product integration by coordinating dependencies and applying disciplined configuration/traceability to deliver working, testable solutions.
Behavioral & leadership skills
Drives Results: The ability to translate strategic and technical goals into clear priorities, execution plans, and measurable outcomes, delivering committed results on time and with the right quality by taking ownership, managing trade-offs, removing obstacles, and sustaining momentum across stakeholders and dependencies.
Demonstrates Self-awareness: The ability to understand and manage one’s own strengths, limitations, emotions, and impact on others; to actively seek and use feedback; and to adapt behaviors and decisions to improve collaboration, leadership effectiveness, and results, especially in high-pressure, ambiguous, or complex environments.
Values Differences: The ability to intentionally seek, respect, and integrate diverse perspectives and working styles to strengthen collaboration and decision quality, ensuring all voices are heard and treated equitably, and enabling inclusive execution across cross-functional and multicultural stakeholders.
Builds Effective Teams: Helps align and enable the team dynamic by clarifying shared goals, roles, dependencies, and ways of working. Fosters trust and inclusion by promoting open dialogue, healthy conflict resolution, inclusion, and mutual accountability. Coaches colleagues to strengthen individual and team capability.
Drives Vision and Purpose: Translates broader direction into clear priorities and practical next steps for a team or technical scope. Builds alignment on goals and trade-offs, communicates context during change or ambiguity, and helps others maintain focus on shared outcomes.
Other
This position is located on-site. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. A flexible workplace arrangement is available for remote work up to two days a week.
Routinely required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch. Occasionally required to move around the campus.

As Head of apprenticeships, you shape the long-term development of our apprenticeship programs and make a significant contribution to securing the future demand for skilled professionals and specialists. Together with your team, you continuously develop our apprenticeship organization, ensure its quality and future readiness, and create the foundation for future generations of talent to succeed.
Role and responsibilities

lead and develop the apprenticeship team, including disciplinary responsibility as well as annual performance, development, and feedback discussions.
further develop the strategic direction of apprenticeship programs and help shape long-term goals and priorities together with internal and external stakeholders.

Introduction to the job
As we enter a new era of technology, everything and everyone will be more connected, and the lines between the physical and digital worlds will become less distinct. Rapid advancements in generative AI, self-driving cars, and artificial intelligence are driving an increased demand for advanced chips. At ASML, we are at the forefront of these changes with our technology, making it essential for our workforce to be well-organized and to be fully empowered to meet our clients' needs.
With these developments, the need for trustworthy workforce insights from our People Analytics expertise team is also rapidly growing. Therefore we are expanding our team and are looking for an energetic and hands-on data management specialist to join our team. In this role, you will play a key role in building and operating our recently set up data management capability. In this team, you will act as the bridge between People Analytics and HR business, systems and process colleagues, as well as enterprise Data Management functions. You will translate data management standards into practical execution, to enable HR data owners to take ownership of their data assets.
Role and responsibilities
In People Analytics, we unlock the potential of ASML’s workforce data to drive evidence-based people decision making in HR and across the business. To achieve our mission, we invest in three areas: data management, products & operations, and Partnering & Employee listening.
This role is part of the People analytics data management team, and will be part of the Data management competency in the HR tech ART (agile release train). This team has recently been set up and this role will help shape our data management framework towards a scalable and future proof expertise. To achieve this, we are looking for an experienced data management professional who combines hands-on execution with the ability to influence stakeholders, drive adoption, and shape the future of people data management within ASML.
Your main responsibilities in this role will include:
Partner with HR leaders, Business Process Owners, Data Owners, Data Stewards, and Subject Matter Experts to strengthen HR's data management capabilities, clarify accountabilities, and support the adoption of data management responsibilities across the organization.
Drive the implementation of People Data Management practices by translating policies, standards, and governance requirements into practical and sustainable ways of working that improve data quality, consistency, compliance, and business value.
Support the identification, documentation, governance, and lifecycle management of HR data assets, critical data elements, business definitions, and data products in alignment with enterprise standards and governance frameworks.
Act as a trusted advisor for HR data management, supporting stakeholders in solving data-related challenges, identifying improvement opportunities, and embedding governance principles within HR initiatives and transformation programs.
Develop and maintain business metadata, including business data models, data lineage, business glossaries, attribute definitions, and relationships between business processes, data assets, and supporting systems.
Support maturity assessments, monitor adoption of data management practices, identify improvement opportunities, and contribute to continuous improvement plans for People Data Management across HR.
Contribute to cross-functional alignment on data standards, quality requirements, governance decisions, ownership structures, and enterprise data management initiatives to ensure a consistent and trusted HR data foundation.
Support the development and execution of the People Data Management roadmap by translating HR, sector, and enterprise priorities into initiatives that strengthen governance, metadata management, stewardship, and overall data maturity.
The activities that might become part of this role as the capability matures:
Drive organizational change, communication, training, and adoption activities to further embed People Data Management as a core capability within HR.
Coordinate governance forums, stewardship communities, and decision-making processes that support effective ownership, accountability, and management of HR data assets.
Support the development of future-state business, information, and data architecture by connecting business capabilities, processes, business objects, data objects, and enterprise architecture principles.
Lead or support strategic initiatives related to data products, trusted data foundations, AI readiness, data democratization, and advanced data governance capabilities across HR.
Identify emerging trends, opportunities, and best practices in data management and translate them into capability improvements that increase the value, usability, and trustworthiness of HR data across the organization.
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Management, Data Management, Business Administration, Business Analytics, Human Resources, IT management or related field.
5+ years of experience in a relevant field or role; for example (HR) data governance, data management, analytics enablement, master data management, or related disciplines.
Experience within HR in expertise or HR data roles is a plus

Introduction to the job
ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers-the world’s leading chipmakers-to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Do you want to enable data driven decision making in a manufacturing environment?
Do you possess a keen eye for detail as well as a birds eye view on the production process?
Do you have an industrial engineering & analytical skillset combined with project management interest?
Then you are the candidate we are looking for to join the Business Engineering team as Business Partner for the Optical Fab!
Please apply and challenge us to hire YOU!
This is not a remote position and will require to be onsite at Wilton, CT
Role and responsibilities
You act as the right hand of the director to help unlock critical data and information, drive analyses and insights, set up reporting and dashboards, and drive continuous improvement. Typical areas for investigation are:
Capacity modeling: you build models and analyze scenarios to determine resource bottlenecks in the factory (people, tooling, floorspace, supply).
Performance Management & KPI’s: you drive continuous improvement efforts that enable management to secure targets related to yield, cycle time, and labor hours while influencing behaviors/decisions at several levels of the organization.
Data analytics: you build reports & data visualizations to make the performance of factory processes transparent, translating data into information.
In this position you will be able to further develop your analytical skills, business perspective, influencing skills, presenting techniques and project management capabilities.
You serve as a mentor to less experienced team members.
There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You will have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.

Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of three (3) years of professional experience with strong analytical, reporting, and data interpretation responsibilities, or a Master’s degree and a minimum of zero (0) years of professional experience required.
