Introduction
The Competence Team within Global Quality & Excellence (GQE) supports quality improvement across ASML by helping teams solve complex challenges and drive structural improvements. In this Internship, you will investigate issues in the return process of highly sensitive EUV mirrors, which are among the most critical and valuable components within ASML systems. By combining data analysis, stakeholder interviews, and structured problem-solving methods, you will help identify root causes and improve process performance. This internship offers a unique opportunity to work on a business-critical challenge with visibility across multiple departments. As an intern, you will contribute directly to improving quality and operational excellence within ASML.
Your assignment
During this Internship, you will become part of a quality investigation team and take ownership of a structured root cause analysis. You will work with experienced quality professionals and stakeholders from different parts of the organization to understand why issues occur in the return flow of EUV mirrors and develop sustainable improvement recommendations. The outcome of your work will support better process performance, quality, and operational reliability. Your main responsibilities will be:
Define and structure the problem statement using established problem-solving methodologies
Collect, organize, and analyze quantitative and qualitative data
Conduct stakeholder interviews to understand current processes and challenges
Identify root causes behind recurring issues in the mirror return flow
Validate findings using data-driven problem-solving techniques
Develop practical recommendations for structural process improvements
Present conclusions and improvement proposals to key stakeholders and management
This is a bachelor's or master's thesis internship for minimum 5 months, minimum 5 days per week. The start date of this internship is as of February 2027.
Your profile
To be suitable for the internship, you:
Are pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in industrial engineering, operations management, technical business administration, or a closely related field
Have experience with or knowledge of structured problem-solving methodologies such as Six Sigma, DMAIC, 8D, A3, or similar approaches
Are analytical and able to translate data into clear insights and recommendations
Are collaborative and communicate effectively with stakeholders from different backgrounds
Are proactive and comfortable taking ownership of complex investigations
This Internship is particularly suited for students who enjoy solving complex operational challenges, uncovering root causes, and creating sustainable improvements. You will receive coaching from experienced quality professionals while gaining exposure to cross-functional collaboration in a high-tech environment. Through this Internship, you will develop valuable skills in quality improvement, stakeholder management, data analysis, and structured problem solving. If you are looking for an impactful Internship, we encourage you to apply.
Other requirements you need to meet:
You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship;
If you are a non-EU citizen, studying in the Netherlands, your university is willing to sign the documents relevant for doing an internship (i.e., Nuffic agreement);
You attach your cover letter with a clear motivation on why you are interested in this internship assignment in particular;
You need to be located in the Netherlands to be perform your internship. In case you are currently living/studying outside of the Netherlands, your application shows the willingness to relocate.

As part of our drive to ‘future-proof’ our products, ASML aims to comply with legislation on hazardous materials and substances. Within Development & Engineering (D&E) Safety & Compliance, we facilitate & ensure that ASML is developing products that comply to regulations and customer requirements. To achieve this goal, the Hazardous Materials and Substances Competence group defines design/safety requirements and verifies compliance.

Networking within ASML and peers in other industries on legislation and implementation.
Collect and analyze relevant data from information systems to define priorities for improvement
Contribute to cross sector improvement programs
Help to embed the occupational health management processes in the EHS Information system
Connect with internal stakeholders on Occupational Health and Industrial Hygiene

Bachelor or master degree in Industrial Hygiene or Occupational Health Sciences
More than 3 years working experience as occupational health expert in the industry

Contribute to reporting and dashboards that support insight and decision-making.

Enjoy working with different stakeholders and building effective working relationships.

Introduction to the job
Are you ready to take on a global challenge? In this role, you will be responsible for installing our cutting-edge lithography systems at customer sites around the world—delivering on time, within specifications, and with quality that exceeds expectations. This position offers the chance to work with advanced technology while traveling extensively (about 70%) to diverse locations. You’ll continuously learn, adapt to new environments, and immerse yourself in different cultures as part of an international team. If you’re passionate about innovation, thrive on variety, and want a career that truly makes an impact, this is your opportunity to join us.

As an International Mechanical Install Engineer you truly understand the need to work safely at all times. You love to troubleshoot and utilize your knowledge, but know when to ask for support as well. Perform mechanical installation, adjustment, commissioning of a complete machine;
Install ASML equipment (NXE) at customer locations, including equipment with new features, pilot and proto systems;

Answer customer questions and assist customers in a professional manner;
Transfer knowledge to local install teams and first/ second line engineers;
Perform administrative duties including service orders, issue resolution tools, handovers, progress reporting, etc.;
Prepare written technical reports if required to do so;
Contribute in structural improvements for the System Install Engineering (SIE) department.
Exhibits strong shift lead competencies to lead engineering team inside the fab
Education and experience:
Vocational with at least 12 years of experience or Bachelor fresh grad, preference candidates with hands-on experience in similar positions in mechatronics, aerospace or automotive industry.

Proven affinity with assembling and troubleshooting is essential;
The preference is not given to candidates who only have work experience in precision/ fine mechanical assembly. A mix between gross and fine mechanics is preferred.

Excellent communication skills with focus on understanding, supporting, and influencing others;
Fluent in English, both in word and writing;
Safety first!;
‘First time right’ mentality;
Passion for hands-on engineering challenges;
Understanding the details without losing track of the bigger picture (helicopter view);
Remain a structured way of working in a dynamic environment;
Flexible;
Stress resistant;
Self-steering;
Team player.

Introduction
ASML is a world leader in the manufacture of advanced technology systems for the semiconductor industry. With over 40,000 people in more than 80 locations worldwide, ASML has an international presence in the semiconductor industry. ASML’s headquarters is in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and the company has 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Within ASML, the Corporate Intellectual Property (CIP) department is responsible for maximizing ASML’s global IP position to protect and support ASML’s business. In particular, the CIP department strives to preserve freedom to operate for ASML and to establish and maintain a portfolio of IP rights. The CIP department includes about 85 members distributed across four worldwide locations (Veldhoven in the Netherlands; and Wilton, San Diego, and San Jose in the USA).
The CIP department is seeking a qualified patent attorney. This position will be based in San Jose, CA and will report to the local Head of IP. The San Jose IP team provides IP support to scientists, engineers and management responsible for ASML products in computational lithography, metrology, and inspection.
Job Mission
The Patent Attorney will be responsible for working in close partnership with business units, engineers, cross-functional teams and other peers to provide a wide range of patent law related functions in the field of computational lithography, metrology, and inspection. Evaluate and protect company innovations and mitigate IP risk from a worldwide perspective. This is a great opportunity to join the local team of a well-established company with a global presence and get to work on cutting edge issues in an exciting, fast-paced environment.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Actively develop and manage a global patent portfolio, including assessing invention disclosures, conducting inventor interviews, presenting at invention review meetings, and recommending strategic portfolio maintenance.
Manage outside counsel to effectively prepare and prosecute high-quality patent applications, draft petitions, appeals, and/or other exceptional or non-routine papers as necessary to gain allowance/issuance and also provide guidance to outside counsel consistent with ASML objectives and operating guidelines.
Contribute to the execution of ASML IP strategies, including patent filing and product clearance.
Evaluate patent and other IP positioning of third parties to provide risk assessment, freedom-to-operate analysis, product clearance, and mitigation strategies and also evaluate any third-party infringement claims against ASML.
Interact and work regularly with key stakeholders in engineering and business organizations to acquire a deep knowledge of current and future ASML products and business goals, and develop and align ASML patent portfolio with those business goals, identify opportunities to establish IP protection, determine existence of patent risks and mitigate such risks.
Provide guidance and counsel to business teams on a range of intellectual property matters as requested or deemed appropriate.
Conduct periodic training to employees on intellectual property matters.
Occasionally assist with advising or structuring and/or negotiating inbound or outbound patent licenses.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Flexible to work extended hours when necessary to meet project deadlines and business objectives.
Some travel, both domestic and international, will be required.
Job description subject to change at any time.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s Degree in the engineering or physical sciences disciplines such as electrical, mechanical, systems and controls science, physics, materials, or optics. Advanced degree in physics with experience in optics a plus.
3+ years of relevant patent experience drafting and prosecuting patent applications and rendering patentability, non-infringement opinions and general risk analysis is required.
Must be licensed to practice before the United States Patent Office.
Must be licensed to practice law in at least one U.S. state or the District of Columbia, California preferred.
Experience with physics, optics, electron optics, and/or semiconductor processing strongly preferred.
Prior in-house experience preferred, including experience with interacting, developing and discussing strategy with engineers and senior management.
Experience planning and directing administrative staff and others in activities supporting the ASML’s IP work and objectives.
Strong foundational technical knowledge.
Proficiency with MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, at least one IP database, and on-line research tools.
Strong English communication skills, including the ability to read, write, and discuss complex legal and technical matters.
Personal Skills
Fully functioning in the job independently with only general direction required.
Strong professional drive to take on challenging assignments.
Decisive and self-initiating.
Ability to collaborate effectively with various teams across ASML including a diverse group of colleagues and internal clients in multiple countries.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Excellent judgment and critical thinking skills to understand how assigned responsibilities advance ASML’s business objectives and the ability to provide practical and actionable solutions and advice
Excellent client service ethics and skills, with an advanced understanding of client relationship-building
Ability to conduct detailed technical analysis while maintaining a high-level strategic view.

Introduction to the job
ASML is the world's leading supplier of lithography systems for the semiconductor industry. Across our global manufacturing network, thousands of employees contribute every day to building some of the most advanced machines in the world. To remain successful, ASML continuously evolves its processes, systems, and ways of working.
Many of these changes are driven by large-scale improvement programs that impact multiple sectors, factories, and employee groups worldwide. Within ASML, these initiatives are referred to as APIs (ASML Prioritized Initiatives): strategic transformation programs that help ASML prepare for future growth, scalability, standardization, and operational excellence.
While these initiatives create business value, successful implementation ultimately depends on people. Employees need to understand what is changing, why it is changing, and how they can successfully perform in the new situation. This is particularly important within Manufacturing, where global standards must often be translated into local factory realities, different organizational structures, and diverse target audiences.
This is where the Manufacturing Academy plays a key role.
Within the Manufacturing API Learning team, we help Manufacturing employees successfully navigate complex business transformations by translating change into effective learning, knowledge, and performance enablement solutions. We partner with global programs, Business Process Improvement (BPI), Manufacturing Change Management, Business Learning teams, factory stakeholders, subject matter experts, and end users to ensure people remain capable, confident, and productive throughout change.
To strengthen our team, we are looking for a Learning Professional (APIs) who thrives in complexity, enjoys creating structure in ambiguity, and is passionate about helping people perform successfully in changing environments.
Role and responsibilities
As our new API Learning Professional, you will operate at the intersection of learning, change enablement, business transformation, and manufacturing operations.
You will work closely with stakeholders across Manufacturing, BPI, Change Management, Learning organizations, and strategic programs to ensure employees are prepared for upcoming changes and can continue to perform successfully before, during, and after implementation.
In this role, you will work on:
Analyzing and understanding impact
- Conduct performance and learning analyses for large-scale transformation initiatives.
Identify the impact of process, system, and organizational changes on Manufacturing employees.
Determine when training is needed and when alternative performance support interventions are more appropriate.
undefined
Designing learning and enablement approaches
- Design learning, knowledge, and performance support solutions that help employees navigate change effectively using evidence-based methodologies to create.
In this role, you support:
Navigating complex stakeholder environments
- Act as a trusted advisor to programs, business stakeholders, and learning partners by aligning diverse perspectives and competing priorities
Represent the Manufacturing perspective in strategic discussions and decision-making.
Influence without formal authority while maintaining strong relationships across the ecosystem.
Creating structure in complexity
- Establish practical approaches, frameworks, templates, and working methods in situations where the path forward is not yet fully defined.
Provide input to the Learning Business Partner and Project Lead to create governance, planning, tracking, and reporting activities where needed.
Contribute to continuous improvement of the API Learning team's ways of working.
Ensuring business continuity
- Help Manufacturing organizations successfully adopt new ways of working with minimal disruption.
Enable employees to remain productive and effective throughout transformation journeys.
Contribute to scalable and sustainable learning solutions that can be leveraged across factories and future initiatives.
What you bring
We are looking for someone who combines Learning expertise with business acumen, stakeholder influence, and the ability to operate effectively in dynamic environments.
Education and experience
Bachelor's or master's degree in Educational Sciences, Learning Sciences, Change Management, Instructional Design, Organizational Learning, Educational & Organizational Psychology, or related discipline.
Task Experience
Experience conducting learning needs analyses and performance analyses.
Experience designing and developing learning solutions and performance support solutions.
Experience translating business requirements into practical learner-centered solutions.
Organizational Experience
Experience operating in complex stakeholder environments and matrix organizations.
Experience supporting large-scale business transformation, process optimization, change enablement, or digital transformation initiatives.
Skills and capabilities
Strong stakeholder management and consulting skills.
Excellent communication and facilitation skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to influence without formal authority.
Ability to navigate ambiguity and make informed decisions despite incomplete information.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with pragmatic execution.
Digital curiosity and affinity with technology-enabled learning solutions.
Experience leveraging AI-enabled tools within daily work.
You will thrive if you:
Enjoy solving time-sensitive complex challenges.
Feel comfortable operating in rapidly changing environments.
Can make progress when not all answers are available.
Are able to create structure where none exists.
Can balance competing stakeholder expectations.
Remain pragmatic when priorities shift.
Enjoy collaborating in a highly autonomous and self-driven team environment.
Have a genuine interest in helping people perform successfully through change.
Nice to have
The following experience would be considered an advantage:
Knowledge of ASML Manufacturing and factory operations.
Experience working within Digital Transformation, or Process Excellence initiatives.
Experience with Change Management practices and business adoption strategies.
Experience with performance support and workflow learning solutions such as the 5 Moments of Need® methodology.Experience with 4C/ID (Four Component Instructional Design) methodology.
Experience with 12 Levers of Transfer Effectiveness®.
Experience with learning evaluation and business impact measurement (ROI, Philips, Kirkpatrick).
Experience with Articulate Storyline, Synthesia, or similar learning technologies.
Experience using Copilot and other AI-enabled tools for analysis, design, and development activities.
Interested?
Do you enjoy turning complexity into clarity? Do you like working at the intersection of business transformation, learning, and human performance? Are you energized by helping Manufacturing employees succeed through change?
Then we would love to meet you.
Join the API Learning team and help shape how ASML enables its global Manufacturing workforce for the next generation of business transformation.
Ready to make change work for people, not just processes? Apply now and help us build the future of learning and performance at ASML.

ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our main headquarters are located in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we also have 18 office locations around the United States- including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.
U.S. Learning Shared Services (LSS) enables learning across the organization by providing reliable, scalable, and customer-focused learning operations and services. ASML supports the semiconductor industry’s ongoing quest for producing faster, smarter and more energy efficient chips. We are a young, dynamic, international and highly skilled workforce. ASML creates the systems that the lithography industry needs to achieve its goals. This can only be accomplished with a strong support of our suppliers.
Are you an engineer who is challenged by managing the logistics (delivery) performance of suppliers in a high tech-low volume environment, specialized in electrical, mechanical, chemical or optical engineering?

As Logistics Supplier Manager (LSM) you are responsible for the logistics (delivery) and operational performance of a selected number of suppliers. You work closely together with the supplier team, quality supplier manager, procurement account managers and New Product Supply Chain Engineers from ASML. Monitor, review and drive supplier logistics (delivery) performance from incidents to structural improvement
Optimize manufacturing processes at suppliers by improving logistics (delivery), manpower and capacity sufficiency
Build-up and develop technical competences within ASML (SPC, lean manufacturing, FMEA, operational excellence) to drive and support operational excellence at suppliers.
Limited travel, depending on assigned supplier base.

Experience in relationships with suppliers

Introduction to the job
Are you challenged by managing strategic suppliers with regard to supply chain management, capacity planning and cycle time reduction towards competitive Supply Chain performance?
The Supply Chain Manager (SCM) is ASML’s logistics interface to its supply base and responsible for material availability for ASML factories. In today’s complex multi-tier supply chains, this is only possible by creating full transparency in the chains and flexibility at suppliers. The SCM addresses potential bottlenecks and supply risks before they impact our customers. The SCM must handle the increased complexity of the ASML light source while reducing cost of ownership for customers. To do this, the SCM works with strategic suppliers to continuously reduce cycle times, secure capacity & increase flexibility and develop supply chain performance of suppliers. Driving supplier development in these areas ensures ASML’s supply base keeps pace with technological developments and can adapt to changing market conditions. The role also converts complex supply chain data into actionable insights, challenges assumptions through structured critical thinking, and leverages digital and AI-enabled tools to improve decision quality, scenario planning, and execution speed.
This position may require access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require the Company to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.
Role and responsibilities
Needs to have explicit experience working with supply/supplier versus demand management or purchasing/negotiation
Manage strategic suppliers towards competitive supply chain performance
Manage all logistics aspects in the Supplier Account Team together with the Account Lead (commercial aspects) and the Quality Supplier Manager (quality and technical aspects)
Drive Cycle Time Reduction projects at suppliers
Plan, align and control the required capacity, buffers and flexibility at our strategic suppliers

Use dashboards, analytics platforms, automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve supply chain visibility, early-warning capability, and operational efficiency
Apply structured critical thinking and problem-solving methods to challenge assumptions, determine root causes, and translate insights into clear actions and measurable outcomes
Ensure data quality, traceability, and responsible use of AI-generated insights, applying human judgment before recommendations or decisions are implemented
Education and experience

Self-starter with strong business acumen

Data-literate and digitally curious, with the ability to interpret trends, evaluate data quality, and communicate insights through clear visualizations and executive-level narratives
Practical understanding of AI concepts, opportunities, limitations, and responsible use, with the ability to identify relevant use cases and validate AI-supported outputs
Strong problem-solving capability, including root-cause analysis, scenario evaluation, prioritization, and conversion of insights into executable action plans

You will work together with a team of security professionals and the ASML Sector Security Representatives to drive the OT/ICS capability and verify the controls performance in the OT/ICS domain across ASML. You will act in close corporation with sector Facing teams (i.e. for Corporate Real Estate).
In this role, you support secure design, development and maintenance of ASML’s operational technologies and industrial control systems by ensuring OT Security capabilities are defined, implemented and monitored.
The role has 3 main focus points:
Determine our OT/ICS security risk control strategy, building blocks and design patterns of our internal control framework. To be designed with your OT/ICS security team
Implement and embed our OT/ICS security standards and policies throughout our sectors. Building bridges with your (internal and where needed external) business stakeholders is key to achieve success in implementing our policies and standards

Strategic thinking and enterprise mindset

Leading projects to results

ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market, and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers, the world’s leading chipmakers, to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics.
Job mission:
As a Manager for Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE), Technical Supplier Managers (TSM), and Cost Engineering (CE), this person will lead a team of SQEs, TSMs, and CEs who have the responsibility to develop industrialized solutions for Wilton’s new products in coordination with the internal design team and ASML key suppliers, and support initiatives to drive the cost of goods down. These new products include optical, opto-mechanical, opto-electronic, electronic, mechanical, and mechatronic systems, subsystems, and components. Using your leadership and technical skills, you will work closely with your team to optimize the effectiveness and efficiency of the product generation process and drive the industrialization process in alignment with the ASML project plan. In parallel, you will be responsible for engaging in and coordinating people management activities and driving the career growth of your team in line with the DM and sector expectations.
Job description:
Within the SC&Q department (SS&P), the TSM is the primary individual responsible for ensuring that the technical capabilities of our suppliers are aligned with the technical roadmap of ASML. The Cost Engineer is the primary individual responsible for delivering high-quality cost calculations for our designed parts and leading technical cost workshops with our suppliers. The Manager role will report to the Head of the SQE, Cost Engineer (CE), and TSM group in SS&P Wilton.

Directly manage a team of 10-15 Cost Engineers, SQEs, and TSMs.

Introduction to the job
ASML’s Production Engineer Team in Linkou supports the mature product portfolio—including PAS5500, YieldStar (YS), Reticle Handler (RH), and XT—with over 450 engineers across mechanical, precision mechatronics, electrical, software, and system specialties.
The team combines the strengths of Development & Engineering (D&E), Manufacturing, and Customer Support to ensure stable factory output, rapid issue resolution, and structural improvements across mature system generations.
As a Production Engineer (Precision Mechanics), you will focus on mechanical system behavior, precision motion assemblies, structural rigidity, tolerance-driven failures, vibration/coupling effects, and mechanical root-cause analysis impacting system performance.
This role is hands-on, system-oriented, and highly collaborative with D&E to drive structural solutions and prevent repeat mechanical issues.
Role and responsibilities
Mechanical System Troubleshooting & Analysis
Diagnose mechanical issues across PAS5500/YS/RH/XT modules, including precision stages, handlers, structural frames, bearings, flexures, linkages, brackets, actuators, and alignment mechanisms.
Perform in-depth investigations such as tolerance stack-up analysis, clearance/fit verification, torque behavior checks, thermal drift evaluation, friction/stiction assessment, and fatigue/wear pattern analysis.
Identify root causes involving misalignment, deformation, vibration coupling, assembly variation, mechanical instability, or loading inconsistencies.
Motion & Mechatronics Related Mechanical Issues
Analyze mechanical contributions to motion anomalies (position/velocity/acceleration behavior, following error, settling time).
Collaborate with S&C, electrical, and mechatronics engineers to interpret motion profiles, dynamic responses, mechanical resonances, backlash/compliance, and mechanical‑control coupling effects.
Support investigations into sensor/actuator mechanical interfaces involving mounting stiffness, interface design, alignment, and structural rigidity.
3rd-Line Engineering & Structural Fixes
Work with D&E on deep-dive mechanical investigations, structured root cause analysis (RCA), and validation of structural or design-related solutions.
Define clear mechanical problem statements when issues persist beyond 1st/2nd-line troubleshooting.
Review ECN proposals, verify mechanical design changes, and confirm effectiveness of implemented corrective actions.
Documentation & Diagnostic Improvements
Maintain and enhance mechanical drawings, assembly sequences, inspection procedures, torque guidelines, and mechanical diagnostic methods.
Identify gaps in mechanical diagnostics and propose new procedures, test steps, measurement tools, or workflows to strengthen troubleshooting efficiency and system reliability.
Create mechanical troubleshooting guides and lead diagnostic improvements across modules.
Production Support & Mechanical Stability Improvements
Ensure stable factory performance of mechanical modules across PAS5500/YS/RH/XT.
Lead DOE, measurement data analysis, structural validation, and mechanical hypothesis testing.
Evaluate mechanical design or process changes and quantify their impact on yield, robustness, stability, and issue recurrence reduction.
Required Qualifications
Education
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in:
Mechanical Engineering
Mechatronics Engineering
Precision Engineering
Automation / Manufacturing Engineering
or related disciplines.
Technical Background
3–5 years of experience in one or more of the following:
Precision machinery mechanical design
Mechanism design, tolerance analysis, assembly/process engineering
Motion system mechanics (bearings, sliders, flexures, stiffness, backlash)
Structural dynamics: vibration, deformation, fatigue
Mechanical failure troubleshooting in semiconductor, automation, robotics, or precision equipment
Core Mechanical Skills
Ability to read and interpret 3D CAD models and detailed mechanical drawings (NX/SolidWorks preferred).
Knowledge of tolerance stack-up, GD&T, torque control, mechanical fits, and assembly principles.
Understanding of motion mechanics, including thermal expansion, friction/wear mechanisms, stiffness, damping, and mechanical coupling.
Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills for system-level mechanical failure analysis.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with semiconductor equipment, automation machinery, robotics, or precision motion systems.
Hands-on experience with alignment processes, assembly fixtures, torque tools, or mechanical measurement instruments.
Familiarity with vibration diagnostics, modal behavior, structural stiffness evaluation, or experimental mechanics.
Exposure to ECN processes, structured RCA (5 Why, FMEA, Ishikawa), and reliability improvement projects.
Ability to design and execute controlled experiments to validate mechanical hypotheses and structural fixes.
Other Information
This role may require occasional weekend support to meet business and production needs. On average, such support is scheduled approximately once every two months and will involve working on either a Saturday or a Sunday (one day only, not both) at the Linkou Factory. Any weekend support requirements will be planned and communicated by the team in advance. Compensation will be provided in accordance with company policy.

enhanced stiffness/damping
vibration isolation measures
calibration/mapping optimizations
motion tuning packages

encoder/sensor integration
calibration/mapping techniques
vibration or dynamic behavior troubleshooting

Strong analytical reasoning; ability to design experiments and validate root causes with data.

Introduction to the job
Do you excel in managing and motivating others in technically challenging and complex projects? Do you have the ability to predict problems before they happen? ...And drive solutions! If so, a career as ASML Project Leader in Tainan Manufacturing awaits you.
Role and responsibilities
Your ultimate mission as a MFG Project Leader is to enable the factory to smoothly transition into the volume production of next generation HMI eBeam products. You will approach this mission from three directions: firstly, ensure meticulous pre-proto preparation of all new systems and products. Secondly, ensure that the factory team is fully trained and motivated. And thirdly, ensure that all possible design improvements identified in the previous generation and during the proto phase are accurately fed back to the Development and Engineering (D&E) organization and committed to be solved. This will help realize more reliable and manufacturable designs and ensure that cycle time and cost targets are hit on time. It is, of course, a difficult task and an exciting career for someone motivated by challenges.
As a MFG PL you will prepare the factory for a smooth transition/introduction of some of the most complex machines ever built – the HMI eBeam metrology product from ASML. You will be the key interface between D&E, Product Engineer (PE) and Manufacturing/Work Center. This typically means interfacing with teams in Asia, the Netherlands and the U.S. Your activities can broadly be divided into two types: pro-active preparation of the factory before the roll-out of new systems, and re-active trouble-shooting and damage control after.
Main Responsibilities
• Prepare the industrialization of all new HMI eBeam products, system and Modules, following ASML’s 6P=P process which covers Product, Procedures, People, Plant, Production Tools, and Parts.
• Prepare necessary documentation in order to pass each Key Decision gate check on time. (PGP 2011 process)
• Drive a large D&E (Development and Engineering) organization (10 to 30 separate projects per new product) towards a reliable and manufacturable system design
• Deliver prototypes on time while documenting all the issues to be solved before ramp to volume production.
• Assist to industrialize the proto and/or pilot production, create way of workings and prepare for ramping up and high volume production
• Drive issue resolution process to reach volume product maturity and cost targets
• Ensure output progress in pilot phase, plan for resource, e.g. manpower or qualified parts, for pilot production
• Specify and secure the training needs to enable the manufacturing group to build the systems.
• Feedback knowledge to D&E to ensure system design improvement, maintain the issue resolution escalation channel
• Serve the Production Engineering team and Sustaining Engineering team by making all of the new product requirements explicitly clear and then work with various competence owners to help them secure their deliverables on time
Education and experience
Master’s degree
Extensive project management experience (5+ years) in a high-tech equipment industry. Preferably experience in the area of new product introduction or design.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
• The ability to influence without power across a global organization to make sure that issues land at the right desk and are committed to a timely solution
• Structured, complete and multicultural communication without fear to speak up in front of unfamiliar audiences
• Understanding of design and assembly and test processes to ensure that you are able to find the right person when you need in-depth expertise and you can validate plans
• Expert planning capabilities to focus on the right level of detail and ensure resources are committed to keep the introduction plan on schedule
• High level of personal flexibility to travel and frequently attend conference calls at inconvenient times to facilitate global connections
• Determination to gather opinions within the manufacturing organization to ensure all voices are heard during the development and ramp up process.
• Work independently and bring clarity to un-clear situations by applying a balance of knowledge, experience and instinct.

Introduction to the job
Help solve some of the most complex materials challenges in the semiconductor industry. As a Materials Engineer at ASML, you will serve as the primary materials expert within a multidisciplinary team developing advanced modules and components for the EUV Lithography Light Source. You'll help ensure our products achieve the highest levels of performance, reliability, and quality while supporting the technology innovation that continues to move the world forward.
Role and responsibilities
As a Materials Engineer, you will provide technical leadership and expertise related to material selection, compatibility, characterization, and reliability for components operating in demanding thermal, mechanical, vacuum, plasma, and contamination-sensitive environments.
You will work closely with design engineers, scientists, suppliers, and quality teams throughout the product development lifecycle, helping to solve complex technical challenges and ensure long-term product performance.
As a Materials Engineer, you will:
Materials Engineering & Technical Expertise
Evaluate material compatibility within the EUV Lithography Light Source, including interactions under high-temperature, vacuum, plasma, and contamination-sensitive environments.
Provide expert materials guidance to design teams throughout concept development, detailed design, and verification phases.
Analyze material interactions such as corrosion, diffusion, oxidation, and multi-material compatibility.
Apply knowledge of engineering metals, including ferrous, non-ferrous, specialty alloys, and refractory metals.
Characterization, Testing & Microstructure Analysis
Perform and interpret materials evaluation techniques including hardness testing, tensile/compressive testing, fracture analysis, and metallography.
Analyze material microstructures, including grain morphology and phase distribution.
Evaluate surface conditions such as roughness, contamination, and cleanliness.
Utilize advanced characterization techniques including SEM, EDS/EDX, XPS, and AFM to support technical investigations and decision-making.
Failure Analysis & Problem Solving

ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Founded in 1984, ASML is the world’s leading provider of lithography systems for the semiconductor industry, manufacturing complex machines that are critical to the production of integrated circuits or microchips. This position is based on-site in Wilton, CT, which has both R&D and manufacturing operations. We design and produce multiple sub-system modules that are shipped to our headquarters in Veldhoven, The Netherlands where they are integrated into the full lithography machine.
As a Mechanical Engineer in Wilton, you will specify, design, develop, realize, integrate, and test modules and tools in close collaboration with cross-functional partners and suppliers. You will collaborate with system architects and senior engineers in a multidiscipline project team to develop concepts, perform engineering analysis, build and test prototypes, generate detailed CAD designs and create engineering drawings to deliver within system specifications, cost targets, and project schedules, ensuring timely realization of solutions that contribute to competitive, achievable, and serviceable products.

In a nutshell

Principal Applications Scientist, Memory Device & Process Integration
Location: Korea
Introduction to the role
ASML’s Technology Development Center, TDC, helps shape the company’s long-term technology direction by connecting semiconductor industry developments with future product and technology roadmaps.
We are looking for an experienced memory technology professional to analyze future memory device architectures and process-integration challenges from a global industry perspective. The primary focus of the role will be advanced DRAM device architecture and process integration, covering major technology paths and customer-specific approaches across the global DRAM industry.
In this role, you will own assigned DRAM-related technical topics, develop the underlying technology scenarios and roadmap inputs, and translate your insights into relevant implications for ASML product and technology roadmaps. You may also contribute to broader memory technology discussions where your expertise and analytical perspective are relevant.
You will collaborate with experts across ASML, customers, research organizations and external technology partners. The position is based in Korea, while its technology and stakeholder scope is global.
Roles and responsibilities
• Analyze future DRAM device, cell and array architectures and their process-integration implications.
• Reconstruct and evaluate process-integration flows for evolving and emerging DRAM architectures.
• Assess the interaction between device architecture, layout, materials, dimensions and process conditions.
• Identify physical limits, critical dependencies, integration risks and unresolved technical challenges.
• Follow relevant developments through customer inputs, publications, patents, conferences, internal sources and expert discussions.
• Develop and evaluate technical hypotheses using incomplete, evolving and sometimes conflicting information.
• Compare alternative technology paths and identify the conditions required for their technical feasibility and transition.
• Clearly distinguish technical evidence, assumptions, interpretations and uncertainties.
• Develop and maintain technology roadmaps for assigned DRAM device and process-integration topics, including their technical basis, alternative scenarios and open questions.
• Identify critical layers, process steps and requirements arising from future DRAM architectures.
• Translate device and process-integration developments into relevant implications for ASML technology areas.
• Work with experts across technical disciplines to validate assumptions and develop technically grounded recommendations.
• Contribute DRAM technology insights and roadmap inputs to the overall TDC memory roadmap and relevant ASML product and technology discussions.
• Provide technical guidance and knowledge transfer to stakeholders with different technical backgrounds.
• Participate in and, where appropriate, lead technical discussions with customers, research organizations and technology partners.
Education and experience
• Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Applied Physics, Chemical Engineering or a related scientific or engineering discipline.
• Proven industry or research experience in memory device development, device integration or process integration.
• Demonstrated experience analyzing complex device structures and process-integration flows.
• Experience independently driving complex technical topics from problem definition through analysis and recommendation.
• Experience working across technical disciplines to develop and validate conclusions.
• Experience translating detailed technical analysis into technology direction, roadmap input or organizational recommendations.
Skills
• Deep understanding of semiconductor device physics, device architecture or process integration in at least one memory technology area.
• Ability to connect device requirements and unit processes with the overall integration flow.
• Ability to identify physical limitations, critical integration dependencies and potential technical risks.
• Ability to decompose complex technical questions into key variables and testable hypotheses.
• Ability to develop credible technical scenarios from incomplete or conflicting information.
• Ability to compare multiple technology paths without prematurely converging on a single scenario.
• Ability to communicate the basis, validity range and uncertainty of technical conclusions.
• Ability to independently own a defined technical domain while actively seeking input and alignment from relevant experts.
• Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to experts in adjacent disciplines.
• Ability to provide technical guidance, conduct reviews and transfer knowledge within an assigned area of expertise.
• Ability to build and maintain an effective global network of technical stakeholders.
Preferred qualifications
• Experience in DRAM device or process integration.
• Experience with advanced DRAM scaling, alternative cell architectures or future DRAM integration concepts.
• Experience in technology pathfinding or roadmap development.
• Experience reconstructing customer or industry technology direction from indirect or limited information.
• Experience collaborating with semiconductor customers, research organizations or external technology partners.
• Experience leading technical reviews involving multiple engineering disciplines.
• Experience with device or process simulation, physical estimation or sensitivity analysis.
Prior knowledge of ASML products, lithography, patterning, metrology or inspection is beneficial but not required. These areas can be developed after joining through collaboration with relevant ASML experts.
Context of the position
This is an individual-contributor position with substantial technical ownership and functional leadership. The successful candidate will primarily own advanced DRAM device and process-integration topics and contribute the resulting insights to the integrated TDC memory roadmap and relevant ASML technology discussions.
The role is based in Korea but covers DRAM technology developments and customer-specific approaches from a global industry perspective. It is not limited to customers or technology developments in a particular region.
The role does not include people-management responsibility or final ownership of the overall TDC memory roadmap. It requires the ability to independently develop technical analyses and roadmap recommendations within the assigned DRAM scope while working closely with experts across organizational and geographic boundaries.
This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the United States Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). The Manufacturing Services (MFS) – Logistics Operations (LO) department is responsible for managing the logistics flows within ASML, such as Receiving, Picking, MICC, CRL & outbound, for both materials & tools. Introduction to the job
The Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE) for MLP Optics Competence is responsible for ensuring supplier capability, quality performance, and manufacturability of complex optical components and assemblies supporting ASML products. The SQE works closely with Development & Engineering (D&E), Manufacturing, Procurement, and suppliers to secure robust NPI introductions, drive continuous quality improvement, and mitigate supply chain risks.
The role focuses on early supplier involvement, supplier process qualification, NPI quality readiness, and resolution of complex quality and manufacturability challenges related to optical manufacturing processes such as precision optics fabrication, coating, cleaning, metrology, and optical assembly. This position requires influencing suppliers and stakeholders to achieve optimal quality, yield, cycle time, and technology readiness.
Role and responsibilities
1. NPI & Supplier Development
Engage suppliers during early Product Generation Process (PGP) phases.
Evaluate optical manufacturing technologies and supplier capabilities for new product introductions.
Drive supplier readiness reviews and qualification activities for complex optical components and modules.
Facilitate technology transfers and industrialization activities supporting new optical designs.
2. Supplier Quality Management
Establish and maintain supplier quality requirements, control plans, process validations, and acceptance criteria.
Ensure suppliers operate effective quality management systems consistent with ASML requirements.
Review process control methodologies for critical optical characteristics and key process indicators.
Monitor supplier quality performance and drive sustainable improvements.
3. Quality Issue Resolution
Lead structured problem-solving activities for supplier quality incidents.
Drive containment, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions using methodologies such as 8D, DMAIC, and FMEA.
Coordinate cross-functional teams to resolve complex optical quality issues impacting product performance or delivery.
4. Risk Assessment & Mitigation
Conduct supplier process audits and risk assessments.
Analyze manufacturing capability, yield performance, process stability, and metrology effectiveness.
Identify risks related to optical fabrication, coatings, contamination control, and assembly processes.
Develop mitigation plans to secure supply continuity and product quality.
5. Supplier Selection & Technology Assessment
Support sourcing and supplier selection activities through capability assessments and technical benchmarking.
Evaluate emerging optical technologies and manufacturing solutions.
Assess supplier maturity, scalability, and capability to meet future technology roadmaps.
6. Stakeholder & Supplier Partnership
Act as the primary quality interface between suppliers and ASML stakeholders.
Influence supplier management and engineering teams to implement quality improvements and process optimizations.
Facilitate alignment among D&E, Procurement, Manufacturing Engineering, SCM, and suppliers.
Build sustainable supplier relationships that support long-term business objectives.
7. Performance Reporting
Monitor and report supplier performance indicators including:
- PPM
Yield
On-time qualification
Process capability
Audit findings
NPI readiness
Provide management visibility of supplier risks and improvement plans.
8. Knowledge Development
Maintain expertise in optical manufacturing technologies, quality systems, and industry best practices.
Stay current on developments in precision optics, coating technologies, contamination control, and optical metrology.
9. Coaching & Best Practice Sharing
Provide technical guidance to peers and project teams.
Promote supplier quality excellence and continuous improvement methodologies within the organization.
Share lessons learned across optical supplier networks and internal teams.

Experience
5+ years of experience in Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, or Supplier Development.
Experience with complex NPI products in high-tech manufacturing environments.
Experience working with optical suppliers or precision manufacturing suppliers.
Skills
Strong understanding of one or more of:
Precision optics manufacturing
Optical polishing and grinding
Thin-film coating processes
Optical cleaning and contamination control
Optical assembly and alignment
Interferometry and optical metrology
Precision machining and ultra-precision manufacturing
Statistical Process Control (SPC)
MSA, FMEA, APQP, PPAP
Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma
Quality Competencies
Supplier auditing
Process qualification
Root cause analysis (8D, Ishikawa, 5 Why)
Risk management

The SQE operates independently within their area of expertise and influences decisions through technical knowledge and negotiation. The role interfaces with:

Introduction
At our global headquarters in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, we welcome students of all backgrounds to apply for our internships and graduation assignments. Worldwide, we have around 600 interns learning and contributing at ASML every year.
In Veldhoven, our Neurodivergent Interns Program provides the support that students with a form of neurodiversity (such as autism, ADHD, dyslexia and giftedness) need to succeed. You are invited to apply for targeted internship assignments. To do so we will keep you abreast of available opportunities within the program. If your internship application is successful, you’ll be matched with a mentor in your team who knows how to help bring out the best in a person with a neurodivergent brain. Mentors are aware of the strengths and weaknesses associated with different forms of neurodivergence and are motivated to see you grow professionally and personally and contribute to solving a particular challenge that the team faces.
Your assignment
You’ll get to explore your capabilities and develop your skills within a close-knit community of interns. Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
Internship start dates are February 1 and September 1 and the duration of each internship is 6–9 months. You’ll receive a full-time monthly allowance depending on your education level, and ASML will pay for public transportation (second class) between your home address and work location (unless you have a week or weekend student travel product).
Your profile
We welcome students in all fields of study who are pursuing associate’s, bachelor’s and master’s degree.
To thrive as an intern at ASML, you’ll need the following skills:
Fluency in English
Dedication to your work
A professional and responsible attitude
Curiosity and a willingness to learn as part of a team
Other requirements you need to meet
To participate in the Neurodivergent Interns Program, you need to be enrolled at an officially recognized academic institution in the Netherlands (such as an accredited school, college or university).
Please add a motivation letter with your reasonable accommodation requests or additional support needs. This so we can match you to the right mentor and team.

Introduction to the Job
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
As an Optical/Optomechanical New Product Introduction (NPI) Engineer within Strategic Sourcing & Procurement (SS&P), you will work closely with the Development & Engineering (D&E) organization and operate in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary product development environment. Using a combination of technical and personal skills, the NPI engineers develops and maintains a relationship with our suppliers to drive the industrialization efforts of the manufacturing process of our optical components and parts. This individual works closely with the suppliers and ASML cross-sector development teams to optimize the effectiveness and efficiency of the product generation process, in alignment with the ASML project. The main goal of this cross-sector activity is to secure an excellent quality of parts delivered by our suppliers.
Job Description
Within the SS&P organization, the Optical/Optomechanical NPI engineer is the primary person responsible for creating an optimal engineering collaboration between our optical suppliers and ASML, starting from early supplier involvement through product design and maturity. As part of the D&E project team, this individual works closely with their suppliers to understand and leverage their technology and processes and integrate these processes into the ASML new product development projects to drive industrialization efforts.
The main responsibilities are:
Early supplier involvement in the D&E project to secure that technology expertise of co-development and supplier are merged in the best way.
Ensure that part quality, manufacturability and serviceability aspects are covered in the design phase.
Document the D&E project collaboration, including supplier & co-development responsibilities and roles via a Statement of Work (SoW).
Support and own new product introduction (NPI) and support early supplier selection and engagement.
Deliverables that secure parts quality from suppliers in the co-development product generation process, such as:
Acceptance of the design and/or specification of complete & detailed parts qualification process
Acceptance of qualified parts
Process flow and Process failure mode effect analysis
First article inspection
Business demands will require travel (~20% but could be more during escalation situations and with notice)
Define and maintain supplier interface processes, such as:
Issue resolution
Qualification deviation
Configuration management
ASML factory disturbances
Contribute to supplier development to improve operational excellence by driving execution of existing agreements, improvement actions, and participation in supplier audits.
The NPI engineer is part of the D&E project team and, therefore, interfaces with SS&P DL, Delivery Team Lead (DTL), design engineers, architects, manufacturing & customer support engineers, logistics, procurement, etc.
Education and Experience
To help us tackle the technical challenges we face, you will need experience working on high-tech products and with complex processes.
Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Material Science (or similar)
Bachelor’s degree and at least 5 years of relevant professional experience; or
Master’s degree and at least 3 years of relevant professional experience.
Relevant work experience must have taken place as an experienced designer or process engineer who has gained experience in the areas of Quality systems and methodologies (Six Sigma Green or Black belt), as well as direct manufacturing and/or engineering experience including:
Manufacturing techniques including optical design, fabrication and polishing, optical materials, coatings, and precision measurement, interferometry, optical microscopy, fiber-optics, laser photonics, optical sensors, etc
Experience in at least one of the following: Precision mechanics, opto-mechanics, electro-mechanics, and laser modules.
Experience with new product introduction in a technically driven field
Technical improvement projects in supply chain operations
Value Engineering and cost-reduction projects
Working closely with suppliers on technical/manufacturing process development including mFLOW, pFMEA, SPC, RCA, etc

Instead, you will be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you will collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You will have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.

As a Manufacturing Group Lead, you will lead a critical production area responsible for building some of the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing systems. Your leadership will help ensure ASML delivers high-quality products on time while supporting technology that enables innovation across industries including healthcare, energy, communications, and mobility.
In this Manufacturing Group Lead role, you will provide both operational and people leadership for a large manufacturing organization. You will develop leaders, drive production performance, support new product introductions, and create a culture focused on safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Role and Responsibilities
As a Manufacturing Group Lead, you will oversee manufacturing operations, develop frontline leaders, and ensure production goals are achieved across your assigned area. You will balance short-term execution with long-term planning while partnering across functions to improve operational performance and organizational readiness.
You will:
Lead daily manufacturing operations to achieve production, quality, delivery, and cost objectives.

You will build and develop a high-performing team of quality professionals while driving factory-wide quality improvements that support production, customer satisfaction, and future growth. Lead, coach, and develop Quality Engineers and technical project leaders.
Establish team priorities, development plans, succession strategies, and talent growth initiatives.
Define and communicate the quality vision, roadmap, and strategic objectives for the factory.

Sponsor cost reduction initiatives that improve quality performance, operational efficiency, and business results.

Minimum 3 years of experience leading engineers, technical teams, or project leaders.

Within ASML, Planning & Delivery is an unbiased party, balancing demand and requests from customers against a stretched, however realistic view on our capability while also facilitating all good flows in a compliant and cost-effective way. This is done transparently and in close collaboration with all internal P&D interfaces, including all ASML factories worldwide.
The Delivery team oversees replenishment (inbound), order management and fulfillment and returnable packaging supply chain logistics
This role of Operational Planner (packaging) sits in the Delivery team.
The purpose of this role will be to ensure that all returnable packaging goods within the ASML Wilton network are tracked utilizing our internal tools and are available at the right time and in the right place to support factory and service requirements, in a compliant, timely and cost effective manner, ultimately meeting our Stakeholders and suppliers needs and agreed upon SLA's. Additionally, establishing metrics that will support pool size analytics to review pool size, demand from various business entities, evaluate supply chain performance vs expected cycle times and then make recommendations for changes / purchases.

Pool management extends globally from suppliers, through manufacturing to customer locations.

Administrative management of all packaging including registration and tracking ensuring all assets are tagged and recorded ·

Operational Service Fulfillment Kit Planner
In a nutshell
Location
Wilton, CT, US

Planning

Other technical backgrounds

Hybrid

Context and Purpose
The Operational Service Fulfillment Kit Planner plays a critical role in ASML’s service organization. They ensure customer availability of spare part and tool kits by panning and executing work orders for service spare kits per upgrade and install schedules, and forecast for maintenance and repair of customer machines world-wide.
Responsibilities
Work Order Management
Maintain Material Requirement Planning data for service spare kits to meet customer contracted commitments.
Release orders and monitor kit execution. Support material handlers as needed to ensure quality execution.
Work with cross-sector stakeholders to resolve shortages and gating issues preventing plan execution.
Root Cause Analysis and Issue Resolution
Identify and track root causes of missed KPI targets
Focus on structural issues and address problems at the root for long term solutions.
Contribute to preventing issues by proactive risk analysis, highlighting potential risks, and implementation of preventative measures.
Makes high quality decisions based on what is best for ASML and our customers.
Stakeholder Management
Actively maintain relationships with cross-sector stake holders.
Professionally manage conflict and escalations while maintaining strong positive relationships.
Convince and motivate stakeholders to implement improvements and manage risk.
Reporting
Prepare weekly report out for critical service kits.
Prepare weekly report out, D&S charts, and slides for escalated service kits.
Professionally report status of supply, root cause, containment, and structural improvements for critical and escalated kits.
Support cross-sector escalation owners as need.
Job Requirements
Education and Experience
High School diploma or equivalent required.
Bachelors Degree preferred.
Experience in Operational Planning, Supply Chain Management, Inventory Management, or equivalent working and thinking level.
Skills
Proficiency in Microsoft Office
Proficiency in SAP preferred.
Candidate must demonstrate strong soft skills, including stakeholder management, conflict resolution, agile learning, organization, and priority management

postings.title: Optical Fabrication Tech CWW Front End Days
postings.description:
Optical Fabrication Tech CWW Front End Days
In a nutshell
Location
Wilton, CT, US
Team
Manufacturing
Work experience
2-3 years
Educational background
Other technical backgrounds
Travel
10%
Workplace type
On-Site
Fulltime/parttime
Full time
Introduction to the role:
You will fabricate some of the world’s most advanced optical components used in the most advanced semiconductor photolithography machines. Through your attention to detail, results orientation, and commitment to task, you will produce high precision quality optics per production schedule. You will maintain the safety and workplace organization of your processing area. You will value adherence to standards while applying your experience and perspective to contribute to continuous improvement in our processing methods. You will enjoy success generated through your individual desire to learn and through teamwork with your colleagues.
We are looking for individuals like you to work in one of our processing competencies. These include: machining glass materials into final configuration using CNC milling equipment; grinding and polishing surfaces of optical components to rigorous dimensional and surface quality specifications; loading material into and operating deposition chambers to coat optics; precisely align and assemble glass parts with a high degree of accuracy in order to produce high quality optical assemblies; measuring optical characteristics of components using advanced metrology equipment for in process material processing feedback and final quality inspection.
Role & Responsibilities:
Shift: Front End Days 6 am – 6pm (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, alternate Wednesday)
Must be willing to work a compressed work week schedule- twelve-hour long shift and rotating from three to four days a week.
Actively monitor and take ownership of optical processing equipment
Handle delicate optical components and visually identify any abnormal characteristics.
Maintain area, tooling, and equipment to 5S area standards.
Identify and escalate any unsafe conditions.
Identify and escalate any product or process quality concerns in a timely manner.
Perform assigned work content to support area and factory schedule execution.
Collaborate with the Production Engineering and Manufacturing Management teams to improve operational efficiency and effectivity.
Learn and apply skills to tackle progressively more challenging products.
Identify and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives in how your work is defined and performed, and more broadly within your area, to improve safety, quality, output, and cycle time.
Inspect and create a map of glass surfaces showing all minute defects.
Clean optical surfaces of all particles and contaminants.
Accurately record time and attendance.
Assist with training new and existing employees
Education & Experience:
High school diploma or GED required
Associate degree in a vocational trade preferred.
Previous experience working in a manufacturing facility or completion of a vocational certification preferable.
Prior use of some of the following: measuring equipment desirable: microscopes, calipers, micrometers, coordinate measuring machine (CMM), interferometer.
Participation in continuous improvement efforts (quality circles, kaizen events, etc.)
Skills:
Commitment to task and results orientation to complete scheduled activities and report status throughout your shift.
Attention to detail to deliver quality results from your processing step, including visually inspecting your work to detect and report any abnormalities.
Organization of information and materials.
Ability to read and understand gages and other measuring devices.
Ability to interpret mathematical and geometrical data. An example would be experience reading and interpreting topographical maps.
Ability to effectively communicate written and verbal information.
Demonstrated ability to clearly document a problem using facts and data.
Accountable for your actions and willingness to engage in problem resolution.
Constructively challenge the status quo in search of a better way.
Care for yourself and others by confronting unsafe behaviors or conditions.
Take pride in your work and speak up when observing abnormal conditions in process or product.
Self-motivated learner.
Dexterity to handle optical components with care.
Other Information:
Routinely required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch. Occasionally required to move around the campus.
May require travel dependent on business needs.
Must be willing to work in a clean room environment, wearing coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses and gloves for entire duration of shift.
The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 35 pounds.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Must be comfortable working around lasers, working with ladders, working on platforms, and working around chemicals.
Must be able to work in a moderate to high noise level environment in a temperature-controlled environment
Must be comfortable operating/working around overhead cranes, fork trucks and motorized pallet movers.
May be exposed to moving mechanical parts, solvents and tooling.
You must be work authorized in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship
The current base annual hourly range for this role is currently:
Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members.
The Company offers employees and their families, medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are able to participate in the Company’s 401k plan. Employees will also receive eight (8) hours of vacation leave every month and (13) paid holidays throughout the calendar year.
