Optical Fabrication Technician CWW Front End Days 6 am – 6pm (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, alternate Wednesday)
In a nutshell
Location
Wilton, CT, US
Team
Manufacturing
Work experience
2-3 years
Educational background
Other technical backgrounds
Travel
Workplace type
On-Site
Fulltime/parttime
Full time
Job Description
Introduction to the role:
You will fabricate some of the world’s most advanced optical components used in the most advanced semiconductor photolithography machines. Through your attention to detail, results orientation, and commitment to task, you will produce high precision quality optics per production schedule. You will maintain the safety and workplace organization of your processing area. You will value adherence to standards while applying your experience and perspective to contribute to continuous improvement in our processing methods. You will enjoy success generated through your individual desire to learn and through teamwork with your colleagues.
We are looking for individuals like you to work in one of our processing competencies. These include: machining glass materials into final configuration using CNC milling equipment; grinding and polishing surfaces of optical components to rigorous dimensional and surface quality specifications; loading material into and operating deposition chambers to coat optics; precisely align and assemble glass parts with a high degree of accuracy in order to produce high quality optical assemblies; measuring optical characteristics of components using advanced metrology equipment for in process material processing feedback and final quality inspection.
Role & Responsibilities:
Front End Days 6 am – 6pm (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, alternate Wednesday) Must be willing to work a compressed work week schedule- twelve-hour long shift and rotating from three to four days a week.
Actively monitor and take ownership of optical processing equipment
Handle delicate optical components and visually identify any abnormal characteristics.
Maintain area, tooling, and equipment to 5S area standards.
Identify and escalate any unsafe conditions.
Identify and escalate any product or process quality concerns in a timely manner.
Perform assigned work content to support area and factory schedule execution.
Collaborate with the Production Engineering and Manufacturing Management teams to improve operational efficiency and effectivity.
Learn and apply skills to tackle progressively more challenging products.
Identify and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives in how your work is defined and performed, and more broadly within your area, to improve safety, quality, output, and cycle time.
Inspect and create a map of glass surfaces showing all minute defects.
Clean optical surfaces of all particles and contaminants.
Accurately record time and attendance.
Assist with training new and existing employees
Education & Experience:
High school diploma or GED required or equivalent experience.
Associate degree in a vocational trade preferred.
Previous experience working in a manufacturing facility or completion of a vocational certification preferable.
Prior use of some of the following: measuring equipment desirable: microscopes, calipers, micrometers, coordinate measuring machine (CMM), interferometer.
Participation in continuous improvement efforts (quality circles, kaizen events, etc.)
Skills:
Commitment to task and results orientation to complete scheduled activities and report status throughout your shift.
Attention to detail to deliver quality results from your processing step, including visually inspecting your work to detect and report any abnormalities.
Organization of information and materials.
Ability to read and understand gages and other measuring devices.
Ability to interpret mathematical and geometrical data. An example would be experience reading and interpreting topographical maps.
Ability to effectively communicate written and verbal information.
Demonstrated ability to clearly document a problem using facts and data.
Accountable for your actions and willingness to engage in problem resolution.
Constructively challenge the status quo in search of a better way.
Care for yourself and others by confronting unsafe behaviors or conditions.
Take pride in your work and speak up when observing abnormal conditions in process or product.
Self-motivated learner.
Dexterity to handle optical components with care.
Other Information:
Routinely required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch. Occasionally required to move around the campus.
May require travel dependent on business needs.
Must be willing to work in a clean room environment, wearing coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses and gloves for entire duration of shift.
The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 35 pounds.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Must be comfortable working around lasers, working with ladders, working on platforms, and working around chemicals.
Must be able to work in a moderate to high noise level environment in a temperature-controlled environment
Must be comfortable operating/working around overhead cranes, fork trucks and motorized pallet movers.
May be exposed to moving mechanical parts, solvents and tooling.
You must be work authorized in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship now or in the future.
This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require ASML to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.

Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members.
The Company offers employees and their families, medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are able to participate in the Company’s 401k plan. postings.title: Optical Sensor Design Engineer
postings.description:
Optical Sensor Design Engineer
In a nutshell
Location
Wilton, CT, US
Team
Design Engineering and Architecture
Work experience
4-9 years
10-15 years
16+ years
Educational background
Physics
Mechanical Engineering
Electrical Engineering
Other technical backgrounds
Technical field
Optical Sensing
Travel
10%
Workplace type
On-Site
Introduction
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Job Mission
ASML’s Wafer Alignment Sensor department in Wilton CT is seeking a Design Engineer to support and develop complex optical/photonic sensor systems used within ASML’s photolithography tools. These systems typically include light sources, detectors, optical/electro-optical components, fiber optics, electronics and signal processing software functioning in close collaboration with the rest of the lithography system. As a design engineer, you will design, develop, build and integrate optical sensor systems.
This position may require access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). As a condition of employment, qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require the Company to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.
Role and Responsibilities
Use general Physics, Optics, Software knowledge and an understanding of the sensor systems and tools to develop optical alignment sensors in lithography machines
Have hands-on skills of building optical systems (e.g. imaging, testing, alignment, detector system, etc.)
Have strong data analysis skills to evaluate sensor performance and troubleshooting
Leadership
Lead executing activities for determining problem root cause, execute complex tests, gather data, and effectively communicate results on different levels of abstraction (from technical colleagues to high level managers)
Lead engineers in various competencies, eg software, electronics, equipment engineering, manufacturing engineering in support of feature delivery for alignment sensors
Problem Solving
Troubleshooting complex technical problems
Develop/debug data signal processing algorithms
Develop and execute test plans in order to determine problem root cause
Communications/Teamwork
Good communication skills during brainstorm/troubleshooting sessions
Good listening skills
Good analytical skills
Draw conclusions based on the input from different stakeholders
Capability to clearly communicate the information on different level of abstraction
Programming
Implement data analysis techniques into functioning MATLAB codes
Optimization skills
GUI building experience
Familiarly with LabView and Python
Some travel (up to 10%) to Europe, Asia and within the US can be expected

Introduction to the job
As we enter a new era of technology, everything and everyone will be more connected, and the lines between the physical and digital worlds will become less distinct. Rapid advancements in generative AI, self-driving cars, and artificial intelligence are driving an increased demand for advanced chips. At ASML, we are at the forefront of these changes with our technology, making it essential for our workforce to be well-organized and to be fully empowered to meet our clients' needs.
With these developments, the need for actionable workforce insights from our People Analytics expertise team is also rapidly growing. Therefore we are expanding our team and are looking for an energetic and hands-on People Analytics Partner to join our team. In this role, you will be pivotal in translating complex people data into actionable insights that enhance organizational effectiveness and support our HR and business leaders in navigating this evolving landscape.
Role and responsibilities
In People Analytics, we unlock the potential of ASML’s workforce data to drive evidence-based people decision making in HR and across the business. To achieve our mission, we invest in three areas: People Data Management, Products & Operations, and Partnering & Employee listening.
As a member of the People Analytics Partnering & Employee Listening team, you will play a crucial role in transforming people data into actionable insights that drive strategic decision-making across the organization. Collaborating with a diverse range of stakeholders—including business leaders, people managers, and the HR leadership team, you will help shape the future of our workforce. Support on people analytics partnering projects hands-on and end-to-end: collaborate with HR and business stakeholders, data scientists and analysts from design to delivery.

Contribute to shaping and executing of the ASML people strategy pillars with actionable people insights.
The focus of your work may change over time based on the team's priorities and needs. Alongside the core responsibilities listed above, you may also be involved in the following tasks:
Support in formulating strategies to generate and validate people-related metrics, define target settings,
Support the creation of strategies and facilitate the deployment of reliable data sets to advance data democratization across the organization, and ensure adherence to operating models and governance.
Help identify opportunities to enhance the foundation of our People Analytics expertise, focusing on accelerating value generation, adoption, ROI, and scalability for products and projects.
Contribute to designing and supporting change initiatives that foster a data-driven culture transformation in HR, including the development of training materials and innovative concepts.
Contribute in designing and supporting employee listening initiatives (e.g., annual engagement survey, exit surveys) to gather feedback and ensure employee voices are included in decision-making processes, including execution of we@ASML, our global engagement survey.
Drive the broader development of employee listening into a CoE: Alignment with different stakeholders in enabling function sectors, define and deliver deliverables of listening strategy with focus on people data insights in a safe and secure IT technology landscape.

Introduction
The Contamination Control team at ASML develops solutions that help protect critical components inside advanced lithography systems. Even the smallest particles can affect highly sensitive optical surfaces, making contamination control an important area of research. In this internship, you will contribute to understanding the behavior of supersonic gas jets at extremely low ambient pressures using advanced optical diagnostics. Your work will help generate insights that support future contamination-control technologies for ASML systems. This Physics Engineering internship offers a unique opportunity to combine fluid dynamics, optics, and experimental research in a challenging high-tech environment.
Your assignment
During this internship, you will help develop and operate an advanced experimental setup for visualizing supersonic gas flows at low ambient pressures. You will work on improving measurement capabilities, performing experiments, and analyzing complex flow phenomena. The results of this project will contribute to future contamination-control concepts and provide recommendations for further technology development.
Your main responsibilities will be:
Upgrade an existing Schlieren imaging setup for low-pressure flow visualization
Develop and implement automated flow and optical control methods
Design and perform experiments across a wide range of pressure conditions
Analyze flow structures, shock patterns, and jet expansion behavior
Compare experimental results with theoretical models and simulation outcomes
Document findings in a clear and structured manner
Present recommendations for future experiments and potential applications
This is a master thesis internship for minimum 6 months, minimum 36 hours per week (4 days on-site). The start date of this internship is as of January or February 2027.
Your profile
To be suitable for the internship, you:
Are pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in physics engineering, applied physics, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related field
Have knowledge of fluid dynamics, optics, or experimental physics
Are analytical and enjoy investigating complex technical challenges
Take initiative and are comfortable working in a pioneering research environment
Communicate clearly and collaborate effectively with others
Have a structured and proactive approach to experimental work and data analysis
This Physics Engineering internship is ideal for students who enjoy hands-on experimental research and want to explore flow phenomena in a pressure regime that remains largely unexplored. You will work with advanced optical diagnostic techniques, contribute to meaningful research, and gain experience in a multidisciplinary environment. The Physics Engineering internship provides the opportunity to combine theory and experimentation while developing technical and professional skills. Through this Physics Engineering internship, you will help advance knowledge that supports future innovations in contamination control for ASML's next-generation lithography systems.

Join a pioneering research team developing next-generation lithography light source technologies. Our laser-produced plasma (LPP) system integrates high-power lasers, advanced optics, plasma-based EUV generation, sensing, and algorithm-driven control. The Physics Informed Machine Learning Scientist works on the Virtual Source team building integrated master-model frameworks to capture the tightly coupled, multi-physics behavior of the system—enabling system-level optimization, reducing uncertainty in future source configurations, and guiding early technology decisions. Introduction to the role
Laser-Produced Plasma EUV is generated by firing high energy laser pulses at tin droplet targets at kilohertz repetition rates. The resulting plasma pulses create both desired EUV light, and undesired Tin debris in the form of ballistic particulates and atomic vapor. If unabated, the Tin debris will coat all surfaces in the vessel, including optical components, impacting the transmission of EUV and Laser light.
We are looking for a Technical Lead. The objective is to identify technologies and design concepts that can be developed to address undesired tin debris using thermal and flow schemes, and partner with Project Management to ensure delivery of robust product solutions. The successful candidate will be a highly motivated and enthusiastic individual with a broad technical background, excellent communication skills, and ability to influence others. As a Technical Lead you will work with a team of highly professional engineers and scientists with diverse academic backgrounds and many years of experience. Your job is to provide technical leadership to the team to deliver practical solutions to enable this complex function.
Role and responsibilities
Own and be the technical leader within the delivery team for technical solutions and required hardware related to tin mitigation. Confer with FEA/CFD analysts and use engineering knowledge and intuition to convince high level stakeholders of the right technical program direction.
Hands-on engineering leader that identifies and drives execution of concepts that can address thermal, flow, and mechanical performance gaps; assesses technology maturity and defines the development and engineering work breakdown for execution by cross-functional teams of seasoned scientists and engineers.
Leads architecture and prototyping definition; develops and provides recommendations for practical tradeoffs between the optimal technical approach vs practical engineering solutions; works with cross-functional teams of mechanical engineers, materials scientists, electrical and software engineers to develop solutions to roadmap.
Develops and maintains sub-module specification document tree; writes and/or reviews key specification and design documentation, coordinates key reviews with Systems Engineering and Project Stakeholders to ensure functional specifications are aligned to system requirements.
Defines Test Protocols; analyzes test data; makes recommendations based on test results for design changes and operational changes to deliver improved performance of sub-modules.
Assesses technology and project risks and defines risk mitigation strategies and approaches with the project leadership team.
Mentors, coaches and oversees the activity of more junior engineers and Competence organizations.
Negotiates interfaces and performance / industrialization specifications between related sub-functions and systems engineering.
Define and continuously update sub-function roadmaps for future products.
Hands-on experience with hardware, testing, prototyping and system troubleshooting.
Experience with the entire product development lifecycle.
Perform other duties as assigned.

10+ years of relevant experience.

ASML US, LP brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.
Job Mission
We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced Principal Scientist - Tin Management Architect to join the Source Research department in San Diego and lead the definition and evolution of the next-generation Tin Management architecture for future lithography light sources.
ASML's leadership in lithography depends on continued innovation in source technology. A key challenge for future EUV systems is the management of tin debris generated during the laser-produced plasma (LPP) process. Effective Tin Management is critical to protecting source hardware, maintaining optical performance, enabling higher source power, and reducing cost of technology. As the Tin Management Architect, you will define the long-term technology roadmap and system architecture required to address these challenges. Working across research, modeling, and product development teams, you will evaluate architectural trade-offs, identify key technology gaps, guide research investments, and shape future source concepts.
The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise with strong systems thinking and the ability to operate effectively in a multidisciplinary environment. Success in this role requires balancing physics, engineering, modeling, manufacturability, and cost considerations to drive architectural decisions at the fuzzy front end of product development.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Define and drive the long-term Tin Management architecture and technology roadmap, identifying architectural challenges, technology gaps, development priorities, tradeoffs, and critical learning required to guide future EUV source development.
Shape experimental strategies and learning plans for research test rigs, ensuring test campaigns address key architectural questions and produce actionable system-level insights.
Define the modeling, simulation, AI, and data capabilities required to support Tin Management decisions, and guide their development in collaboration with Virtual Source, analysis, and research teams.
Drive technical alignment between research, system engineering, product development teams, and external stakeholders to ensure Tin Management learnings influence future product architectures and node development.
Capture, document, and communicate architectural learnings and technology recommendations to leadership and development teams through reports, reviews, and executive presentations.
Work independently and across multidisciplinary teams to pursue new knowledge, demonstrate new capabilities, and solve critical system-level challenges.
Provide technical leadership for critical Tin Management initiatives while remaining actively engaged in hands-on technology development, experimentation, modeling, and problem solving for approximately 50% of the role.
Perform other duties as assigned or required.
Qualifications
Ph.D. in Physics, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related discipline, with 5+ years of relevant experience, and demonstrated expertise in complex physical systems and one or more areas such as thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, plasma physics, lasers, photonics, or related technologies.
Strong background in experimentation, modeling, simulation, and data-driven decision making.
Experience applying computational modeling, data analytics, AI/ML, and digital engineering tools to technology development challenges.

ASML Wilton is seeking a Senior Process Engineer to join the Wilton Factory Optics team with primary ownership of functional testing and inspection processes. This role is responsible for process development, stabilization, and daily performance across automated and manual functional testing and inspection operations. The position requires a deep technical understanding of optical fabrication, strong analytical capability, and the ability to drive sustainable improvements in a fast-paced production environment.
The engineer will directly support output, yield, and quality targets—including improving First Pass Yield (FPY) through stable, predictable, and well controlled process behavior.
This role requires a proactive engineering mindset: anticipating issues before they impact production, driving structured 6P readiness, performing thorough RCA, and continuously evaluating new technologies to strengthen long-term process control. This is not a reactive support role; the expectation is ownership, foresight, and continuous improvement.
Job Description
The Senior Process Engineer will operate as a technical leader within Wilton Factory Optics with end-to-end ownership of functional testing and inspection processes. Responsibilities include defining and optimizing process parameters, ensuring measurement stability, selecting tooling, and understanding machine behavior. The engineer will manage functional testing and inspection process performance, inspection and functional testing control strategies, and inspection and functional testing output quality while ensuring consistent results across tools, people, and shifts.
The functional testing and inspection scope includes control of tooling, environment, fixturing, and other factors influencing inspection output. The PE will lead the introduction and qualification of new fixtures, tools, software, manual processes, and machine upgrades, and will convert functional testing and inspection data into actionable decisions.
A key responsibility is establishing strong process control: defining process windows, capability targets, and long-term monitoring systems. The PE will use JMP or Minitab to identify variation, drift, and chronic stability risks, ensuring processes are robust, documented, and repeatable. This includes maintaining process specifications, work instructions, and standard work while driving alignment across production and support teams.
The engineer will collaborate daily with production technicians, supervisors, cross factory teams, quality, equipment engineering, and maintenance, balancing immediate production needs with structured long-term improvement projects.
The Senior PE is expected to:
• Build process stability that prevents rework and FPY loss
• Detect and eliminate sources of variation impacting FPY and yield
• Lead structured RCA using statistical and analytical methods
• Ensure corrective actions are verified, embedded, and sustainable
• Own full 6P readiness for process, material, or equipment changes
Beyond daily support, the engineer is expected to proactively seek, evaluate, and integrate:
• Functional testing and inspection process control methods
• Advanced functional testing and inspection tools
• Next generation functional testing and inspection technologies
• Equipment or software capabilities that improve stability, predictability, and throughput
Education and Experience
• BS, MS, or PhD in Mechanical, Optical, Materials, or related engineering field
• Minimum 5 years of experience in optical fabrication and functional testing and inspection
• Experience in tooling mechanics, inspection methods, functional testing methods, and process development
• Demonstrated ability in structured problem solving, data analysis, RCA, and process improvement

• Strong understanding of functional testing and inspection best practices and tooling mechanics for accurate measurements
• Proficiency with manual and automated functional testing and inspection tools
• Proficiency with spectrometry equipment required
• Proficiency with electrical, pressure, and hardness testing equipment highly desired
• Experience using JMP, Minitab, or equivalent statistical software
• Strong communication, cross functional collaboration, and leadership in a production environment
• Ability to manage multiple priorities under time sensitive conditions
• Demonstrated capability in 6P readiness, structured RCA, and verification driven corrective action

Translate operational data into actionable insights and recommendations.
Act as the operational focal point for material availability related topics.

Introduction to the Job
ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
The Production Engineer 2 is responsible for developing, optimizing, and sustaining manufacturing processes to support both New Product Introductions (NPI) and volume production. This role requires hands-on experience in a high-tech manufacturing environment, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to lead small-scale projects independently. The position emphasizes continuous improvement, cross-functional collaboration, and technical leadership to ensure operational excellence.
Roles and Responsibilities
Process Optimization & Continuous Improvement
Develop and optimize processes for NPI and volume manufacturing.
Implement SPC for new products and monitor process stability.
Drive structural improvements for recurring manufacturing issues and chronic quality challenges.
Manufacturing Process Development
Develop and maintain manufacturing procedures, technical work instructions, and process specifications.
Create and update process documentation, routings, and sequences for factory execution.
Role model compliance with quality, safety, and regulatory standards.
New Product Introduction (NPI)
Support introduction of new products into production within a concurrent engineering environment.
Participate in design reviews, PFMEAs, and documentation reviews to ensure manufacturability.
Evaluate and optimize tooling for NPI and volume manufacturing
Production Support & Troubleshooting
Provide technical support assisting First Line Support (FLS) for production issues, including troubleshooting modules and driving to root cause resolution
Evaluate and disposition parts with quality issues, validate supplier failure analysis reports, and implement corrective actions.
Provide technical details and recommendations during root cause analysis (RCA) investigations and escalations.
Participate in DRB/MRB to drive structural solutions
Drive small-scale Lean and Six Sigma improvement initiatives.
Planning & Control
Maintain MRP controls for module production and support production planning activities.
Perform cycle time analysis, capacity planning, and present findings to stakeholders.
Collaboration & Communication
Work closely with cross-functional teams to further industrialization
Collaborate with internal teams and external customers regarding assembly and testing of components and final products.
Provide clear and timely reporting on improvement actions, cycle time analysis, and project progress.\
Document results, write procedures, and support qualification plans.
Education & Experience
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Industrial, or Manufacturing Engineering (or related field).
Experience: 2–4 years in production engineering or process development.
Solid understanding of SPC, PFMEA, and lean principles.
Proven ability to manage projects and deliver improvements.
Technical Requirements
Experience with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma tools (Kaizen, 5S, DMAIC).
Proficiency in CAD tools (SolidWorks, AutoCAD, NX).
Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes (machining, assembly, automation, material handling).
Strong understanding of SPC, PFMEA, and root cause analysis methodologies.
Familiarity with ERP/MES systems for routing and documentation updates.
Competence in data analysis tools (Excel, Minitab, or similar statistical software).
Knowledge of GD&T and ability to interpret complex engineering drawings.
Role model of safety standards, compliance, and risk mitigation in manufacturing environments.
Hands-on experience with process validation and equipment qualification.
Key Competencies
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Effective communication and ability to influence cross-functional teams.
Adaptability and resilience in a dynamic environment.
Proactive mindset with a focus on continuous improvement.
Customer focus and commitment to satisfaction.
Ability to train and coach junior colleagues in technical problem-solving and process knowledge.
Professional, clear, concise communication.
Leadership & Behavioral Competencies
Influences and support others based on professional knowledge.
Coach and mentor junior colleagues.
Present technical matters effectively within competence groups and to key interfaces.
Provide guidance, feedback, and demonstrate listening skills.
Collaborate across sectors and maintain cooperative working relationships.

15% documenting results and writing procedures.
25% collaborating with Manufacturing Engineering on process recommendations and qualification plans.

Introduction to the Job
As a Senior Production Engineering Tooling Designer, you will create advanced mechanical, electrical, and mechatronic tooling for high-tech manufacturing. Your work will help production teams build complex technology safely, accurately, and efficiently. You will guide tooling from requirements and early concepts through qualification, release, and ongoing production support.
Role and Responsibilities
You will lead tooling design projects of varying complexity from concept through production. You will collaborate with production engineers, technical support teams, technicians, project leaders, and other partners to meet safety, quality, cost, and schedule requirements.
Define functional requirements and technical specifications with engineering teams, technicians, and internal customers.
Develop business cases, design proposals, risk assessments, and environmental, health, and safety reviews.
Design complex manufacturing tools, fixtures, and jigs that meet safety, ergonomic, and regulatory requirements.
Create detailed three-dimensional models and two-dimensional drawings using computer-aided design software.
Lead design reviews and apply tolerance, motion, material, structural, thermal, and performance analysis.
Release qualified designs with complete documentation for procurement, production, duplication, and lifecycle support.
Resolve advanced tooling issues, implement corrective actions, improve processes, and support investment planning.
Education and Experience
To succeed as a Senior Production Engineering Tooling Designer, you will need:
A bachelor’s or master’s degree in mechanical, electrical, mechatronics, manufacturing engineering, or a related field.
At least five years of experience in manufacturing tooling design, production engineering, process development, or manufacturing.
At least three years of experience leading projects and improvement initiatives.
Proficiency with three-dimensional design software, such as SolidWorks, CATIA, Siemens NX, or AutoCAD.
Experience with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, manufacturing processes, and finite element analysis.
Experience with enterprise resource planning, product lifecycle management, and engineering change processes.
Experience working in semiconductor, high-tech, complex assembly, or cleanroom environments is preferred.
Certification in geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, project management, Lean, or Six Sigma is preferred.

Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Translate manufacturing needs into clear, practical tooling requirements.
Communicate technical decisions clearly to engineering, production, and leadership partners.
Analyze complex problems and use evidence to identify sustainable solutions.
Collaborate effectively across disciplines, roles, and levels of technical experience.
Balance safety, quality, cost, schedule, and production needs when making decisions.
Mentor junior engineers and share tooling design and problem-solving practices.
Lead continuous improvement with a proactive, organized, and accountable approach.
In this Senior Production Engineering Tooling Designer role, you will combine hands-on technical expertise with project leadership. You will help strengthen tooling reliability while supporting safe, efficient, and scalable manufacturing.

In our high-tech small production runs, single part and prototype production, you will support us in the high-precision manufacture of optical components, assemblies and systems made of glass, glass ceramics and ceramics.
Role and responsibilities
As a Production Operator in High-Tech Manufacturing, you will:
Apply your skills across various production areas within ASML Berlin, depending on business needs and qualifications
Grind and polish optical or ceramic components with high precision
Assemble and fine-clean components under gray room and cleanroom conditions
Join components into assemblies using processes such as thermal bonding, anodic bonding, gluing, and flame bonding
Operate coating systems and perform lithographic processes including coating, laminating, and exposure
Conduct and evaluate quality control measurements using a variety of measurement systems and equipment
Document measurement results and production data accurately and clean components, tools, auxiliary materials, and packaging using dedicated cleaning equipment
Education and experience

Initial professional experience in a production, manufacturing, or laboratory environment
Experience working in cleanroom environments
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
Experience using SAP in a manufacturing environment

Good German language skills

Working in a highly precise manufacturing environment requires accuracy, reliability, and strong collaboration across different production areas. To succeed in this role, the following skills are important:
Strong fine motor skills for handling delicate components and performing precision work
Careful and structured working style when completing repetitive or detail-oriented tasks
High level of attention to quality and the ability to recognize deviations on sensitive surfaces
Reliability and accountability when working within strict production and quality standards
Team-oriented mindset with the ability to collaborate effectively in a manufacturing environment
Physical resilience to perform tasks in standing positions and under production conditions
Flexibility to adapt to changing priorities, processes, and operational requirements
Other information

Job with bright future prospects at an innovation leader in the semiconductor industry in Berlin Neukölln
Remuneration in accordance with the IG Metall collective wage agreement (company-specific collective wage agreement) including 13th month’s salary and variable remuneration components
Collective working time: 35 hours/week

Dein Arbeitsumfeld
An unserem Standort in Berlin fertigen unsere Mitarbeitendenden Schlüsselkomponenten für die ASML Lithografiesysteme. Als Teil unserer Präzisionsfertigung unterstützt du bei der Produktion optischer Komponenten, Baugruppen sowie Systeme aus Glas, Glaskeramik und Keramik für unsere High-Tech-Kleinserien, Einzelteil- und Prototypenfertigung.

Als Produktionsmitarbeiter:in in der High-Tech Fertigung wirst du:
Je nach Qualifikation und betrieblichem Bedarf in unterschiedlichen Produktionsbereichen bei ASML Berlin eingesetzt
Optische oder keramische Bauteile mit hoher Präzision schleifen und polieren
Bauteile unter Grau- und Reinraumbedingungen montieren und feinreinigen
Komponenten durch thermisches Bonden, anodisches Bonden, Kleben oder Ansprengen zu Baugruppen fügen
Beschichtungsanlagen bedienen und lithografische Prozesse wie Belacken, Laminieren und Belichten durchführen
Qualitätskontrollmessungen mit unterschiedlichen Messsystemen und Messmitteln durchführen und auswerten
Messergebnisse und Produktionsdaten dokumentieren sowie Bauteile, Werkzeuge, Hilfsmittel und Verpackungen mit dafür vorgesehenen Reinigungsanlagen reinigen

Abgeschlossene technische Berufsausbildung in den Bereichen Optik, Physik, Chemie, Fertigungstechnik oder einem vergleichbaren technischen Umfeld

Introduction to the job
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
The D&E Functions Group in the Cymer Light Source Division of ASML, located in San Diego, performs the Design and Engineering of new and upgraded DUV Source products, and other supporting projects. The work is diverse, fast-paced, and innovative. The Light Conditioning Team is responsible for the development and engineering of the optical systems and light conditioning solutions that shape, stabilize, and optimize laser performance to meet system and customer requirements.

As a Project Lead in Light Conditioning Team, you are responsible for the organization, structure, project planning, and delivery of the optical components/modules in any projects that light conditioning group involved in. The activities cover the complete development cycle, including architecture and requirements definition, design, implementation, integration, validation and test, high volume manufacturing and lifecycle support and troubleshooting. Introduction to the Job
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
ASML Wilton, Connecticut is seeking a Quality Program Leader to serve as the organizational leader for quality across the Wilton Factory. This role is a key leadership position within the Quality organization, responsible for establishing quality direction, strengthening factory-wide quality governance, owning the Wilton Factory Quality Management System, ensuring audit readiness, and driving sustained improvement in product quality, process capability, defect prevention, and measurable factory quality outcomes.
This leader will ensure that quality is understood, owned, and executed as a factory-wide priority, translating business, customer, supplier, and process performance signals into prioritized actions that improve quality performance and strengthen the Wilton Factory quality culture.
Role and Responsibilities
This is a critical leadership role within the Wilton Factory, responsible for enterprise-level quality leadership, factory quality governance, Quality Management System ownership, audit readiness, and end-to-end alignment of quality priorities across the Wilton value stream.
Wilton Factory Quality Leadership
Serve as the organizational quality leader for Wilton Factory, setting direction, priorities, governance, and expectations for quality performance across factory operations.
Lead, develop, coach, and performance-manage a team of direct reports, setting clear expectations, fostering strong engagement, building capability, and ensuring individual and team performance supports Wilton Factory quality priorities.
Lead the development and execution of the Wilton Factory quality strategy, ensuring alignment with business priorities, customer expectations, global quality standards, and operational performance goals.
Own the Wilton Factory Quality Management System, ensuring it is effective, current, compliant, and embedded into daily operations, standards, controls, and leadership routines.
Ensure Wilton Factory maintains strong audit readiness for internal, customer, regulatory, and certification-related audits, including effective preparation, response, corrective action, and sustainment.
Translate quality performance signals, customer feedback, supplier input, factory data, and risk indicators into clear priorities, improvement roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
Establish and monitor measurable factory quality outcomes such as defect reduction, escape reduction, first-pass yield improvement, repeat issue prevention, audit finding closure, process capability improvement, and corrective action effectiveness.
Partner closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, Supplier Quality, Customer Support, and global Quality to ensure alignment on containment, root cause, corrective action, prevention, and sustainment.
Provide regular executive-level reporting on factory quality performance, systemic risks, improvement progress, audit readiness, QMS health, and strategic quality priorities.
Factory Quality Governance & Cross-Functional Alignment
Establish and sustain effective quality governance across Wilton Factory, ensuring quality priorities are visible, owned, and actively managed across functions.
Collaborate with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supplier Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Support, and Operational Excellence to address systemic quality gaps impacting factory performance.
Ensure effective quality handoffs, learning loops, and corrective action sustainment between suppliers, Wilton operations, downstream factories, and customer-facing organizations.
Strengthen factory participation in global quality forums, cross-sector quality initiatives, and enterprise-level improvement routines.
Quality Management System & Audit Readiness
Own and continuously improve the Wilton Factory Quality Management System, ensuring quality requirements, procedures, controls, records, and governance routines are clear, effective, and consistently followed.
Lead audit readiness for Wilton Factory by establishing preparation routines, internal assessment practices, leadership review mechanisms, and corrective action governance.
Ensure audit findings, nonconformities, and systemic gaps are addressed through timely root cause analysis, robust corrective action, effectiveness checks, and sustained prevention.
Use QMS performance, audit trends, nonconformance data, and corrective action effectiveness to identify systemic risks and strengthen factory quality controls.
Quality Strategy, Six Sigma & Data-Driven Improvement
Own and deploy quality improvement strategy and Six Sigma methodology within the Wilton Factory to address chronic quality issues, defect drivers, escapes, audit findings, and process instability.
Identify and prioritize high-impact improvement opportunities using factory performance data, customer signals, supplier inputs, process capability data, QMS performance, audit trends, and risk-based thinking.
Define measurable outcomes for key quality initiatives, including expected improvements in defects, escapes, repeat issues, process capability, corrective action effectiveness, yield, cost of poor quality, and audit performance.
Mentor and coach teams on DMAIC, root cause analysis, quality planning, and sustainment practices.
Ensure that lessons learned from quality events and improvement projects are institutionalized across the factory and embedded into standards, controls, QMS documentation, and daily management routines.
Statistical Process Control (SPC)
Provide strategic leadership for SPC deployment, maturity, and effectiveness within Wilton manufacturing.
Ensure SPC is used consistently to monitor process capability, detect variation, and prevent defects before impacting customers.
Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, and global SPC competence teams to align on standards, tooling, and best practices.
Drive regular KPI deep dives and ensure action plans are in place and executed.
Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving
Lead cross-functional problem-solving efforts for complex factory, supplier, and customer quality issues.
Promote and coach structured problem-solving approaches such as 8D, A3, Lean Six Sigma, and other ASML standard methodologies.
Influence behaviors and culture to reinforce quality ownership, accountability, defect prevention, and customer focus across all levels of the factory.
Up to 10% travel annually within the US and internationally
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s Degree required (Master’s preferred) in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Optical, Quality, Mechatronics or a related scientific and/or technical field
10+ years of progressive experience in quality engineering, manufacturing or operational excellence in a high-tech manufacturing environment
5+ years of experience in a leadership role managing direct reports and leading quality priorities across cross-functional teams
Demonstrated experience leading factory-wide or organization-wide quality strategy, governance, Quality Management System ownership, audit readiness, and improvement initiatives across organizational boundaries
Strong background in Statistical Process Control, Six Sigma, quality systems, audit management, and structured problem solving
Proven experience defining, tracking, and improving measurable quality outcomes such as defect reduction, escape prevention, process capability, audit performance, corrective action effectiveness, and repeat issue prevention
Proven ability to influence without authority and lead cross-functional, cross-site improvement efforts
Six Sigma Black Belt strongly preferred; ASQ CQE or CMQ/OE a plus
Fluent in English with strong written and verbal communication skills
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you will always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way do that. You will not work in a silo. Instead, you will be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you will collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You will have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you will need the following skills:
Strong quality leadership mindset with the ability to set direction, align stakeholders, and represent factory quality priorities across the organization
Demonstrated people-leadership capability in team engagement, performance management, talent development, and coaching, with the ability to build accountability, strengthen capability, and support employee growth.
Data-driven, analytical thinker with the ability to translate quality performance insights into action and measurable factory outcomes
Strong working knowledge of Quality Management Systems, audit readiness, audit response, corrective action governance, and effectiveness verification
Influential leader capable of driving alignment across functions, sites, and leadership levels
Results-oriented with a strong sense of ownership, accountability, and urgency for quality outcomes
Effective communicator at both technical and executive levels
Skilled in facilitating complex problem-solving, governance routines, audit preparation routines, and cross-functional decision-making
Able to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution
Proactive, resilient, and comfortable challenging the status quo when needed
Other Information
This position is located on-site in Wilton, Connecticut. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation

The Quick Response Team (QRT) Factory & Field Integration (FFI) is part of the Manufacturing Process Support organization within the TWINSCAN Factory. As a QRT FFI 5-Shift Engineer, you provide first-line troubleshooting support for Factory and Field Integration activities and play a key role in securing factory progress and machine availability. You report to the QRT FFI Group Lead or Team Lead of your assigned team.
In this role, you are expected to solve technical issues independently during your shift, through troubleshooting and problem analysis. You can design and provide action plans for others within execution to solve these issues (e.g. damages, failing tests, progress and performance issues). You have a crucial role in enhancing the solving power of the execution teams through coaching and guidance.
You function as a 1st line support organization of execution engineers. Using your skills and knowledge to assess technical complexity of issue, to suggest the correct way forward in close collaboration with the 2 shift QRT Team engineers.
During unsupported shifts in the night you focus on securing progress both for factory and field.
You are expected to support delicate or complex hardware actions, in order to decrease hard down time during supported and particularly unsupported shifts. You keep learning and developing your knowledge and (hands-on) skills by collaborating closely with the QRT 2 Shift and joining other organizations (e.g. Technical Support/Module Production). You share the acquired knowledge and skills with your colleagues, to strengthen the overall competence of the QRT FFI 5-shift team.

In addition to troubleshooting and technical decision-making, you play an important role in coaching colleagues, sharing knowledge, and continuously strengthening the technical capability of the QRT FFI organization.

Introduction to the job
As recruitment marketing manager, you will help ASML attract and convert relevant talent into high-quality applicants by improving how we present roles, campaigns and candidate journeys to the market. You will translate talent priorities, audience insights and ASML’s employer positioning into clear recruitment marketing frameworks, communication objectives, and activation practices that support better hiring outcomes.
In this role, you will strengthen the connection between attraction, sourcing, selection and candidate experience. Your work will help teams create realistic job previews, targeted vacancy campaigns, effective job advertisements and data-driven channel improvements that make it easier for candidates to understand the opportunity and decide whether to apply.

You will be part of the Attract, Select & Onboard Center of Expertise within Talent Acquisition. This center provides global expertise, frameworks and improvement practices that strengthen the quality, consistency and impact of ASML’s hiring approach across regions, sectors and talent domains.
As recruitment marketing manager, you will focus on improving recruitment-facing activation: the recruitment marketing approach through which ASML engages relevant audiences and moves identified talent from consideration into application. You will work closely with Talent Marketing and Sourcing, Corporate Communications, regional Talent Acquisition teams, HR stakeholders and business stakeholders to ensure recruitment marketing materials are aligned, credible and locally usable.

Define and improve recruitment marketing frameworks, campaign requirements, communication objectives and recruitment content needs for agreed talent priorities.
Govern recruitment marketing practices by enabling consistent use of agreed frameworks, campaign approaches, briefing requirements recruitment messaging and activation toolkits.
Use quality-of-hire insights, persona input, candidate journey insights and funnel data to improve job advertisements, realistic job previews and candidate-facing messaging.

Partner with Talent Marketing and Sourcing, Corporate Communications, HR teams, Talent Acquisition teams and business stakeholders to align recruitment-facing activation with ASML’s employer positioning.
Introduce improved recruitment marketing practices, identify opportunities for improved content formats, personalization approaches and automation opportunities that strengthen recruitment outcomes.

You bring solid experience in recruitment marketing, employer brand activation, campaign strategy, content strategy or recruitment communications, preferably in a global technology environment. Advanced knowledge of existing Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) actors and/or other stealthy threat actors.
Experience in conducting risk, threat and vulnerability assessments, force protection planning and threat modelling, solid experience in intelligence community analytical methodologies, standards and software tools.
Excellent knowledge of best practices in security management principles, advanced knowledge of (strategic and tactical) intelligence-led operations, espionage vectors, social engineering and infiltration.

Team player and leadership skills.
Able to give direction and good at planning & prioritizing.
Creative when handling problems independently, commitment and flexibility.

Counterintelligence (CI) and/or HUMINT Intelligence operations leadership experience is preferred.

Introduction
The Product Communications team within ASML’s Communications sector helps explain some of the world’s most advanced technology in a clear and engaging way. As an intern, you will help translate complex scientific and engineering topics into content that informs and inspires different audiences. You will work with communication professionals, content creators, engineers, and technology experts to bring technical stories to life. This internship offers hands-on experience in science communication within a leading deep-tech company. If you enjoy making complex ideas easy to understand, this Internship could be the right opportunity for you.
Your assignment
During this internship, you will contribute to ongoing content projects while leading your own internship project from concept to publication. You will learn how communication supports technology and innovation in an international organization. Working closely with experienced colleagues, you will help create content that connects technical expertise with audiences ranging from engineers and students to the general public. Your main responsibilities will be:
Create engaging social media content about ASML technology and innovation.
Research complex technical topics and translate them into clear, accessible stories.
Develop content concepts for articles, short-form videos, animations, and digital campaigns.
Collaborate with subject-matter experts to validate technical accuracy and context.
Identify interesting stories behind technologies, engineering challenges, and people.
Monitor content performance and recommend improvements based on audience insights.
Contribute fresh ideas and formats that support ASML’s content strategy.
We ask that you submit a writing sample together with your CV so we can better understand your writing style and communication skills. If you used AI tools during the writing or editing process, please indicate this clearly.
This internship primarily focuses on practical work experience. However, there is also the possibility to combine the assignment with thesis research when relevant.
This is a bachelor’s or master’s thesis internship for minimum 5 months, minimum 5 days per week (Hybrid). The start date of this internship is as of February 2027.
Your profile
To be suitable for the internship, you:
Are currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree in communication science, applied communication science, journalism, science communication, or a related field.
Can share a writing sample (preferably science/tech-focused) along with your CV.
Have excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
Are curious, analytical, and able to explain complex topics in a simple and engaging way.
Are collaborative and comfortable working with technical experts and different stakeholders.
Are proactive, detail-oriented, and open to receiving feedback.
The following experience is considered an advantage:
Affinity with physics, engineering, semiconductors, or other applied sciences.
Experience creating written content for social media, newsletters, blogs, magazines, or student publications.

You are enrolled at an educational institute for the entire duration of the internship, and you are at least 18 years old at the start of the internship;

As a Security risk expert - AI & emerging technology, you are responsible for executing security risk assessments and providing specialist security expertise for Artificial Intelligence (AI), Generative AI, Agentic AI, machine learning solutions, and other emerging technologies.
You will perform detailed security analysis, identify risks, evaluate controls, and develop practical recommendations to support informed risk-based decisions.
Role and responsibilities
As a Security risk expert - AI & emerging technology, you will operate as a senior individual contributor under the direction and prioritization of the Security risk manager.
In this function, you will join the first-line Corporate Sector Security Risk Management department. You will be part of the ASML Security community and work closely with sector Security Risk Management (SRM) teams, central security competence teams, AI and data governance, Information Technology, Privacy, Legal & Compliance, Internal Audit and business stakeholders.
In this role, you will:
Execute security risk assessments for AI and emerging technology initiatives, identifying threats, vulnerabilities, control gaps, and risk scenarios, and developing evidence-based findings and recommendations
Perform detailed analysis of proposed technologies and architectures, including threat modelling, attack-path analysis, and evaluation of security controls and mitigations
Assess AI-specific risks, including model compromise, prompt injection, data leakage, training data risks, supply chain vulnerabilities, agentic behaviour risks, and access control weaknesses
Support security-by-design reviews throughout the technology lifecycle, provide subject matter expertise to project teams, advise stakeholders on security-by-design principles, and support solution design reviews
Assist teams in understanding security expectations and requirements, validate implementation of agreed security controls, and review remediation activities and compensating measures
Support exception management, risk treatment planning, and risk acceptance discussions, providing technical security expertise and recommendations
Contribute to the improvement of assessment methodologies, security standards, control frameworks, procedures, and reporting mechanisms, share knowledge and mentor less experienced practitioners, and escalate material risks, novel technologies, risk appetite concerns, regulatory concerns, and significant disagreements or unresolved issues to the Security Risk Manager
Education and experience
Bachelor's or master's degree in a relevant discipline, e.g., business administration, information technology, cybersecurity, internal audit, IT management and/or data science & AI.
3-7 years professional experience with a focus on security, IT auditing, Information Security Management Systems (ISMS). AI specialization required
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM or CRISC.
Experience with defining and running AI security baselines, assessments
Proven track record in Security at tactical level
Deep Knowledge of current security technologies, current and future developments for AI security, in-depth working knowledge of IT, Data and Information Risk/security frameworks and best practices, such as NIST Cyber security framework, ISF Standard of Good Practice for Information Security, IEC 62443, NIST SP 800 30 framework, NIS2 , ISO 27001/2 framework

Excellent influencing and interpersonal skills

Introduction
ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our main headquarters are located in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we also have 18 office locations around the United States- including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.
Role and Responsibilities
The Senior Accountant is part of the ABS Financial Operations organization and plays a key role in supporting U.S. accounting operations, financial reporting, internal controls, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Other responsibilities will include:
Perform and coordinate general accounting activities for U.S. entities in accordance with U.S. GAAP and company accounting policies. Execute month-end close activities, including preparing journal entries, completing account reconciliations, performing financial reviews, and executing other assigned close procedures within established deadlines.
Manage assigned U.S. government reporting requirements. Prepare, analyze, and validate consolidated financial information and submit required reports accurately and on time to applicable U.S. government agencies, including the U.S. Census Bureau.
Evaluate lease arrangements under ASC 842, including reviewing agreements for lease identification, classification, and measurement. Maintain complete and accurate lease records in the company’s lease accounting system and support related monthly accounting processes.
Support fixed asset accounting and reporting activities in accordance with company policies and U.S. GAAP. Partner with business stakeholders to address ad hoc requests, resolve accounting and process issues, and drive improvements across end-to-end fixed asset processes.
Review check deposits, determine the appropriate accounting treatment and application, communicate coding instructions, and research unidentified or incorrectly applied receipts through resolution.
Prepare and post journal-entry uploads for American Express travel and expense transactions. Validate the completeness and accuracy of the underlying data and maintain appropriate supporting documentation.
Execute assigned SOX controls in accordance with documented control procedures and established deadlines. Prepare and retain complete supporting documentation, investigate exceptions, and escalate control issues when appropriate.
Perform monthly fluctuation and variance analyses for assigned general ledger accounts. Research significant or unexpected movements and clearly communicate the underlying business and financial drivers to relevant stakeholders.
Prepare and maintain balance sheet account reconciliations. Investigate reconciling items and drive the timely resolution and clearing of open items.
Prepare and post journal entries in accordance with U.S. GAAP and company policies. Ensure journal entries are accurate, properly approved, and supported by complete and auditable documentation.
Identify and implement process improvements using Lean principles. Support finance transformation, ERP, automation, and other cross-functional initiatives that improve accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and internal controls.
Support internal and external audits by preparing accurate and timely documentation, responding to auditor inquiries, and coordinating follow-up items with process owners and other stakeholders.

Experience in public accounting or within the finance organization of a large multinational company required.
Experience with month-end close, journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, financial analysis, and applying U.S. GAAP required.
CPA licensure, active CPA candidacy, or a master’s degree in Accounting or Finance preferred.
Experience using artificial intelligence tools and developing effective prompts is a plus.
Experience with SAP preferred; experience across multiple ERP environments is a plus.
Experience working in a global organization and collaborating with international stakeholders preferred.

Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.
Strong working knowledge of U.S. GAAP and general accounting principles.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to research accounting matters, apply professional judgment, and develop and communicate well-supported conclusions.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and complete assignments accurately within established deadlines.
Ability to evaluate end-to-end processes and identify opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and control effectiveness.
Ability to research complex transactions, investigate account variances, and drive issues through resolution.
Strong attention to detail, with a focus on the accuracy, completeness, and quality of financial information and supporting documentation.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate cross-functionally with U.S. and international stakeholders.
Effective verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate accounting matters to finance and non-finance stakeholders.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and the ability to learn and work effect

As a Business Planner, you set the plan for materials supplied by external parties and internal factories, enabling our supply chain to deliver, while balancing availability and inventory in line with business objectives. You are the orchestrator of the ASML supply chain, ensuring material availability for our factories and our customers. You understand and clarify demand dynamics towards your supplying parties, supporting your counterparts to meet the ASML growth path.

- Optimizing planning parameters

Collaborating closely with demand planning departments, supplier-facing departments, product lifecycle management and production planning to reach agreement on the supply plan and D&S gap closure actions

The Plasma Controls Department is responsible for the development and engineering of the metrology, automation and control loops for the EUV light source system. The complexity of the EUV source puts exciting and challenging demands on the Plasma Control Engineers who will be engaged in all phases of the control system development and integration involving sophisticated control algorithms, real-time embedded software, high speed electronics, precision sensors, and all working under extremely challenging dynamic conditions to produce stable EUV light.
Role and responsibilities
As a Senior Controls/Automation Engineer you will:
Serve as a technical expert for one or more control/optimization/calibration subsystems, capable of independent decision making for critical technical issues.
Perform feasibility studies, support the development of product roadmaps, advise on future product definition and system specifications.
Monitor integrity of system architecture during development, ensure the availability of Test Specifications, and coordinate or execute the testing process and design verification.
Coordinate or execute the testing process and design verification in lab test bench and cleanroom fabrication environment
Coordinate the specification of system functionalities, and design the system architecture based whilst ensuring commonality between products and subsystems across all programs, support program definition, co-ordinate decomposition and specification of sub systems, and support the review process and approval of designs in co-operation with applicable Product- and Project- Management.
Define, plan, manage and coordinate assigned (portfolio of) projects and ensure execution and delivery, within the project management guidelines.
Ensure and support optimal communication of specifications to all relevant parties to improve the decision processes, and prepare the introduction of approved new projects by defining all technical specifications on system level for Development & Engineering.
Leads and mentors junior controls engineers, leads the development and integration of innovative control system solutions to enable stable and efficient production of EUV.
Organize, coordinate, optimize, lead, coach, develop and appraise employees within the person's expertise / team.
Applies broad knowledge in sensors, actuators, control algorithms, automation, software, and data analysis tools to drive control system improvements to enable continuously increased EUV power and system availability.
Leads and performs integration activates including trouble shooting the control system, designing and executing test plans, to ensure the system functions as designed in the EUV light source. Such activities can take place in lab test bench and manufacturing cleanroom at various ASML sites.
Documents work results with system requirements, design specifications, procedures, and training materials.
Willingness to work in a dynamic customer focused environment.

Generates requirements and design specifications for automation logic and implementation.
Mentors more junior level algorithm engineers through technical guidance and assistance.
Investigates the feasibility of applying scientific and mathematical control design principles and concepts to potential inventions and products.
Plans and executes laboratory research pertaining to algorithm design and validation in lab test bench and/or cleanroom

Ability to carry a product design from conception into production.
Experience designing and implementing practical feedback control or optimization systems of significant complexity
Knowledge of modern control theory, optimization, stochastics, and some nonlinear control theory

Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Working at the intersection of customer technology strategy, business development, and product management, the CTM builds trusted relationships with customer stakeholders, identifies future challenges and opportunities, and drives adoption of ASML innovations. The role acts as the primary bridge between the customer and ASML's Business Lines, ensuring that customer requirements are understood, prioritized, and translated into compelling solutions.
The Senior CTM influences both customer technology decisions and ASML product development by aligning stakeholders around a common vision and creating business cases that accelerate technology adoption and customer value creation.
