Introduction to the job
ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that enable the world’s leading chipmakers to manufacture faster, more powerful, and more energy-efficient microchips. Headquartered in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, ASML has major U.S. locations in Chandler, Arizona; San Jose and San Diego, California; Wilton, Connecticut; and Hillsboro, Oregon.
As a Senior Electronics Connectivity Design Engineer, you will lead the design, integration, and validation of reliable electronic connectivity solutions for ASML’s EUV source and lithography systems.
You will drive electrical architecture decisions across PCBAs, cabling, interconnects, racks, and subsystem interfaces, ensuring compliance with requirements for EMC, signal integrity, safety, reliability, manufacturability, and serviceability.
You will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to define requirements, evaluate trade-offs, guide implementation, and support suppliers and development partners throughout the product lifecycle.
As a subject matter expert in connectivity, you will contribute to technology roadmaps and promote best practices for high-reliability electronics in advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
Role and responsibilities
Lead the development of a submodule's electrical connectivity architectures, including PCBAs, cables, harnesses, racks, cabinets and subsystem interconnects.
Participate in the definition of module specifications and maintain electronic hardware requirements, interface definitions and validation plans.
Maintain Cable Overview (CO) and Detailed Wiring (DW) diagrams owned by the department.
Design, review and qualify PCBAs for control, monitoring and communication applications.
Select appropriate hardware components and architectures to implement required functionality within complex, high-precision systems with multiple interdependencies.
Drive EMC/EMI compliance activities throughout the product development lifecycle, including design reviews, mitigation strategies and qualification testing.
Define design rules and layout constraints for signal integrity, grounding, shielding, high-speed interfaces and EMC performance.
Support schematic capture, component selection, design verification and root-cause analysis activities.
Lead troubleshooting and failure analysis at board, module and system levels.
Collaborate with system architects, software engineers, mechanical engineers, manufacturing engineers and suppliers to deliver robust electronic solutions.
Review supplier designs and provide technical guidance on electrical design, EMC performance and qualification readiness.
Contribute to technology roadmaps and support the adoption of best design practices, including state-of-the-art hardware architecture and design methods.
Mentor junior engineers and provide technical guidance to project teams.
Transfer technical knowledge to manufacturing, service and support organizations.
Communicate technical risks, trade-offs and mitigation proposals to stakeholders.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Job description is subject to change at any time.
Education and experience
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field.
Minimum of 10 years of industry experience in electronic hardware development.
Minimum of 5 years of experience designing PCBAs and electronic modules for industrial, semiconductor, aerospace, medical, automotive or similarly demanding applications.
Demonstrated experience developing electrical connectivity solutions, including cables, harnesses, racks, enclosures and interconnect systems.
Demonstrated experience with PCBA design, schematic capture, component selection and design validation.
Hands-on experience with EMC/EMI design techniques, test methodologies and applicable regulatory standards.
Experience supporting EMC qualification activities, including emissions and immunity testing.
Experience defining grounding, shielding, filtering and signal-integrity strategies for complex electronic systems.
Experience working in multidisciplinary product-development teams.
Experience troubleshooting at board, module and system levels.
Experience using laboratory equipment, including oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers and communication bus analyzers.
Experience using schematic capture and hardware design tools; experience with Capital, XPedition, Altium Designer or similar platforms is preferred.
Familiarity with high-speed digital interfaces, including Ethernet, SPI, I2C, UART, RS-232, RS-422, RS-485, PCIe or similar technologies.
Understanding of reliability engineering concepts, including MTBF, HALT, ALT and DFMEA.
Experience with configuration management and engineering change-control processes.
Familiarity with supplier collaboration and outsourced development models.
Knowledge of semiconductor equipment, industrial automation, motion control or precision mechatronic systems is preferred.
Skills
Strong knowledge of connectivity, EMC, grounding, shielding and electrical integration principles.
Solid fundamentals in analog and digital electronics.
Hands-on knowledge of EMC certification and compliance testing to IEC, EN, CISPR, FCC, CE or equivalent standards.
Knowledge of high-speed digital PCB design, signal-integrity analysis and interface constraints.
Ability to define grounding, shielding, filtering and EMC mitigation strategies for complex electronic systems.
Ability to create clear technical specifications, design documents, validation plans and engineering reports.
Structured problem-solving skills for root-cause analysis, troubleshooting and failure analysis.
Knowledge of functional safety principles, electronics safety requirements and high-reliability hardware qualification.
Understanding of semiconductor capital equipment, complex mechatronic systems or regulated hardware environments.
Ability to communicate technical risks, trade-offs and mitigation proposals clearly to engineering stakeholders.

The position requires highly motivated, extremely organized, and self-driven individuals.
Based in Wilton, Connecticut, this role gives you the opportunity to solve challenging engineering problems while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams across product development, manufacturing, and suppliers. As a Senior Electrical Engineer, you will take full technical ownership and lead multiple complex designs end-to-end, with a broader view of system impacts and cross-functional dependencies. Contribute to sub-module development and change, oversee functional relationships across domains, and drive solutions through significant technical uncertainty.

Introduction to the Job
ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography systems that enable the world’s leading chipmakers to manufacture faster, more powerful, and more energy-efficient microchips.
As a Senior Electronics Design Engineer – PCBA Design, you will design, develop, integrate, and qualify complex Printed Circuit Board Assemblies used in ASML’s electronic control systems. You will define board-level architectures, develop schematics, guide component selection, support layout activities, and ensure robust operation in demanding semiconductor manufacturing environments.
You will work closely with system architects, FPGA designers, embedded software engineers, EMC specialists, mechanical engineers, manufacturing teams, and suppliers to deliver high-reliability electronic hardware for current and future platform needs.
Role and responsibilities
Design and develop complex active PCBAs for electronic control systems.
Define board-level architectures for FPGA, processor, memory, communication, and sensor-interface functions.
Develop and maintain schematics using ASML-approved design tools and methodologies.
Select and qualify components to meet functionality, reliability, lifecycle, EMC, and manufacturability requirements.
Translate system and module requirements into board-level requirements, interface definitions, and implementation plans.
Define electrical constraints for signal integrity, power integrity, EMC, grounding, shielding, and thermal performance.
Support PCB layout reviews and guide placement, routing, stack-up, and high-speed implementation decisions.
Perform board bring-up, verification, debugging, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis.
Support EOL redesign, PFAS replacement, and component-obsolescence mitigation activities.
Collaborate with suppliers, contract manufacturers, and internal teams through design, prototype, qualification, and release phases for production.
Participate in design reviews, risk assessments, DFMEA activities, and technical decision-making.
Resolve field, manufacturing, and qualification issues related to board-level design performance.
Contribute to hardware roadmaps and next-generation platform development.
Mentor junior engineers and promote robust PCBA design practices.
Education and experience
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
Minimum of 10 years of industry experience in electronic hardware development.
Minimum of 7 years of experience designing complex active PCBAs for industrial, semiconductor, aerospace, medical, automotive, or similarly demanding applications.
Demonstrated experience with FPGA, processor, memory, and high-speed communication interfaces.
Experience with board-level architecture definition, schematic capture, component selection, and design verification.
Demonstrated experience using LTspice or comparable SPICE-based simulation tools to analyze and validate analog, mixed-signal, and power-electronics circuits.
Validating simulations of high speed board design and verifying quality in the lab using iBert and other eye pattern test tools required.
Experience supporting PCB layout activities and resolving board-level implementation issues.
Proven track record for successful SoC power distribution, clocking and high speed board design a must.
Experience with board bring-up, debugging, troubleshooting, and failure analysis.
Experience with component lifecycle management, EOL redesign, and obsolescence mitigation.
Experience working with contract manufacturers, board fabrication suppliers, and outsourced development partners.
Experience working in multidisciplinary product-development teams.
Skills
Strong hands-on experience in analog and digital board design, validation, and troubleshooting.
Strong knowledge of FPGA-based and processor-based board architectures for high-reliability electronic systems.

Introduction of the job
As an FPGA Design and Verification Engineer, you will specify, design, develop, realize, integrate, and test modules and tools in a multi-disciplined team, collaborating closely with cross-functional partners and suppliers. You will deliver within system specifications, cost targets, and project schedules, ensuring timely realization of solutions that contribute to competitive, achievable, and serviceable products. The FPGA Firmware Engineer provides discipline specific expertise throughout the entire product life cycle. This Includes concept feasibility, new product introduction, existing product sustainment and customer facing problem resolution. The position requires highly motivated, extremely organized, and self-driven individuals.
The FPGA Design and Verification Engineer will be responsible for definition, design, verification, and documentation for Field Programmable Gate Arrays. They will provide RTL design, simulation, physical implementation and verification of complex FPGA modules comprising a mix of custom RTL with hard and soft vendor IP cores within a larger architecture.
Design:
Determine architecture and detailed system design approach for the FPGA
Define module interfaces and all aspects of device design coordinated with the Printed Circuit Board Designers
Evaluate the process flow including but not limited to high level design, synthesis, place and route, timing constraints and power utilization
Support the generation of technical engineering products by using the appropriate standards, processes, procedures, and tools throughout the FPGA development life cycle
Independently determine approach to solutions and get alignment from System Engineers and Printed Circuit Board developers
Contribute to design and development of FPGA hardware for control, communications systems and digital signal processing (DSP) platforms.
Technical Writing: Define and Document Specifications and Design Decisions
Test, Verification & Integration:
Develop and Implement the Product Validation and Verification (V&V) Strategy for FPGA
Determine system verification approach for the FPGA, ensuring proper test coverage
Develop, implement and supervise design verification test plans at system level.
Design, Develop and Build Product Specific Test Tooling
Includes: Simulation, Emulation, and Hardware Test Tools.
Test Validation and Verification (V&V) of Product Requirements
Plan and Execute Component Level Testing & Sub-module Integration
Plan and Execute Module Level and System Level Integration
Bridge the gap between Electrical Systems and System Software
Technical Writing: Define and Document Test Procedures, and Test Reports
Role and Responsibilities
In this role, you will contribute to engineering deliverables that scale with job grade, from executing defined tasks and supporting senior engineers to owning complex technical scope, coordinating cross-functional work, and leading program-level outcomes.
Identify, analyze, document, and manage requirements with traceability, and coordinate verification criteria to confirm deliverables meet intent.
Conduct research and feasibility studies, document findings, and translate results into recommendations, tradeoffs, and decision inputs.
Develop engineering concepts and solutions, make technical choices, and resolve issues to meet functionality, performance, cost, and compliance needs.
Define and communicate specifications and high-level designs, align interfaces, and support reviews and approvals to enable quality execution.
Support system or product integration by coordinating dependencies, applying configuration management, and enabling smooth project execution.
Define and execute validation and test approaches, improve methods and procedures, and ensure qualification evidence supports release readiness.
Estimate effort, plan and track work, manage risks and dependencies, and deliver assigned work packages or projects to agreed quality and timelines.
Maintain accurate technical documentation, share knowledge through coaching and mentoring as applicable, and follow EHS policies while identifying and mitigating safety risks.
Education & experience
Bachelor degree in Electrical Engineering required. MS or PhD preferred.
Minimum of 4 years of relevant work experience required.
Skills
Technical & functional skills
Requirements, Interfaces & Technical Specification Management: Ability to identify, analyze, document, and manage requirements with traceability, translate them into clear specifications, and align interfaces so engineering deliverables meet intent and enable reliable downstream design, integration, and verification
Engineering Solution Development (Electrical): Ability to develop engineering concepts and solutions, make sound technical tradeoffs, resolve issues, and realize designs that meet functionality, performance, cost, compliance, and schedule constraints within system/module specifications.
Preferred Skills in Embedded Logic and Firmware Design and Verification includes:
Highly proficient use and understanding of FPGA engineering concepts, principles, and theories
Highly proficient in FPGA design languages and tools including VHDL and UVM or OSVVM (Altera High Level Synthesis is preferred)
Experience with FPGA development software - (Modelsim, Quartus, Mentor CDC is preferred)
Highly proficient in Microsoft Office applications
Experience with FPGA SoC, including Avalon and AXI architectures
Experience with architecting and implementing embedded processors including NIOS
Proficient in implementing IP blocks based on interface requirements and designing the required interface logic to overall FPGA architecture
Expertise using VHDL for implementation and verification of FPGA designs
Basic knowledge of signal algorithms
Preferred knowledge and experience using design software and technical tools includes:
VHDL, System Verilog, UVM
Questa Sim, Modelsim, Quartus
GIT, JIRA
MATLAB and SimuLink
Electronic Laboratory Equipment
LabVIEW
Python
Integration, Verification & Validation (V&V) Execution: Ability to plan and execute verification and validation, ensure qualification evidence supports release readiness, and support system/product integration by coordinating dependencies and applying disciplined configuration/traceability to deliver working, testable solutions.
Behavioral & leadership skills
Drives Results: The ability to translate strategic and technical goals into clear priorities, execution plans, and measurable outcomes, delivering committed results on time and with the right quality by taking ownership, managing trade-offs, removing obstacles, and sustaining momentum across stakeholders and dependencies.
Demonstrates Self-awareness: The ability to understand and manage one’s own strengths, limitations, emotions, and impact on others; to actively seek and use feedback; and to adapt behaviors and decisions to improve collaboration, leadership effectiveness, and results, especially in high-pressure, ambiguous, or complex environments.
Values Differences: The ability to intentionally seek, respect, and integrate diverse perspectives and working styles to strengthen collaboration and decision quality, ensuring all voices are heard and treated equitably, and enabling inclusive execution across cross-functional and multicultural stakeholders.
Builds Effective Teams: Helps align and enable the team dynamic by clarifying shared goals, roles, dependencies, and ways of working. Fosters trust and inclusion by promoting open dialogue, healthy conflict resolution, inclusion, and mutual accountability. Coaches colleagues to strengthen individual and team capability.

Introduction to the job
In the departments of the "Supporting Functions" you may not come into direct contact with our products, but with your expertise you contribute significantly to the smooth functioning of our company. Only with colleagues from these structured, efficient and supportive departments, such as Human Resources, Accounting, Controlling, IT and Communications, is it possible for us to grow beyond ourselves and achieve our goals as a company.
As a Senior General Ledger Accountant, you will play a key role within our Finance organization. You will ensure the quality and integrity of our financial reporting, work closely with internal and external stakeholders, and actively contribute to the continuous improvement of financial processes and systems.
Role and responsibilities
As a Senior General Ledger Accountant, you will:
ensure the preparation and quality assurance of financial reporting as well as monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with statutory, tax, and corporate requirements.
take ownership of compliance with accounting standards and serve as a subject matter expert for accounting and reporting matters.
act as the primary interface for external auditors, tax advisors, regulatory authorities, and internal stakeholders in connection with audits, statutory reporting, and regulatory requirements.
monitor accounting processes, internal controls, and compliance requirements while driving their continuous enhancement.
support financial transparency through analyses, balance sheet reconciliations, cash flow forecasting, and meaningful management reporting.
serve as a key user for financial systems and reporting tools, ensuring their stability and continuous development.
identify optimization opportunities and implement initiatives related to digitalization, process improvements, and efficiency enhancements within Finance.
Your qualifications
You hold a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a comparable qualification.
You have several years of professional experience in accounting, financial reporting, and financial statement preparation within a mid-sized or international business environment.
You possess strong knowledge of German GAAP (HGB), IFRS, and ideally US GAAP, as well as a solid understanding of tax and regulatory requirements.
You have experience collaborating with external auditors, tax advisors, and other external stakeholders.
You have hands-on experience with SAP FI/CO and standard Microsoft Office applications.
You communicate confidently in English and have good written and spoken German skills.
Your Competencies
Working in an international finance environment requires a high level of accuracy, collaboration, and continuous improvement. The following competencies are essential for success in this role:
You take ownership of complex topics, work in a structured manner, and remain focused even under demanding deadlines.
You analyze issues thoroughly, think in a solution-oriented way, and derive pragmatic and sustainable decisions from financial data.
You collaborate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders and communicate confidently across different levels of the organization.
You identify opportunities for improvement and proactively drive change and optimization initiatives.
You combine high-quality standards with a hands-on mindset and are equally effective working independently and as part of a team.
Other Information

Diversity and Inclusion

Our policy is to recruit, hire, train, and promote individuals in all positions regardless of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. Dein Arbeitsumfeld
Im Sektor der „Supporting Functions“ kommst du vielleicht nicht direkt mit unseren Produkten in Kontakt, aber mit deinem Fachwissen trägst du maßgeblich dazu bei, dass unser Unternehmen reibungslos funktioniert. Nur mit den Kollegen und Kolleginnen aus diesen strukturierten, leistungsbereiten und unterstützenden Abteilungen wie dem Personal, der Buchhaltung, dem Controlling, der IT und der Kommunikation, ist es uns möglich über uns hinaus zu wachsen und unsere Ziele als Unternehmen zu erreichen.
Als Senior Bilanzbuchhalter:in übernimmst du eine Schlüsselrolle in unserer Finanzorganisation. Du stellst die Qualität unserer Finanzberichterstattung sicher, arbeitest eng mit internen und externen Stakeholdern zusammen und gestaltest die Weiterentwicklung von Prozessen und Systemen aktiv mit.

Als Senior Bilanzbuchhalter:in wirst du:
die Erstellung und Qualitätssicherung der Finanzberichterstattung sowie der Monats-, Quartals- und Jahresabschlüsse gemäß gesetzlichen, steuerlichen und konzerninternen Vorgaben sicherstellen.
die Einhaltung von Rechnungslegungsstandards verantworten und als fachliche Ansprechperson für Bilanzierungs- und Reporting-Themen fungieren.
als zentrale Schnittstelle zu Wirtschaftsprüfer:innen, Steuerberater:innen, Behörden sowie internen Stakeholdern bei Audits, Jahresabschlussprüfungen und regulatorischen Fragestellungen agieren.
Rechnungslegungsprozesse, interne Kontrollen und Compliance-Anforderungen überwachen sowie deren kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung sicherstellen.
die finanzielle Transparenz durch Analysen, Bilanzabstimmungen, Cashflow-Prognosen und aussagekräftige Management-Reportings unterstützen.

Introduction to the job
ASML is relentlessly driving the semiconductor industry’s ongoing quest for producing faster, smarter and more energy efficient chips. We are a young, dynamic, international and highly skilled workforce creating, with strong support of our suppliers, the lithographic tools the industry needs to achieve its goals.
Are you looking for a challenge to ensure the ultimate photonic solutions in our scanners and metrology instruments? Then you will enjoy this position in the Optics and Photonics group at ASML research. You will be part of the group responsible for demonstrating how new or existing technological solutions can be adapted to meet and exceed the needs of our metrology and lithographic tools.
Role and responsibilities
As research architect in the Optics and Photonics group you will be responsible for developing cutting edge photonic solutions and demonstrating their applicability to our industrial context. You will work in a fast paced and multi-disciplinary environment. Your responsibility is to take ownership of the experimental and theoretical work with the rest of the team and drive feasibility studies towards clear conclusions. This includes definition of the architecture, design, specification, development, documentation of photonic solutions as well as communication of the results towards various stakeholders. Using your technical knowledge, analytical thinking and people skills, you will work closely together with the team and other researchers at ASML.
You will join a project team whose mission is to focus on the development of photonic solutions for both our lithographic as well as our metrology tools. The job consists of:
Translate optical sensing concepts into photonic solutions in an industrial context
Define the requirements, architecture and technology development needs for the photonic solutions and contribute to the photonics technology roadmap
Identify concepts and address technology maturity
Design and specification of photonic integrated circuits
Definition of experiments for evaluation of these PICs
Work together with other researchers towards better understanding of the technologies
Generate new ideas and solutions for current and future photonic solutions
Build a network towards other parts of the organization and academia
Education and experience
PhD in Electrical engineering, Physics or Applied Physics with 4+ years of experience in the field of integrated photonics.
Experience in identifying system-level needs and technology development needs for the photonic solution concepts
Experience in developing photonic integrated circuits: design and specification.
Experience in designing photonic components using numerical methods such as FDTD, EME, and FEM and optics modeling software (e.g. Lumerical).
Experience with experimental evaluation of PICs
Experience with manufacturing of PICs and interacting with foundries.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Ability to translate optical sensing concepts into innovative technical solutions for photonics
Ability to think on a functional level and in design details
Good communicational skills
Ability to switch between complex matters and high-level conclusions, ability to convey these in an understandable fashion
Team player with ability to build network towards other parts of the ASML organization and academia

Flexible, committed, result driven with the ability to plan and prioritize.
Strong analytical skills and drive for quality.

We work in small, diverse, and multidisciplinary teams of approximately 5 to 15 persons and deliver a proof of concepts or fundamental understanding that can be valorized and transferred within the company. We intensively work together with external research institutes and universities. Senior Laser & Optics Design Engineer
In a nutshell
Location
San Diego, CA, US
Team

We are a part of ASML, located in beautiful San Diego. ASML provides chipmakers like Intel, Samsung, TSMC, Global Foundries and others with everything they need - hardware, software and services - to mass produce patterns on silicon, helping to increase the value and lower the cost of a semiconductor chip. Our key technology is the lithography system, which brings together high-tech hardware and advanced software to control the chip manufacturing process down to the picometer. Our vision is a world in which semiconductor technology is everywhere and helps to tackle society’s toughest challenges.
Job Mission
We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Laser & Optics Design Engineer to join our Source Research team. The mission of this role is to translate emerging laser and optical concepts into engineered, testable systems that advance next-generation high-power Laser Produced Plasma Extreme Ultraviolet (LPP-EUV) light sources and DUV lasers. Working within a dynamic Source Research environment, the engineer will define and execute the detailed engineering work needed to mature new technologies within the project goals and high-level technical direction established with the lead scientist, despite high-level and evolving requirements. This role combines optical and laser system design, modeling, hands-on experimentation, integration, and validation to demonstrate system performance and prepare successful concepts for future product development.
Role and Responsibilities
Execute the detailed design, integration, and validation of laser and optical systems, including optical architectures, laser subsystems, diagnostics, controls, and supporting hardware.
Work as part of a multidisciplinary project team, partnering with laser scientists, system architects, mechanical engineers, software engineers, electrical engineers, and product development teams to deliver program objectives.
Develop and utilize system models and engineering analyses including optical, thermal, gain, gas-flow, structural, and performance models to guide design decisions, predict system behavior, and reduce technical risk.
Translate high-level and evolving system needs into implementable subsystem requirements, designs, interfaces, and verification criteria, maintaining appropriate bi-directional traceability within Source Research as the design matures.
Working within the project goals and high-level technical direction established with the lead scientist, own the detailed engineering execution of assigned work packages, including developing the implementation approach, identifying required tasks, conducting design reviews, planning tests, managing technical risks, resolving issues, documenting results, and delivering against schedule and performance targets.
Design, build, and commission experimental hardware and prototype systems to evaluate new concepts, mature technologies, and support future product development.
Define and execute verification and validation activities to demonstrate compliance with performance, reliability, manufacturability, and safety requirements.
Drive design improvements through data-driven engineering, analyzing test results and system performance to identify root causes, improve robustness, and increase system capability.
Support technology transfer from research into development, ensuring designs are scalable, maintainable, manufacturable, and aligned with long-term product roadmaps.
Demonstrate system-level performance against future technology roadmap objectives through analytical predictions, laboratory testing, and integrated system demonstrations.
Perform other duties as assigned or required.
Education and Experience
Ph.D. with a minimum of 3+ years of experience or a Master’s degree with at least 6+ years relevant experience in laser physics, optics, photonics, electrical engineering, or an equivalent field.
Strong foundation in laser and optical system design, integration, alignment, characterization, and troubleshooting.
Ability to translate high-level, incomplete, and evolving system requirements into practical subsystem designs, interfaces, specifications, and verification plans.
Firm understanding of optical modeling, particularly Gaussian beam propagation, resonator behavior, and beam delivery; proficiency with Zemax OpticStudio is preferred. Ability to apply optical and multidisciplinary engineering analyses—including thermal, structural, gain, gas-flow, and performance models—to guide design decisions and reduce technical risk.
Hands-on capability to design, build, commission, and validate experimental hardware and prototype laser and optical systems.
Strong experimental design, data analysis, and root-cause problem-solving skills, with the ability to convert test results into actionable design improvements.
Ability to plan and execute technical work packages, including design reviews, test planning, risk management, issue resolution, documentation, and delivery against schedule and performance targets.
Working knowledge of design for reliability, manufacturability, maintainability, scalability, and safe operation.
Working knowledge of optomechanical design principles, including tolerancing, alignment stability, mounting, and sensitivity to thermal and mechanical disturbances.
Working knowledge of laser safety practices and disciplined laboratory execution involving high-power laser systems.
Skills
This role requires a hands-on engineer who can translate scientific concepts and system requirements into reliable, testable laser and optical hardware. Success depends on sound engineering judgment, rigorous analysis, disciplined execution, and effective collaboration across multidisciplinary teams.
To thrive in this role, you will need the following skills:
Ability to thrive in a rapidly changing research and development environment where requirements may evolve, priorities may shift, and formal processes may be limited.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate across scientific, engineering, and product teams and to effectively influence implementation and design decisions without direct authority.
Clear and concise written, verbal, and graphical communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical information to varied audiences.
High integrity, ownership, and initiative, with the judgment to independently identify what needs to be done, establish structure and priorities, and drive work forward without waiting for detailed direction.
Relevant experience developing, integrating, testing, or troubleshooting laser and optical systems in a research, prototype, or product-development environment.
Demonstrated experience driving the detailed execution of complex engineering work from high-level and evolving technical direction, including independently defining the tasks, priorities, analyses, experiments, and documentation needed to achieve the intended outcome.
Experience applying optical modeling and engineering analysis to the design and evaluation of laser or beam-delivery systems.
Experience using experimental results and system-performance data to diagnose issues, validate designs, and implement improvements.
Experience working within multidisciplinary research and engineering teams to mature concepts from initial feasibility through integrated demonstration.
Other information

Introduction to the Job
ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers—the world’s leading chipmakers—to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States, including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA, and San Diego, CA.
You must be work authorized in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship
Role and Responsibilities
The Senior Manufacturing Engineer is a senior individual contributor responsible for the manufacturing readiness and technical performance of assigned prototype test rigs, products, modules, or manufacturing domains. The role connects product development with hands-on factory execution by planning and supporting prototype builds, integration, testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement. Working across design, systems, test, quality, manufacturing, planning, and project teams, the engineer converts prototype learning into safer, more repeatable, scalable, and cost-effective manufacturing solutions. The role leads through technical expertise and influence and does not have formal people-management authority.
Prototype Test-Rig Engineering and Factory Readiness
Plan and support prototype test-rig build, integration, test, commissioning, troubleshooting, modification, and decommissioning activities.
Assess execution readiness for procedures, tooling, test methods, technical information, resources, and approvals.
Establish safe, executable assembly, integration, and test sequences for new or evolving hardware and systems.
Coordinate tooling, equipment, material, documentation, facility, safety, hardware, software, and engineering dependencies.
Capture test-rig learning and apply it to product designs, procedures, sequences, tooling, test methods, manufacturability, and future factory readiness.
Manufacturing Process and Technical Ownership
Own assigned manufacturing processes or technical domains and provide readiness leadership across dependent factory activities.
Develop and improve manufacturing methods, procedures, tooling, equipment, test methods, and process controls.
Evaluate and qualify manufacturing changes, including engineering changes and approved departures from standard requirements.
Analyze yield, quality, cycle time, capacity, reliability, safety, and cost performance to identify improvements.
Lead complex problem definition, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and recurrence prevention.
Cross-Functional Product and Module Engagement
Serve as the Manufacturing Engineering focal point for an assigned cross-functional product or module leadership team, referred to internally as an MDU.
Convert stakeholder objectives, constraints, and decisions into clear Manufacturing Engineering actions and ownership.
Prepare decision-ready technical recommendations supported by evidence, factory impact, implementation risks, and required decisions.
Communicate risks, decisions, commitments, and changes to affected teams and confirm follow-through.
Planning and Execution Coordination
Translate ambiguous objectives into executable plans with clear scope, deliverables, owners, milestones, dependencies, and success criteria.
Coordinate interdependent technical work across engineering contributors and assigned manufacturing domains.
Identify technical, resource, schedule, and readiness risks and coordinate mitigation with responsible owners.
Escalate unresolved decisions with the impact, options considered, and a recommended path forward.
Coaching and Capability Development
Coach engineers in technical problem solving, execution planning, stakeholder preparation, and follow-through.
Prepare engineers to represent their assigned technical domains with product, module, and cross-functional stakeholders.
Review technical plans, risk assessments, presentations, and recommendations before key decisions.
Build distributed ownership of critical knowledge, responsibilities, and stakeholder relationships.
Continuous Improvement and Knowledge Transfer
Convert prototype and factory lessons into sustainable improvements to products, processes, tooling, test methods, and training.
Standardize effective manufacturing methods, planning practices, procedures, and technical documentation.
Improve handoffs among the engineering function supporting prototype test-rig build, integration, test, commissioning, troubleshooting, and learning capture; the engineering function supporting repeatable integration and test execution across systems, modules, and factory operations; and related manufacturing teams.
Share technical knowledge across engineers, technicians, and cross-functional stakeholders.
This senior individual-contributor role leads assigned technical work and stakeholder interfaces through expertise, planning, coaching, and influence. The role is accountable for ensuring work is clearly scoped, appropriately owned, integrated, and communicated.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline; an advanced degree or equivalent experience is preferred.
Minimum of five years of relevant experience in complex manufacturing, prototype, new-product introduction, integration, test, industrialization, or a closely related engineering environment.
Experience with complex high-technology systems, such as electromechanical, mechatronic, vacuum, fluid, laser, or controls systems.
Experience supporting prototype test-rig build, integration, commissioning, troubleshooting, qualification, or manufacturing readiness.
Experience developing manufacturing processes and applying structured problem-solving methods.
Experience leading root-cause analysis, corrective action, and recurrence prevention.
Experience providing cross-functional technical leadership without formal reporting authority.
Experience with technical planning, risk management, stakeholder communication, manufacturing documentation, bills of material, engineering changes, procedures, or product industrialization.
Familiarity with statistical analysis, design of experiments, process capability, Lean methods, data visualization, and relevant planning or analytical software is preferred.
Skills
Apply sound technical judgment in ambiguous prototype and evolving factory environments.
Maintain a strong manufacturing and factory focus across safety, quality, delivery, cost, manufacturability, and execution.
Assess end-to-end system impacts across products, modules, test rigs, processes, and factory operations.
Influence cross-functional teams and build alignment without formal authority.
Communicate complex technical information clearly to engineers, technicians, stakeholders, and senior management.
Structure work through clear scope, priorities, ownership, dependencies, risks, and decisions.
Coach others and transfer technical knowledge to strengthen team capability.
Demonstrate ownership, attention to detail, adaptability, and reliable follow-through.
Other Information

Develop, implement, and optimize manufacturing processes for ASML products.

Introduction to the Job
ASML San Diego is a global leader in semiconductor technology, developing advanced lithography systems that enable the world's leading chipmakers. This role is the senior technical authority for machine safety, equipment safety, and occupational safety across San Diego and Korea Factory (KF) operations. The position provides expert guidance on hazard identification, risk assessment, safeguarding strategies, equipment compliance, and application of safety standards throughout the equipment lifecycle.
Working with minimum supervision, the Manufacturing Senior Equipment Safety Engineer sets the technical standard that other safety engineers work to, serves as the escalation point for the most complex safety and compliance challenges, and mentors and develops junior safety staff. They collaborate with stakeholders to proactively identify and mitigate risk, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and ensures compliance to all applicable regulatory and corporate standards while building the capability of the team around them.
Roles and Responsibilities
Technical Leadership and Mentorship
· Serve as the senior technical safety authority for the San Diego and KF safety engineering team.
· Coach, mentor, and develop junior and mid-level safety engineers, including formal on-the-job training, technical review of their work, and growth planning.
· Establish the technical standard for risk assessments, compliance documents, and inspections that the broader team executes against.
· May represent the safety function in front of regulators, NRTLs, corporate EHS, auditors, and customers as a senior technical expert.

· Lead process safety audits and equipment and tooling inspections.
Equipment and Product Safety

· Partner with manufacturing, test, and lab owners to close gaps identified against those expectations.

· Champion a proactive, solution-oriented safety culture across sites.
· Develop and deliver toolbox talks, safety communications, and training on equipment and tooling safety, and equip junior engineers to deliver the same.

Introduction of the job
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Founded in 1984, ASML is the world’s leading provider of lithography systems for the semiconductor industry, manufacturing complex machines that are critical to the production of integrated circuits or microchips. The mission of the Mechanical Development department is to design and develop the complex mechanics for these machines, which are some of the highest precision products ever produced in the world. This position is based on-site in Wilton, CT, which has both R&D and manufacturing operations. We design and produce multiple sub-system modules that are shipped to our headquarters in Veldhoven, The Netherlands where they are integrated into the full lithography machine.
As a Mechanical Engineer in Wilton, you will specify, design, develop, realize, integrate, and test modules and tools in close collaboration with cross-functional partners and suppliers. You will collaborate with system architects and senior engineers in a multidiscipline project team to develop concepts, perform engineering analysis, build and test prototypes, generate detailed CAD designs and create engineering drawings to deliver within system specifications, cost targets, and project schedules, ensuring timely realization of solutions that contribute to competitive, achievable, and serviceable products.
You take the lead in developing complex parts of modules and deliver technically complex solutions with full ownership, considering industrialization and cross-team impacts. Introduction to the role
Within ASML, the Corporate Intellectual Property (CIP) department is responsible for maximizing ASML’s global IP position to protect and support ASML’s business. In particular, the CIP department strives to preserve freedom to operate for ASML, to establish and maintain a portfolio of IP rights, and to mitigate IP risk. The CIP department includes about 85 members distributed across four worldwide locations (Veldhoven in the Netherlands; and Wilton, San Diego, and San Jose in the USA).

The CIP department is seeking a qualified U.S. patent attorney to be based in San Diego, CA USA. You’ll be a member of the San Diego IP team reporting to the local IP line manager and providing services to a corps of scientists, engineers, and management that is driving ASML’s EUV and Cymer’s DUV light source research and development.
You’ll help to establish, prosecute, and maintain a worldwide patent portfolio in the field of light sources for lithography systems, and to evaluate and mitigate patent risks from a worldwide perspective. This role is responsible for process development, stabilization, and daily performance across automated and manual mechanical inspection operations. The position requires a deep technical understanding of optical fabrication, strong analytical capability, and the ability to drive sustainable improvements in a fast-paced production environment.
The engineer will directly support output, yield, and quality targets—including improving First Pass Yield (FPY) through stable, predictable, and well controlled process behavior.
This role requires a proactive engineering mindset: anticipating issues before they impact production, driving structured 6P readiness, performing thorough RCA, and continuously evaluating new technologies to strengthen long-term process control. This is not a reactive support role; the expectation is ownership, foresight, and continuous improvement.
Job Description
The Senior Process Engineer will operate as a technical leader within Wilton Factory Optics with end-to-end ownership of visual inspection processes. Responsibilities include defining and optimizing process parameters, ensuring measurement stability, selecting tooling, and understanding machine behavior. The engineer will manage mechanical inspection performance, inspection control strategies, and inspection output quality while ensuring consistent results across tools, people, and shifts.
The mechanical inspection scope includes control of tooling, environment, fixturing, and other factors influencing inspection output. The PE will lead the introduction and qualification of new fixtures, tools, software, manual processes, and machine upgrades, and will convert mechanical inspection data into actionable decisions.
A key responsibility is establishing strong process control: defining process windows, capability targets, and long-term monitoring systems. The PE will use JMP or Minitab to identify variation, drift, and chronic stability risks, ensuring processes are robust, documented, and repeatable. This includes maintaining process specifications, work instructions, and standard work while driving alignment across production and support teams.
The engineer will collaborate daily with production technicians, supervisors, cross factory teams, quality, equipment engineering, and maintenance, balancing immediate production needs with structured long-term improvement projects.
The Senior PE is expected to:
• Build process stability that prevents rework and FPY loss
• Detect and eliminate sources of variation impacting FPY and yield
• Lead structured RCA using statistical and analytical methods
• Ensure corrective actions are verified, embedded, and sustainable
• Own full 6P readiness for process, material, or equipment changes
Beyond daily support, the engineer is expected to proactively seek, evaluate, and integrate:
• Inspection process control methods
• Advanced inspection tools
• Next generation inspection technologies
• Equipment or software capabilities that improve stability, predictability, and throughput

• Proficiency with manual and automated mechanical inspection tools
• Experience using JMP, Minitab, or equivalent statistical software

postings.description:
Senior Scientist - EUV Research
In a nutshell
Location
San Diego, CA, US

ASML US, LP brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.
Job Mission
We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Scientist – EUV Research to join a dynamic and innovative Technology Development team, focused on conceiving and demonstrating the technologies required for next generations of high-power extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light sources. Based on a laser produced plasma (LPP), our light source relies on a wide range of unique and challenging technologies, ranging from laser light amplification and high-power optical systems to laser produced plasma for EUV generation, electro-optical signal detection and algorithm-based actuation for process control. You are invited to bring your passion, knowledge and expertise in areas of applied physics, plasmas, metrology, optics, controls, lasers, and experiment design to push the boundaries of these technologies forward.
A key ingredient in the EUV generation process is a stable source of molten tin droplets. These droplets provide the fuel for the laser-produced plasma and serve as the heart-beat for synchronizing the EUV source. The challenge is to reliably produce nearly perfect droplets of molten tin at a rate of tens of thousands of times per second with speeds of 10’s of m/s and position stability within a fraction of a droplet diameter. If these dimensions were scaled up to the game of golf, this would be equivalent to continuously scoring hole-in-ones in a hole that’s 25 km away in swirling gas flows and a plasma that’s hotter than the surface of the sun. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating in this diverse mix of physics, materials science and engineering, in order to define the droplet generator architecture for next generations of the EUV source. The successful candidate will also have a passion for innovation, be driven by curiosity, and have deep technical understanding, in order to excel in a Research environment operating at the fuzzy front end of product development. A key ingredient for success in this space is the ability to transform a complicated multi-physics environment into a sequence of more easily digestible phenomena. The successful candidate will be given the opportunity to carry forward the innovations all the way from feasibility studies to hardware development and implementation by bridging the gap between modelling and experiments. The successful candidate will work in a team environment and will also get the opportunity to lead small x-competence team members towards the completion of planned research goals.
Duties and Responsibilities
Guide development of high-level architecture used for the generation of droplets in the EUV source.
Lead the design of droplet generation hardware and build the needed metrology + testing capabilities to demonstrate the droplet performance up to 1000’s of Kbar.
Provide input to technology roadmaps and identify key scientific learning objectives and define corresponding experimental design to arrive at design guidelines, performance requirements and procedures to product teams.
Identification of key scientific learning objectives and corresponding experimental design which will further the technological progress of the EUV generation process
Develop and execute system and subsystem performance tests, analyze test results and extract actionable knowledge from sub-module to full-system levels.
Troubleshoot issues with droplet generation, tin delivery, and optical systems in order to improve droplet performance at the bench and source level.
Build, improve and maintain droplet generator models anchored via experimental validation; build and maintain model improvement roadmaps; prioritize model improvement activities.
Document learning and communicate knowledge to engineering and product development teams to guide product improvement and release of new product nodes.
Work independently and in teams to deliver on a stated objective, whether it be the pursuit of new knowledge, the demonstration of a new capability, or the characterization of existing performance.
Perform other duties as assigned or required.
Education and Experience
PhD or MS degree with a minimum of 3+ years of relevant experience in Materials engineering, Mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, material science, physics, optics, or equivalent field.
Experience with glass, ceramics, refractory materials, high pressure sealing technology in corrosive environments is highly desired.
Hands-on experience with complex, preferably high pressure, system design and build, including rapid prototyping, characterization and troubleshooting via breadth of metrology techniques, and system-level demonstrations.
Deep understanding of scientific research methods and strong scientific curiosity, with demonstrated knowledge in metrology development and data analysis.
Experience with microfluidics, liquid jet breakup and droplet coalescence in particular; piezoelectricity; and acoustics is highly desired; familiarity with modeling one or more of these processes is also desired.
Experience with high pressure applications such as water jet cutting, jet breakup, and nozzle design is a plus.
Experience architecting high-level model structure into digestible components with crisp interfaces is desired; experience coordinating multiple components of a model is a Plus; experience implementing physics concepts into models is also a plus.
Experience with droplet formation, sprays, common-rail diesel, and/or injectors is a plus.
Experience with acoustics designs is also a plus: resonant cavities in the kHz/MHz regime; transfer function design for enhancing/suppressing energy transfer into liquids; piezo-driven system design.
Extensive experience with experimental data analysis and development of data analysis tools with, for instance, Matlab or Python and data acquisition systems such as NI Labview.
The successful candidate will not only have excelled in their technical field, but will have demonstrated inter-personal and communications strengths.
Ability to clearly and logically communicate ideas and knowledge to various audiences.
Demonstrated ability to manage and lead a research project involving multiple stakeholders and constraints.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a part of a team and lead investigation and research efforts.
Other information
PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT

Introduction to the job
Are you motivated by solving complex software and computer-related problems on advanced e-beam machines? Do you enjoy applying solid computer science fundamentals to diagnose real-world machine issues, improve system reliability, and support critical products used by customers worldwide?
We are looking for a Software Engineer with a strong foundation in computer science and hands-on software engineering skills to join the Diagnostics Tooling group. In this role, you will help diagnose, investigate, and resolve software and computer-related issues observed on customer e-beam machines, while designing and developing software tools that improve troubleshooting efficiency, automate diagnostics workflows, and strengthen our overall machine diagnostics capability.
You will work closely with equipment specialists, architects, product owners, and stakeholders across multiple domains to analyze complex problems, identify root causes, and deliver reliable, maintainable software improvements.
Role and responsibilities
As a Software Engineer in DnE, you will act as a software expert for software and computer-related diagnostics on e-beam machines. You will analyze issues reported by Field from customer sites, provide technical feedback and troubleshooting guidance, and develop software tools and test applications that improve diagnostics efficiency and support internal module validation.
Your responsibilities include:
Acting as a DnE software expert for software and computer-related issues reported by Field from customer e-beam machines
Analyzing Field feedback, diagnosing symptoms, identifying possible root causes, and providing practical troubleshooting recommendations
Developing software tools to reduce the effort and complexity for Field engineers when investigating software, computer, and machine-related problems at customer sites
Building diagnostics and automation tools for log collection, system health checks, issue reproduction, data analysis, and root cause investigation on e-beam machines
Supporting the development of internal DnE module test software, including software for module communication, test execution, result analysis, and validation workflows
Contributing to software solutions involving module communication interfaces, image processing workflows, and image algorithm validation where applicable
Working closely with Field, equipment specialists, architects, and software teams to translate technical problems into maintainable software solutions
Writing clean, maintainable, and well-tested code for diagnostic tools, test utilities, backend components, and integration software
Continuously improving diagnostics workflows, tool usability, and knowledge transfer between DnE and Field teams
Collaborating effectively across DnE, Field, application, and equipment domains to drive customer-impacting issues toward resolution
Education and experience
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation, or equivalent
At least 5 years of professional software development experience, preferably in equipment, diagnostics, automation, test software, or engineering tool development

Introduction to the job
As a Supplier Quality Engineer within Strategic Sourcing & Procurement, you will lead supplier part industrialization in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary development environment, supporting Development & Engineering projects from early supplier involvement through readiness for volume production.
You will combine hands-on technical expertise with leadership of complex industrialization projects and supplier improvement activities. Working closely with suppliers and ASML development teams, you will translate product requirements into robust manufacturing processes, resolve capability gaps, and secure part quality and timely delivery in alignment with the ASML project plan.
Role and responsibilities
Within Strategic Sourcing & Procurement, the SQE owns industrialization status and manufacturing readiness for assigned parts. You will independently lead complex supplier quality and industrialization activities, challenge supplier readiness, and drive decisions with Engineering, Supplier Account Teams (SAT), and Quality Supplier Managers (QSM). You will remain directly involved in technical assessments and problem solving while guiding stakeholders toward agreed project outcomes.
The main responsibilities are:
Lead SQE activities and deliverables within assigned projects, coordinating contributions from other SQEs and cross-functional stakeholders. Establish priorities, milestones, and action owners, and drive timely closure of issues affecting NPI deliverables.
Lead supplier part industrialization through new product introduction (NPI) and ramp-up. Assess supplier NPI readiness with the SAT and contribute technical and manufacturing input to supplier selection.
Drive early supplier involvement in development projects. Incorporate supplier manufacturing and prototype feedback into design decisions to address manufacturability risks before qualification and volume release.
Define and align the part Statement of Work (SoW) with Engineering, the SAT, and suppliers, covering development and volume manufacturing requirements, deliverables, and responsibilities.
Ensure part quality, manufacturability, and serviceability requirements are addressed during design, including critical-to-quality (CTQ) requirements, design risk assessments, and lessons learned.
Own and drive part qualification and manufacturing readiness deliverables in the ASML product generation process, including:
Supplier acceptance of specifications and designs, with clear manufacturing requirements
Complete part and process qualification plans, including risk mitigation and capability validation
Acceptance of qualified parts and documented industrialization status, with open issues resolved or assigned to agreed owners for the SQE-QSM transfer
Manufacturing process flows, process failure mode and effects analysis (PFMEA), CTQs, and control plans
First article inspection, test coverage, measurement system analysis, and process capability evidence
Drive resolution of NPI manufacturing and quality issues, including deviation approvals, containment, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions. Maintain configuration and change management interfaces, monitor part quality disturbances with QSM, and verify that actions prevent recurrence.
Assess supplier manufacturing processes and identify capability gaps affecting quality, technology, delivery, or cost. Drive part-related improvement plans with suppliers and SAT stakeholders, coach suppliers on process control and quality maturity, and escalate unresolved risks with clear recommendations.
The SQE is part of cross-functional development project teams and interfaces with project leaders, design engineers, architects, manufacturing and customer support engineers, logistics, procurement, and suppliers.
Education and experience
Bachelor or Master’s degree in industrial engineering, optics, mechatronics, electronics or related field.
Minimum 10 years of relevant experience with a Bachelor's degree or 7 years with a Master's degree, including demonstrated ownership of complex technical or supplier industrialization activities.
Demonstrated hands-on leadership experience in at least one of the following: technical project management, supplier management, or people management. Candidates must show how they set direction, coordinated work, resolved technical or stakeholder issues, and delivered measurable outcomes while remaining directly involved in execution.
Experience in high-tech industry and complex modules, with a focus on industrial engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing engineering, or technical project management. Experience applying quality systems and methods and developing production processes is required. Six Sigma Green or Black Belt certification is preferred.
Experience with multiple NPI projects, including completion of at least one full product development cycle, and direct technical interaction with suppliers in an industrial environment.
Industry experience in either coating technologies (e.g. ALD coatings), 3D printing (3DP), mechatronics, or similar technical field
Skills
The ideal candidate demonstrates a combination of technical, manufacturing, and supplier quality competencies, including:
Strong understanding of New Product Introduction (NPI), product industrialization, and Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP).
Proficiency in Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA/PFMEA), Control Plans, and process flow development.
Experience with First Article Inspection (FAI), Measurement System Analysis (MSA), Statistical Process Control (SPC), and capability analysis (Cp/Cpk).
Working knowledge of root cause analysis and structured problem-solving methodologies such as 8D, A3, DMAIC, 5-Why, and Ishikawa.
Ability to assess manufacturing processes and process capability across precision machining, sheet metal fabrication, optics, coatings, mechatronics, electronics, or assembly technologies.
Experience with supplier visits, process assessments, and driving corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
Understanding of configuration management, engineering change control, and product lifecycle management processes.
Ability to interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, technical specifications, and critical-to-quality (CTQ) requirements.
Ability to identify, assess, and reduce manufacturing and quality risks, and independently drive qualification planning for complex components and assemblies.
Experience analyzing technical data using statistical methods and quality tools to drive process improvements.
Experience with Production Part Approval Process (PPAP), and qualification methodologies.
Familiarity with semiconductor, optics, precision mechanics, mechatronics, or other complex high-tech products is a strong plus.
The following personal skills are also crucial for a successful execution:
Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects, supplier improvement activities, or teams and drive results without formal authority.
Strong stakeholder management and negotiation skills, including alignment of Engineering, suppliers, and SAT stakeholders on priorities and action ownership.
Clear communication of technical risks, project status, and recommendations to engineering teams, supplier management, and ASML leadership.
Ability to translate complex technical data into clear decisions, challenge readiness assumptions, and escalate risks at the right time.
Independent judgment, initiative, and accountability for agreed deliverables.
Flexible, result driven and committed.
Collaborative leader who coaches colleagues and suppliers and builds trust across functions.
Process oriented.
Fluent in English.

ASML US, LP brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.
Job Mission
We have an exciting opportunity for a Source Research Project Lead to join our dynamic and innovative Technology Development team, focused on conceiving and demonstrating the technologies required for next generations of high-power extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and Deep ultraviolet (DUV) light sources. Both light sources rely on a wide range of unique and challenging technologies, ranging from laser light amplification and high-power optical systems to laser produced laser for EUV generation, electro-optical signal detection and algorithm-based actuation for process control. You are invited to bring your passion, knowledge and expertise in areas of applied physics, plasmas, metrology, optics, controls, lasers, and experiment design to push the boundaries of these technologies forward.
In this role, you will help to advance the light source technology for next generation products. You will be invited to join the research team responsible for pathfinding and innovating the heart of the EUV source, the drive laser, to enable the performance of the next generation light source products. As a project lead you will organize the team’s tasks in alignment with the teams “3 in a box”, the group lead and architect. Your project team will conceive and evaluate technical concepts and design, and develop experimentation to test the validity of such hypothesis. You will plan and manage resources for such ideation and experimental validation up to full scale architecture performance demonstrations. Furthermore, you will drive innovation to scale light source power and stability by collaborating closely with the Controls and Software team, as well as laser scientists. Finally, you will foster cross-functional teamwork connecting with the droplet generator and tin management research teams towards a holistic light source development vision.
Duties and Responsibilities
Responsible for project leadership of the light source research projects within the S-Next research program and other projects as assigned
Scope will include alignment of the roadmaps to the program planning, and project-level execution of the activities within the scope of these roadmaps as they support the program objectives
Generation and maintenance of the project plan, detailing all activities to be conducted within the assigned EUV research projects, including test planning, test execution, report generation, etc
Responsible for understanding of, contributing to the creation, and contextualizing of the execution of the Laser roadmap and portfolio
Ensures proper documentation is completed and reviewed for each activity within the project, and that adequate documentation exists for the product program and D&E (feasibility results, test procedures, drawings, BOMs). Facilitate the communication of appropriate knowledge to engineering and product development teams
Outward reporting towards senior management of the progress of the assigned research projects
Ensure the successful demonstration of system-wide performance targets to meet the future technology roadmap, as conducted by the project members
Enable technical project team to successfully identify key scientific learning objectives and corresponding experimental design which will further the technological progress of the EUV source
Proactively communicates issues and manages the solution paths. Assesses and highlights risks and develops mitigation plans
Supports the Program Manager (provides information, fill-in during absence, etc.) as required
Manage and align resources provided by cross-functional teams
Develop resource plans for experimental campaigns and project related work
Management of the triple constraint: timing, budget, and resourcing
Minimum Qualifications
BS or MS degree with 6+ years of relevant experience in physics, laser engineering, photonics or equivalent technical field
Successful demonstration of project management and leadership over the full life-cycle of a project, with corresponding successful completion and delivery of project objectives
Possess very strong skills acquired through advanced training, study and experience
Understanding of scientific research methods and strong curiosity
The successful candidate will not only have excelled in their technical field, but will have demonstrated inter-personal and communications strengths
Hands-on experience with complex system design and build, characterization, troubleshooting
Ability to clearly and logically communicate ideas and knowledge to various audiences
Demonstrated ability to manage and lead a research project involving multiple stakeholders and constraints
Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a part of a team and lead investigation and research efforts
Other information
PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee routinely is required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch
The employee is occasionally required to move around the campus including working while fully gowned in a clean room environment
The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds
The employee may be required to travel based on business needs
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus
The environment generally is moderate in temperature and noise level
Extended periods of time in a clean room environment should be expected
Requires gowning in Class 10K gowning protocol
May need to work in labs with equipment that emit high-pitched noise
May spend extended periods of time at a computer workstation
