Job description summary
Responsible for day-to-day management of a technical project and to run this within the triple constraints described in the project plan. Responsible for the project supply chain deliverables, from project plan to final delivery, to realize its deliverables that will support the business case of the overall program.
Introduction to the job
As a Supply Chain and Sourcing manager within the ASML Strategic Sourcing and Procurement sector (SS&P), you will make a real difference by driving the end-to-end introduction and industrialization of ASML’s products from a Logistics, Cost, and Quality point-of-view, following ASML’s Product Generation Process (PGP). To achieve this, you will be using your unique mix of technical, creative, and people skills to lead and coordinate natural teams both at ASML and at suppliers.
Role and responsibilities (Final)
Define, secure and monitor the supply chain and sourcing NPI and industrialization deliverables in the Product Generation Process (PGP) to successfully deliver volume-worthy products, including alignment on the SS&P sector’s KD decisions and driving D&E (Development&Engineering) deliverables.
Identify and manage supply chain risks, acting as the voice of the suppliers within product teams. Conduct assessments on material availability, including supplier move-rate capabilities and long-leadtime item.
Drive, monitor and report-out on Cost of Goods roadmap vs. target on Cluster in close collaboration with the SS&P clusters/commodities in Business Line and across SPFT’s/Supplier account teams.
Prepare yearly OPEX/CAPEX forecast and manage spend within budget for Supplier NRE (Non-recurring expenses) and tooling&packaging, including monitoring throughout the year.
Proactively solve QLTC (Quality, Logistics, Technology, Cost) in collaboration with internal (engineering and procurement/sourcing) and external stakeholders (suppliers) and organize periodic management reviews.
Collaborate closely with cross-functional team (engineering, factory, field, suppliers) representatives in product teams to ensure alignment and integration of KD deliverables, together with a team of PLM Product Coordinators. Mobile resources if needed to fulfill the plans.
Apply Early Supplier Involvement and Concurrent Engineering methodology to secure the required introduction timeline, including defining Complex Part List, and coordinating Make/Buy decisions and Supplier Selections w/the Supplier Account Teams.
Identify bottle necks, prepare decisions and take actions towards engineering, suppliers, factories as well as the field to manage the critical path of new parts for time-to-market and ramp up.
First point of contact for supply chain operations aspects and related issues in the cross-sector project cluster team and direct counterpart of the Module Delivery Unit (MDU)-lead.
Report pro-actively on project status to relevant senior stakeholders, ensuring transparency and timely updates, including activities, milestones and resources.
Represent SS&P in the AIR (ASML Issue Resolution) triage, managing AIR issues related to SS&P and End of Life/Supply.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives within SS&P function to enhance efficiency and effectiveness
By fulfilling these responsibilities, you will play a crucial role in the successful industrialization and introduction of ASML’s cutting-edge product, ensuring that they meet the highest standards of quality, cost efficiency and performance.
Education and experience
Technical or Supply Chain Bachelor's degree required. Master's degree preferred.
A minimum of 6 years' relevant work-experience in a NPI environment preferably in a high-tech industry
Proven track record in project management and leading multi-disciplinary teams
Proven track record to improve efficiency and effectivity in technical production environment
Experience in interfacing with suppliers on industrialization targets preferred
Experience in out-of-the-box creative problem solving
Experience in bottleneck management of manufacturing processes
Previous sourcing experience highly preferred
Skills
Highly organized, capable to drive complex issues to simple and pragmatic solutions;
Influencing without formal authority, sense for tactical and political relations on both strategic and operational level;
Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships on different levels in the organization
Able to show resilience in a high stress, high pressure environment (e.g. escalations)
Conceptual and analytical thinker
Pragmatic, hands on and result driven mindset
Strong communication skills (listening, asking the right questions, constructive challenging), able to get buy-in and commitment from relevant stakeholders
Excellent influencing skills, able to lead and coach team members
Project management skills, able to translate requirements into a Product Masterplan
Strong affinity with working in a technical environment
Good business judgement and ability to organize and manage multiple concurrent projects and priorities. Prioritize between key and side topics.
Ability to judge when support is necessary, and know how to involve the right stakeholders
Action oriented self-starter who can drive strategy and be hands-on as situations deem appropriate
Energized by fast paced environments
Strong analytical, structure and organizational skills
Stakeholder management: experience with dealing effectively with internal and external stakeholders both at operational and executive levels

postings.description:

In a nutshell

Introduction to the job
Help enable the technology behind the world's most advanced semiconductor machines. In this program, you'll learn how one of the world's most complex supply chains operates while developing the skills needed to make an impact within ASML. Working alongside experienced professionals, you'll gain hands-on experience, collaborate with diverse stakeholders, and tackle real business challenges that support our suppliers, customers, and operations. This program is the perfect combination of starting in a sourcing and supply chain related role and involvement in a two-year development program.
Role and responsibilities
By applying for the Sourcing and Supply Chain Graduate Acceleration Program, you will be considered for multiple positions, such as operational supplier coordinator, tactical buyer, project coordinator or central fulfillment management coordinator. During the recruitment process we will investigate together which role best aligns with your background and future ambitions. In the positions, you will:
Support operational or tactical activities within your assigned supply chain domain.
Collaborate with suppliers, customers, logistics partners, engineers, and/or internal stakeholders to solve business challenges.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that increase efficiency, quality, and reliability across the supply chain.
Develop expertise within a specific supply chain discipline while building a broad understanding of ASML's end-to-end operations.
Specialize in a specific field with no job rotations.
Participate in an intensive 2-year training and development program to accelerate your personal growth. The program consists of approximately 10 training days a year to develop your soft skills.
Receive guidance from a personal mentor from the company as well as a professional coach from an external company to define your personal learning goals and drive your personal development.
Education and experience
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in supply chain management, logistics, industrial engineering with a focus on supply chain management, or another closely related field.
You can have a maximum of six months of relevant work experience, excluding internships.
You will be fully graduated before starting your position at ASML.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Build strong relationships and communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders.
Thrive in a dynamic environment and manage competing priorities effectively.
Use data and critical thinking to solve problems and identify opportunities for improvement.
Take initiative, demonstrate ownership, and follow through on commitments.
Adapt quickly to changing circumstances and embrace new challenges.
Navigate complexity with confidence while balancing stakeholder and business needs.
Be fluent in English.
More information
We offer you
​A contract of one year at ASML, with the intention of an indefinite contract after the first year.
A highly competitive compensation and benefits package which includes: a competitive salary, 40 days paid leave, 13th month payment, 8% holiday allowance, pension plan, commuting allowance.
A two-year intensive development program focused on your personal and professional growth.
A safe environment to experiment with what you learn.
A close network of other early career employees and colleagues.

Video interview: If you are selected, you will be invited to record your answers to a few pre-determined questions.
Selection day: If you are chosen, you will be invited for the onsite selection day on November 19th, 2026.
Job offer: A few days after, we will let you know if you have been selected to receive a job offer.

Introduction to the job
In this role, you work for the Product Lifecycle Management department (within Strategic Sourcing & Procurement organization) as part of a cross-departmental R&D team. This means you’ll be balancing a broad range of stakeholders both from within your cross-functional project team and from the supply chain management department. You’ll be supporting technology-driven development projects by finding creative supply chain solutions that not only meet your stakeholders’ needs but also help bring the supply chain management department to the next level. Additionally, you will support the large-scale transfer of currently produced parts from across the globe towards Asia and be a valuable partner for the Transfer Team during the transfer phases. This includes supporting supplier readiness, ensuring logistical availability and quality assurance.
Role and responsibilities
The parts life cycle management department prides itself on its tight collaboration with other departments and teams across the company, and for securing material availability without fail. Specific responsibilities for this role include:
Creating an integrated project plan and maintaining key milestones; Incorporating logistics requirements into designs;
Ordering materials in order to ensure availability; Conducting logistics risk analyses; Securing and allocating financial resources for packaging and customer tooling
Proactively managing materials availability by making sure the bill of material (raw materials list) and technical product drawings required for a particular part are available on schedule;
Creating transparent parts supply and demand schedules;
Evaluating the consequences that proposed plan changes have on the supply chain
Creating, aligning, and monitoring implementation plans for engineering changes, while safeguarding the impact on material timing, cost and quality
Contributing to the further development of the product life cycle management department
Transfer Specific requirements
Support Transfer Projects following the agreed roles and responsibilities for specific transfer types – drive supplier readiness and timeline adherence through transfer team (SQE and LSM)
Own continuity of supply during reallocation — n-tier capacity checks, buffer and last-time buy strategies, and risk identification with mitigations.
Support and execute technical release procedures to ensure quality and prevent (hard)downs in the factory — first build/qualification milestones, Factory Integration Testing and release criteria following Transfer Methodology.
Manage escalations across suppliers/factories/engineering — resolve bottlenecks and prevent recurrence through collaboration with the SAT and Transfer Team to find root-causes of issues and solutions, sharing lessons learned.
Provide structured input for Transfer Team owned Cross-overplanning — tooling ownership, NRE, packaging/customer tooling budgets and D&S/buffer planning.
Education and experience
MSc in Industrial Engineering or Supply Chain / Logistics
Up to 7 years of experience in planning, logistics processes and quality in preferably high-tech, low-volume environment, and in ramping up new products
Project management related experience preferably in a high-tech, low volume environment (e.g. supply chain engineering; new product logistics)
Experience in driving process development and process improvements

Root cause analysis and proactively drive improvements for process / system
Ensuring accountability of deliverables of cross-sector stakeholders
Proficient planning and alignment skills
Stakeholder management - influence without authority; Persuasion and collaboration skills
Customer focus
Team player orientation
Able to manage ambiguity; Resilience
Learning agility to drive self development

People are our single most valuable asset. In product life cycle management, our management team works with our project coordinators to help develop both their hard and soft skills through dedicated training programs.
Working environment
You’ll be part of a team of 8–12 project coordinators, headed by a team lead, who will guide your personal development. The department’s other teams include one team of operationally-focused product life cycle management project leaders, and one team of strategically-focused supply chain management project leaders.
Meetings
Being ‘in the middle’ between R&D teams and supply chain management means you’ll spend a significant amount of time in meetings with various stakeholders. Examples include:
Development and engineering (R&D) project meetings;
Calls with suppliers to align on materials availability and planning;
‘Escalation’ meetings as part of a ‘tiger team’ managing urgent materials issues;
Alignment meetings to manage engineering changes related to introducing new materials in our supply chain, factories and customer locations.

Middle circle: R&D project managers, supplier quality engineers, manufacturing engineers, customer support engineers and supply coordinators.
Outer circle: configuration change specialists, sourcing leads, purchasers, logistics supply managers and field modification planners.

Quality Supplier Manager (QSM) is responsible for managing the quality and operational performance of strategic suppliers within the Supplier Account Team (SAT).
The role focuses on:
Driving suppliers toward a Zero Defects mindset
Ensuring material quality stability and availability
Leading process optimization and continuous improvement
Developing suppliers’ technical capability and maturity
Acts as a bridge between factory operations and supply chain ecosystem
QSM is expected to influence both operational execution and strategic direction of supplier quality.
Key Responsibilities
1. Supplier Quality Ownership
Own full scope of supplier quality and operational performance (Q, delivery, yield, reliability)
Serve as primary quality interface across internal teams and multi-tier suppliers
Ensure supplier adherence to quality systems, specifications, and agreements
Manage supplier performance using data-driven KPIs and governance model
2. Systemic Problem Solving & Escalation Leadership
Lead cross-functional teams to resolve systemic and recurring quality issues
Drive structured problem solving using RCA, 8D, FMEA, SPC methodologies
Manage critical escalations (CQN, DOA, line stops) with fast containment + permanent fix
Ensure zero-repeat mindset through closed-loop corrective action

Drive suppliers toward high maturity level and operational excellence
Define and deploy supplier quality roadmap aligned with business strategy
Lead improvement initiatives in:
- Yield & process capability
Cycle time & efficiency
Cost of poor quality reduction
Implement Lean / SPC / FMEA practices across supplier base

Resolve material quality issues impacting manufacturing line stability
Collaborate with Manufacturing, D&E, Procurement, and Supply Chain

Own supplier-side process control, validation, and quality assurance systems
Manage N-tier supplier changes, engineering changes, and qualification
Identify and mitigate supply chain risks proactively

Introduction to the job
ASML supports the semiconductor industry’s ongoing quest for producing faster, smarter and more energy efficient chips. We are a young, dynamic, international and highly skilled workforce. ASML creates the systems that the semiconductor industry needs to achieve its goals. This can only be accomplished with a strong support of our suppliers.

Do you have a passion to improve the Quality of ASML’s products and processes?

Are you experienced in Quality Assurance to drive the improvement of products, services and processes in a high-tech environment?

If you are looking for a next challenge in your career – Join ASML Supplier Audits, a team of Supplier Audit professional
Role and responsibilities
The Supplier Audit team identifies risks and drives continuous improvement in key processes at suppliers related to Quality, Logistics, Technology, Cost reduction and Sustainability (QLTCS) performance.

As Supplier Lead Auditor you act as an independent expert to identify risks, verify risk mitigations and drive quality improvements at suppliers and in the ASML supply chain.

The Supplier Lead Auditor plans, executes, and leads cross-sector audits versus defined ASML requirements and standards. He/she supports the Category Management and Supplier Account Teams in driving effective resolution of key quality, logistics, or technology issues in the supply chain by executing theme audits at suppliers. Because of risk based supplier audits, QLTC risks are identified before supplier selection via focused selection audits.

Together with the category management the supplier strategy is translated in an agreed audit plan. This includes the alignment with the worldwide audit strategy. To drive impact, audits are managed end-2-end, from planning, to execution and follow-up. Regular status updates are provided to the cluster, categories and other stakeholders. Finally the verification of the improvements is done in collaboration with the supplier account teams.

Next, the Global Quality lead auditor team owns the audit process and the Supplier Lead Auditor supports the audit process by identifying best audit practices for the Global Supplier audit team.
Education and experience
Master or Bachelor degree in Engineering, Science or Management Sciences.

Seniority and broad experience in: supplier management, manufacturing, logistics, development & engineering.
> 5 years working experience preferably at ASML or other high-tech companies, working with complex products and processes
Auditing experience, preferably in semiconductor industry
Broad experience with different technologies (e.g. mechatronics, optical etc.)
Experience with new product introductions at suppliers
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Certified ISO9001 Lead Auditor or equivalent
Good knowledge of International Quality Standards e.g. ISO9001, ISO14001
Broad expertise of Quality tools: QFD, FMEA, Design Reviews, Design for Reliability, Ishikawa, 5 Why analysis, 8D, MSA, SPC, statistical methods, value stream analysis, Kaizen events, brainstorming sessions
Expertise in risk management
Experienced in project management
Broad manufacturing knowledge: World-class operations, Flow-production, Lean Manufacturing, Cleanroom standards and procedures, 5S etc.

Strong personality with natural authority towards supplier and audit team
Independent, objective personality acting with integrity
Organizational knowledge and business sense (good feeling where “win – win” can be obtained for ASML and suppliers)
Strong communication skills
Strong analytical skills to identify key issues and associated risks as well as their root causes
Strong networker with good negotiation and team building skills

Reports to Manager - Supplier Collaboration (Audit, Quality & Logistics)
Functions as part of the ASML Global Quality audit team
Interfaces with internal stakeholders at ASML & external key suppliers
Contributes to the continuous improvement of the Supplier Audit framework of ASML

The position requires frequent travelling up to ~50%

ASML is seeking an experienced technical project manager to play a key role in bringing critical modules from development into high‑volume manufacturing. In this position, you will drive sourcing, industrialization, and manufacturing readiness in line with the EUV Source product roadmap.

ASML US, LP brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.
Job Mission
We have an exciting opportunity for a Staff Laser Scientist to join a dynamic and innovative Source Research team, focused on conceiving and demonstrating the technologies required for next generations of high-power Laser Produced Plasma Extreme Ultraviolet (LPP-EUV) light sources and DUV lasers. Our light sources rely on a wide range of unique and challenging technologies, ranging from laser light amplification and high-power optical systems to laser produced plasma for EUV generation, electro-optical signal detection and algorithm-based actuation for process control. We invite you to bring your passion, knowledge, and expertise in applied physics, plasmas, metrology, optics, controls, lasers, and experiment design to advance these technologies.

Strategic Sourcing & Procurement (SS&P) Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) department bridges product development and supply chain volume operations by securing material availability, Bill of Material readiness, logistics implementation, and supplier readiness through the Product Generation Process (PGP). As SS&P PL Logistics, you represent SS&P with a logistics focus in a product team under delegated responsibility. The role focuses on the logistics-critical path from definition through ready-for-volume. You translate product and integration plans into logistics consequences, drive timely availability of SS&P PGP logistics deliverables, and proactively identify and mitigate product-level logistics risks before they become material escalations.

Represent SS&P with a logistics focus in the product team under delegated responsibility, ensuring two-way alignment between the product team and SS&P.

Introduction to the job
At our Berlin site, our employees manufacture key components for ASML lithography systems. As part of our precision manufacturing team, you support the production of optical components, assemblies, and systems made of glass, glass-ceramics, and ceramics for our high-tech small-batch, single-part, and prototype production.
As a Strategic Space Planning Engineer, you will shape the long-term development of production and laboratory facilities across the entire campus. The role focuses on analyzing future space requirements, developing and evaluating different planning scenarios, and creating sustainable concepts to support growth, transformation, and evolving business needs. You will operate in an environment characterized by continuous change and long-term strategic decision-making.
The emphasis of this role is on strategic space and site planning rather than the operational planning or optimization of day-to-day manufacturing processes, such as material flow planning or cycle time improvements.
Role and responsibilities
As a Strategic Space Planning Engineer, you will:
Own and further develop the long-term space planning process for cross-functional space demand planning across manufacturing, research, and development areas.
Coordinate annual planning cycles with business stakeholders and translate future requirements into an integrated space development plan.
Analyze, model, validate, and interpret complex data to enable sustainable planning decisions.
Conduct scenario analyses and feasibility assessments to evaluate future space requirements and development options.
Develop, challenge, and optimize space and layout concepts to support long-term campus objectives.
Evaluate the effectiveness of implemented planning measures, identify improvement opportunities, and continuously enhance planning approaches and processes.
Prepare decision-making materials and recommendations for senior stakeholders and contribute to the long-term strategic development of factory and campus planning.
Education and experience
Degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Factory Planning, or a comparable technical discipline.
Several years of experience planning and developing space concepts and space requirements within a manufacturing environment.
Strong knowledge of demand planning, scenario modeling, and data-driven decision-making processes.
Experience analyzing large datasets, evaluating data quality, and translating analytical findings into robust planning recommendations.
Good understanding of industrial facilities, technical infrastructure, and the spatial requirements of technical equipment and organizational functions.
Experience working with planning and visualization tools, including CAD-based environments.
Professional proficiency in German and English.
Skills
The role requires strategic thinking, analytical strength, and the ability to bring together different business requirements. To thrive in this role, you will need the following skills:
Strategic mindset with a focus on long-term space and site development.
Analytical and data-driven approach to complex challenges.
Ability to quickly identify relationships, dependencies, and implications.
Confident communication with a wide range of stakeholder groups.
Ability to balance competing priorities and interests.
Strong ownership and a structured way of working.
Continuous improvement mindset and willingness to learn.
Other information
What we offer
Job with bright future prospects at an innovation leader in the semiconductor industry in Berlin Neukölln
Remuneration according to company collective agreement (with IG Metall) including 13th monthly salary and variable remuneration components
Collective working time: 35 hours/week
Flexible arrangement of your daily working hours (depending on the work area)
30 days of vacation

Participation in the Employee Share Purchase Plan (ESPP)
Specific advanced training and development opportunities
Access to organized childcare and vacation care
Comprehensive health and well-being programs

Diversity and inclusion
ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. Dein Arbeitsumfeld
An unserem Standort in Berlin fertigen unsere Mitarbeitenden Schlüsselkomponenten für die ASML Lithografiesysteme. Als Teil unserer Präzisionsfertigung unterstützt du bei der Produktion optischer Komponenten, Baugruppen sowie Systeme aus Glas, Glaskeramik und Keramik für unsere High-Tech-Kleinserien, Einzelteil- und Prototypenfertigung.
Als Ingenieur:in Strategische Flächenplanung gestaltest du die langfristige Entwicklung von Produktions- und Laborflächen auf dem gesamten Campus. Im Fokus stehen die Analyse zukünftiger Flächenbedarfe, die Entwicklung und Bewertung verschiedener Szenarien sowie die Erarbeitung nachhaltiger Konzepte für Wachstum, Transformation und sich stetig wandelnde Geschäftsanforderungen. Dabei bewegst du dich in einem Umfeld, das von kontinuierlicher Veränderung und langfristigen Entwicklungsentscheidungen geprägt ist.
Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf der strategischen Flächen- und Standortplanung und nicht auf der operativen Planung oder Optimierung laufender Produktionsprozesse, beispielsweise im Bereich Materialfluss oder Durchlaufzeiten.
Deine Aufgaben
Als Ingenieur:in Strategische Flächenplanung wirst du:
den langfristigen Flächenplanungsprozess der bereichsübergreifenden Flächenbedarfsplanung für Fertigungs-, Forschungs-, Entwicklungsbereiche verantworteten und weiterentwickeln.
jährliche Planungszyklen mit den Fachbereichen koordinieren und zukünftige Bedarfe in eine integrierte Flächenentwicklungsplanung überführen.
komplexe Daten analysieren, modellieren, validieren und interpretieren, um nachhaltige Planungsentscheidungen zu ermöglichen.
Szenarioanalysen und Machbarkeitsbewertungen durchführen, um zukünftige Flächenbedarfe sowie Entwicklungsoptionen zu bewerten.
Flächen- und Layoutkonzepte erarbeiten, kritisch hinterfragen und im Hinblick auf strategische Campusziele optimieren.
die Wirksamkeit umgesetzter Planungsmaßnahmen bewerten, Verbesserungspotenziale identifizieren und Planungsansätze sowie Prozesse kontinuierlich weiterentwickeln.
Entscheidungsvorlagen und Empfehlungen für Senior Stakeholder erarbeiten und zur langfristigen strategischen Weiterentwicklung der Fabrik- und Campusplanung beitragen.
Deine Qualifikation
Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich Ingenieurwissenschaften, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Fabrikplanung oder einer vergleichbaren technischen Fachrichtung.
Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Planung und Weiterentwicklung von Flächenkonzepten und -bedarfen innerhalb eines Produktionsumfelds.
Fundierte Kenntnisse in Bedarfsplanung, Szenario Modellierung und datenbasierten Entscheidungsprozessen.
Erfahrung in der Analyse umfangreicher Datensätze, der Bewertung von Datenqualität sowie der Überführung analytischer Ergebnisse in belastbare Planungsempfehlungen.
Gutes Verständnis von Industriegebäuden, technischer Infrastruktur und den räumlichen Anforderungen technischer Anlagen sowie organisatorischer Einheiten.
Erfahrung im Umgang mit Planungs- und Visualisierungstools einschließlich CAD-basierter Umgebungen.
Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse.
Deine Kompetenzen
Die Rolle erfordert strategisches Denken, analytische Stärke und die Fähigkeit, unterschiedliche Anforderungen zusammenzuführen. Dafür bringst du folgende Kompetenzen mit:
Strategischer Blick für langfristige Flächen- und Standortentwicklung
Datenbasierte und analytische Herangehensweise an komplexe Fragestellungen
Fähigkeit, Zusammenhänge und Abhängigkeiten schnell zu erkennen
Souveräne Kommunikation mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdergruppen
Geschick im Ausbalancieren unterschiedlicher Interessen und Prioritäten
Hohe Eigenverantwortung und strukturierte Arbeitsweise
Kontinuierlicher Verbesserungsanspruch und Lernbereitschaft

zukunftssicherer Arbeitsplatz bei einem Innovationsführer der Halbleiterindustrie in Berlin Neukölln

Introduction to the job
Job Mission
Our goal is to improve operational control and prepare our supply chain for 2030
The role of an engagement manager is to identify and drive sustainable improvements, fact-based and in a collaborative way. You support the ASML SAT (Supplier Account Team) and Supplier shoulder to shoulder. You define and prioritize the right actions for ASML.
As Supplier Collaboration Engagement Manager you will lead a team of Supplier Collaboration professionals in their assignments to drive the transformation at ASML suppliers. For your team members this requires the identification of areas of improvement, solution design, and implementation. Examples include transformation of procurement organization, drive of equipment expansion, structuring of NPI process, working with supplier senior managers and offloading / outsourcing of critical capacity.
You act as their escalation channel into line management of the account teams, support them to drive their engagement by managing stakeholders across ASML, and drive the development of a standard Way of Working and sharing of lessons learned across engagements.
Drive structural change (projects) within ASML that have been identified in the supplier engagements, thus working with a broad range of (senior) stakeholders and sectors – ensuring that the ‘handshake’ we make with suppliers as part of supplier engagements gets executed and prioritized as expected.
In summary, during a supply collaboration engagement, as lead you will
Ensure clear assignment objective at start ‘address business need’
Define & coordinate right actions, mobilize resources ‘lead the way’
Drive progress and ensure right conditions ‘make it happen’
Provide transparency on progress and impact ‘move the needle’
Align and drive transition to regular organization ‘ensure change is owned’
Coach SC experts, analysts and other support ‘collaborate & care’
Role and responsibilities
Program Management Strategy and Methodology
Has extensive experience with project / program methodologies, project reporting, risk analysis and using ASML's project management tools. Ensures application and adhere to program methodologies and standards (e.g. Project Management, Key Decision, ASML Development Model, Manage Successful Programs) as applied within multiple sectors.
Program scope definition
Plans and leads the delivery of a range of information gathering, analysis, and stakeholder consultation activities. Specifies, negotiates, and agrees on project deliverables.
Business Needs / Improvements
Plans and coordinates the identification, elicitation of requirements; conducts analysis of those requirements for completion and alignment; documents and manages requirements throughout the life of the project; and coordinates the verification of the end deliverable. Builds and reviews improvement solutions and develops recommendations for implementation of those improvements. Generally done at the project level.
Program Planning / Roadmap
Drives the production of and approves project plans, ensuring that all activities are identified, appropriately organized to deliver program and project objectives, comply with the organization's project and program management framework, and comply with the organization's wider governance structure and processes.
ProgramTeam Management
Leads medium project and program teams (or multiple small to medium teams); defines the project/program vision and communicates the outcomes needed along with guidance to achieve outcome, manages resources across projects/programs; negotiates flow of additional team members on and off the team as needed; and builds the capability of the team through training, coaching and mentoring.
Program Resource Management
Negotiates and manages deployment of project resource budgets, providing forecasts and presenting variances with narrative at appropriate review points to ensure effective utilization.
Program Governance
Ensures that roles and responsibilities are clearly defined within the project delivery and project management office teams, and ensures project compliance with ASML's wider program and/or portfolio management decision-making structures and processes.
Stakeholder Management and Advising
Manages a complex organizational environment with tactical stakeholders, needs to acquire management buy-in (at least JG 13/14 level), both internal and at supplier
Develops and implements stakeholder engagement plans for projects to identify relevant stakeholders, to develop positive stakeholder relationships, and to ensure that each stakeholder has an appropriate share of voice.
Program Risk and Issue Management
Manages identification of risks, issues, dependencies, and constraints associated with the project, escalating these where appropriate. Ensures adequate risk assessment of (high) cross-sector risks within the full scope of the roadmap and is able to interpret the results of the risk assessment. Where risks or issues threaten delivery of the project, develops and agrees recovery plans or, if relevant, together with sponsor/project board agrees to pause or cancel the project.
Program Review / Reporting
Specifies and leads the delivery of the project review process to ensure that stakeholders are able to evaluate progress and agree on change at appropriate points.
Program Benefit Realization
Develops and manages the delivery of a plan to evaluate and track business benefits and to identify actions needed to maximize these.
People Development
Ensures continuous and open lines of communication and feedback. Gives feedback to team members and peers on their behavior as team member and helps them to improve. Leads, engages and motivates PL's and project team members
Education and experience
Master’s degree in management/ business, industrial engineering, supply chain, engineering (mechanical, electrical, physics) or equivalent
>10 years of experience related to job mission as described above (e.g. head of manufacturing, head of supply chain management, supplier development manager, head of engineering department in semi-con industry)
Experience in running operations/ supply chain / program management
Proven track record of improvement project involving cultural change
Operational Excellence experience and continuous improvement mindset

As a Supply Chain and Sourcing manager within the ASML Strategic Sourcing and Procurement sector (SS&P), you will make a real difference by driving the end-to-end introduction and industrialization of ASML’s products from a Logistics, Cost, and Quality point-of-view, following ASML’s Product Generation Process (PGP). Introduction to the job
As the System Electrical Domain Architect in San Jose, you define and steer system-level, domain-specific architectural direction and act as the decisive authority when domain performance, risk, and interface conflicts arise between sub-systems. You lead system-level domain architecture topics (e.g., dedicated architecture sessions) and apply deep, up-to-date expertise in your domain while maintaining a system-wide overview across functions and modules. You translate abstract requirements into executable architecture that balances business context, domain considerations, and system requirements, ensuring a multi-domain balanced solution across relevant business drivers. In doing so, you lead technical teams, align and convince diverse stakeholders, and clearly communicate complex technical topics within ASML processes and domain-specific ways of working (WoW).
You define the scope and work breakdown for the domain architecture of a single product or multiple products within a small set of MDUs (<10) or a small NPI (typically <100 FTE) and drive the domain vision for the product(s) you own. You align across Foundation Heads of Domain, System Engineering, and the MDUs in scope, balancing domain aspects across all relevant modules to ensure overall product performance. You take an initiating role in innovations within your domain and translate customer questions related to your domain into clear, actionable architectural direction within the product.
Role and responsibilities
In this role, you are responsible for end-to-end system domain architectural accountability by ensuring full lifecycle compliance to domain requirements and standards, delivering an optimized and balanced multi-domain architecture decomposed into sub-systems, and safeguarding architectural coherence, robust boundary conditions, domain performance, and domain interfaces across sub-systems within the product(s).
Deliver system level domain specific SEG documents and provide input for design rules.
Create domain specific PBS items, and work with SE and D&I teams to optimize work breakdown.
Coach technical team on architectural skills.
Deliver system level domain specific SEG documents.
Align architectural requirements with MDU (domain) architects/technical lead.
Review architectural work for the relevant sub-systems.
Include in architecture setup roadmaps and business needs, in alignment with overarching product, sectors and foundation guidelines.
Identify required studies in the domain.
Identify and mitigate domain risks.
Giving direction on domain roadmaps and their connection to SE roadmap.
Escalate architectural risks, conflicts or scope decisions to the Head of Domain Architecture.
Contributes to Architect Development Programs and Architect Community to develop talent.
Education and experience
BS in engineering or in relevant technical field.
MSc or PhD preferred in relevant technical field.
Extensive experience (typically 10+ years) in defining and realizing an architecture within the relevant Domain.
Experience in different sub-systems or different business lines, as Domain Architect responsible for a function.
Proven ability to make sound decisions in ambiguous situations where scale and scope are not fully defined.
Naturally associated with the domain within a product. Widely recognized by others to get technical direction within the product.
Technical leader with seniority within the domain and high impact on technical domain decision within the product.
Skills
Technical & functional skills
System-Level Domain Architecture Governance: Defines and steers system-level domain architecture topics and acts as the decisive authority to resolve domain performance, risk, and interface conflicts between sub-systems.
End-to-End Domain Requirements & Architecture Delivery: Translates abstract requirements into executable system domain architecture, delivering system-level domain SEG documentation and ensuring full lifecycle compliance to internal/external standards across the product(s).
Multi-Domain Sub-System Integration, Roadmaps & Risk Control: Drives an optimized, balanced multi-domain architecture decomposed into sub-systems by aligning roadmaps and business needs with SE/foundation guidelines, reviewing sub-system architecture, identifying required studies, and proactively managing/escalating domain risks, conflicts, and scope decisions.
Proven capability to define the end‑to‑end electrical system architecture across subsystems (power, SEM e-beam control, signal, safety, EMC), translating system requirements into robust electrical concepts, design principles and interfaces while ensuring system performance, reliability, safety, compliance, cost target  across all subsystems.
Strong capability to perform electrical trade‑offs, steer design decisions across modules and functions, and identify and mitigate technical and architectural risks early in the development cycle while being able to balance short-term project needs with long-term roadmap considerations. Introduction to the job
As a system performance engineer, you will test our deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography systems after they are fully assembled in the cleanroom factories. A remarkable and unique environment to work in
Find out more: ASML IN ONE MINUTE  .
Role and responsibilities
Running the business: As a system performance engineer, you will accurately calibrate, qualify and perform manual actions on our DUV systems according to agreed specifications, quality standards and delivery times by logging in to the machine via your laptop. You recognize and report (structural) problems and give support in solving these problems when required. Communication is key: identifying, informing and involving the relevant stakeholders is crucial to keep the process running.
Improving the business: Be involved in working on improvements. Identify waste in our processes and contribute/take the lead in initiating improvement projects that leads to cycle time reduction by using 4C, A3 and just do it as problem solving methods.
As a system performance engineer you’ll focus on:
Quality: perform calibration, adjustment, performance and system qualification tests on ASML products and/or (sub) systems in accordance with established specifications. Recognize and report (structural) problems and give support in solving these problems when required;
Production: ensure system progress by achieving an amount of tests guided by strict procedures;
New Products: contribute to the pilot process and transition from pilot to volume production. Execute and improve procedures, processes, protocol etc;
Teamwork: able to work in a multi-cultural team with mutual respect within a high-tech environment. Contribute to the team by sharing your knowledge amongst your colleagues. Bring up improvement ideas and contribute to implement them when feasible and possible;
Knowledge and skills: acquire sufficient knowledge of new and established products and processes, modifications, sub-modules and complete systems;
Reporting: process and administrate information in SAP and reporting of the machine status in the machine logbook according to the way of working;
Communication: synchronize, plan and execute manual adjustments. Inform technical support in case of disturbances. Keep the system owner/team leader informed in case of disturbance in progress. Inform the material handler in case of material ordering or returning;
Education and experience
secondary vocational degree (MBO+) in mechatronics, electronics, mechanics, software or VAPRO-C. MBO candidates are only considered if they posses a minimum of 1-2 years of relevant work experience;
bachelor's degree (HBO) in mechanics, electronics, mechatronics or computer science;
Preferred: experience in a high-tech production environment, e.g. electronics, ICT hardware, aircraft construction, precision engineering or maintenance.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve. Being creative and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive as a system performance engineer, you’ll need the following skills:
Excellent communication skills in English;
Interest in other technical and business processes;
Independent, enterprising, purposeful and flexible;
Service orientated and team worker;
Structured way of working;
Able/willing to work mainly with computers in a remote testing environment.
Manual skills to be able to perform adjustments, part swaps etc
Troubleshooting and analytical skills
Other information
Please take the time to write your motivation for this specific position. Write about why you find your experience and profile matching with this vacancy. Without a motivational letter we will not process your application.
The Engineer will:
- Work in a 5 shift schedule (this includes working weekend days and night work). This schedule is cycle of 10 days: 2 x morning shift (07.00 – 15.30), 2 x evening shift (15.00 – 23.30), 2 x night shift (23.00 – 07.30) followed by 4 days off. So this schedule is repeating itself every 10 days.
- Be working in a clean room environment in a special suit and wearing a mouth cap

Introduction to the job
ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics.
The Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) team that you will lead is responsible for the introduction, industrialization and phase-out strategies of new products as well as engineering sustaining activities on existing products. In this role, you’ll make a real difference to the efficiency and profitability of the company by determining and managing the supply chain project plan of platforms, new products, associated introduction types (new builds, installs and upgrades), industrialization, and phase-out strategies. To achieve this, you will be using a mix of technical, creative and interpersonal skills to guide, coordinate, and mentor your team to meet program deliverables and deadlines.
Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler Arizona, San Jose and San Diego California, Wilton Connecticut, and Hillsboro Oregon.
Role and responsibilities
Manage concurrent supply chain introduction of new product designs in the global supply chain from technical feasibility towards ramp and release-for-volume including the critical path of Bill of Material readiness, technical documentation readiness, and material availability towards prototype, pilot and volume systems and spares.
Plan & mobilize and support resources of the Strategic Sourcing and Procurement (SS&P) supplier collaboration teams to fulfill the plans.
Manage worldwide material availability balanced against customer service levels, inventory, quality, costs and risks: Identify bottle necks, prepare decisions and take actions towards engineering, suppliers, factories, field to manage the critical path both for time-to-market and ramp.
Secure that PLM team is taking full accountability and ownership in designated x-sectoral Project Delivery Teams (DT) to enable successful NPI engagement and Industrialization at suppliers by driving quality and timing of deliverables from Project Team members.
Work closely with SS&P/PLM-PL team to secure up-to-date and complete Project overviews for their respective Product Teams (PDT) and Module Delivery Units (MDU) scope and address and signal risks for timely and quality execution of the respective NPI.
Pro-actively manage resource planning and staffing of the PLM project coordinators to ensure the optimal use of capacity and capabilities.
Ownership of operational processes and KPIs tied to material availability, inventory management, end of life and excess and obsolescence.
Build and lead a high-performing PLM team, developing talent and capabilities to achieve the required level of expertise, ownership, and execution excellence.
To foster global collaboration and learning, working effectively across regions and cultures to meet operational and strategic business needs.
Education and experience
Master’s degree in mechanical, electrical, industrial engineering or similar technical education preferred.
10+ years of work experience, of which 5 years of experience in new product introductions preferably in high-tech, low-volume environments.
Skills
Result oriented, able to act under high pressure
Stakeholder management : Able to deal effectively with internal and external stakeholders both at operational and executive levels
Building a cohesive PLM team with a shared focus on PLM performance requirements based on PLM Action Card Metrics and build strong collaboration with internal stakeholders
Able to coach team members by developing trust and demonstrating role model behaviors.

Conflict navigation and constructive challenge/ being able to challenge with care

Change leadership and adaptability
Excellent professional communication in English.
Context of the position
The mission of The SS&P Product Lifecycle Management team is to drive ASML product roadmaps into lean supply chain solutions. As such, PLM is responsible for securing material availability for ASML’s new systems during proto phase, early shipping and initial ramp up. This involves the planning and release of new and changing materials (initiated by Engineering Changes EC’s) throughout the logistics chain from system development through suppliers and manufacturing to customers. In a fast-paced industry, PLM is involved in system development from day one – defining logistics requirements and identifying potential risks in suppliers’ design and production processes. In the spirit of concurrent engineering, this happens while the system is still being developed, so specifications are constantly subject to change. Hence PLM drives timely delivery of Bill of Materials of new/changed materials and technical documentation during development, and ensures supply chain and in-field infrastructures can handle the new products.

Introduction to the job
As MS LO Tool Maintenance & Repair Execution Team Lead, you will be part of the Tool Center department within Logistics Operations. The Tool Center teams are responsible for the timely registration of new tools, delivery and return of tools to EF, TF and D&E users, quality check of tools after use, and timely repair & maintenance of tools.
Your main mission within the Tool Center department will be to organize and coach your team to execute a fast and high quality tool repair & maintenance execution process, with the goal to optimize time-to-repair with the highest quality and lowest cost possible, resulting in fast tool availability, tool compliance, and high quality and safe to use tools for the tool users at EF, TF and D&E.
Role and responsibilities
The Team Lead Tool Repair & Maintenance Execution will lead a team of 10-15 technicians and logistics professionals, responsible for two main elements:
Internal Tool Repair: your team works with EF, TF and D&E to ensure a fast intake on tools on which an MN/DN is logged, meaning the tool is defect. The intake will result in either a repair in the cabin / work center, or a further assessment at Tool Center. Based on this assessment, there are various options to resolve the MN/DN:
- The technicians in your team are able to repair the tool immediately with available spare parts and/or technical skills
Spare parts need to be ordered from external suppliers to repair the tool. The tool will be stored outside the cleanroom until the spare parts arrive at ASML, at which point the tool will be repaired.
The tool needs to be send to the supplier for repair, at which point it will be handed over to the Repair & Maintenance Support team for logistical processing
In case the tool can not be repaired, in case it will be scrapped after getting scrap approval from the tool owner.
Internal Tool Maintenance: your team also works with EF, TF and D&E to ensure a timely preventive maintenance execution of tools. Preventive maintenance typically has an annual interval and can consists of calibration, certification, physical control, etc. For compliant use of tools, timely preventive maintenance of tools is critical. This can either be performed by external supplier when specific technical skills or supplier knowledge is needed, in which case it is coordinated by the Repair & Maintenance Support team, or by the Technicians in your team in case your technicians have the in-house knowledge to execute the preventive maintenance.
Spare Part & Logistics Management: your team is responsible for identifying and maintaining a pro-active stock of spare parts to ensure fast repair of tools, based on breakdown history, spare part lead times, costs and other parameters. It is also responsible for ensuring tools are made complete again if returned incomplete after usage in the factory. Lastly, your team is also responsible for ensuring tools with an MN/DN are picked up and delivered back to the work centers in a timely fashion.
Tool Lifecycle Management: your team will drive continuous improvements in the lifecycle of a tool. The ambition is to be involved in an early stage when new tools are introduced, and be an active sparring partner for the factories in ongoing design & usage improvements during the lifetime of a tool, resulting in increased tool availability and decreased tool repair costs.
We are looking for an empathic and strong people leader who can lead this team and the individual team members towards best in class performance and a continuous improvement mindset. You will do this by building constructive relationships with your internal stakeholders (EF & TF factories, D&E) and external suppliers and by initiating and sponsoring improvement proposals and successfully driving these to closure. Key responsibilities in your role include:
People management: ensure adequate organization and staffing to realize your team’s targets. Ensure proper execution of HR policies and procedures. Coaches your team members, delegate tasks, set priorities, solve problems and contribute to a productive and collaborative work environment. Set personal targets for your team members, regularly evaluating their performance.
Daily Performance Management: observe and steer day to day execution through daily performance management meetings at tier 1 / tier 2 level. Responsible for solving issues and preventing reoccurrence, and for ensuring execution of processes in line with agreed ways of working.
Tactical Performance Management: define, review and improve performance, quality and cost in the tool repair process with internal stakeholders (especially EF & TF).
Safety: ensures a safe work environment for your team and a proactive safety mindset within your team.
Quality: responsible for the high quality execution of logistical processes to support tool repair & maintenance.
Continuous Improvement: initiate and sponsor process improvement proposals and successfully driving these to closure, ensuring high quality and cost effective execution of your team’s responsibilities. Participate in cross-sector improvement projects.
Collaboration: sets up & promotes effective and open cooperation with other Logistics Operations departments, the EF & TF factories, D&E, and external suppliers.
Education and experience
Bachelor / Master level in Engineering, Technical Business Administration, or a related technical filed.
Preferably a minimum of 5 years in a coordinating or leading position
Preferably a background in engineering or technical support within ASML
Skills
Experience with a dynamic working environment
Knowledge of and experience with the MN/DN process at ASML and the importance of a fast time-to-repair
Enthusiastic, clear and empathic people manager (motivator, team builder, coach)
Service oriented mindset and excellent stakeholder management skills
Able to think in end-to-end processes and understanding the bigger picture
SAP (EWM) knowledge is preferred
Other information
The candidate will need to follow additional training and courses
A certificate of conduct (‘Verklaring Omtrent het Gedrag’, VOG) is required
Work will mostly be done in an office environment but you will be expected to be in ASML’s cleanroom on a regular basis

Introduction to the job
Do you want to be part of our dynamic and innovating working environment and lead a team to further strengthen our manufacturing process? We might be looking for you!
Job Mission
In the role, the task is to
Lead, develop and inspire a (natural) team consisting of a diverse group of technicians and engineers (inside and outside TF) that work towards a common goal. Manage the Production Process, in order to realize the planned production targets and objectives in terms of e.g. Safety, Customer Satisfaction, Delivery, Quality and Efficiency/Costs. Leading organizational change by actively driving the transformation towards the TWINSCAN Factory (TF) Flow Factory vision, required to grow the TF production capability within the current footprint and with the current amount of people.
Roles and responsibilities
The NXT system Build department is responsible for building our DUV machines
The team consists out of +/- 100 people divided into 8 teams, working in a 2-shift basic working schedule, inside the TF cleanroom.
The systems are manufactured according to a flow line concept where the role of the TL is crucial to ensure people follow and improve on the safety, quality and work standards, ensuring production line meets hourly, shift and daily output targets.
Your job will include to:
Manage people effectively: hire, develop, set goals, and monitor performance to keep your team engaged.
Build self-supporting, collaborative teams that work well together.
Lead by example: demonstrate TF behavioral anchors like listening, following standards, taking ownership, speaking up, improving processes, and showing respect
Ensure training and compliance with ASML processes, quality, and safety standards.
Plan resources for both short- and long-term needs, aligned with market demand.

Motivate and support your team, fostering continuous improvement to boost quality, reduce costs, and increase customer satisfaction.
Drive problem-solving and set priorities within the team.
Maintain Operational Excellence in manufacturing.
Lead change by actively driving and promoting the TF Flow Factory vision.
Respond promptly to issues raised by team members or customers.
Support New Product Introductions (NPIs).
Set and enforce norms and standards, ensuring process adherence.
Manage stakeholders, both internal and external.
Main drivers: Safety, Quality, Delivery performance, Customer satisfaction, Cost effectiveness, Inventory and People engagement
Education and experience
We are looking for candidates with a relevant (technical) bachelor or master degree with multiple years of experience (at least 5 years) in leading a team.
Additionally you have:
Experience in (flow) production management;
Experience in a complex working environment;
Experience in LEAN and FLOW as a (Natural) Team Leader;
Experience in leading and coaching improvement projects.
Lastly you have excellent communicational abilities and can use English (written and verbally) with ease.
Skills
Together is the only way. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues.
You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems. To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Lead by example and “walk the talk.”
Inspire and empower your team with motivation and trust.
Show care, challenge constructively, and collaborate with all team members.
Coach and teach using a servant leadership approach.
Build high-performing teams and encourage diversity.
Be visibly present on the shop floor at least 80% of the shift.
Communicate clearly and give/receive feedback regularly.
Stay results-focused while showing empathy and cultural awareness.
Perform under pressure and solve problems pragmatically.
Take ownership of your area and act responsibly.
Think beyond your team, considering upstream and downstream impacts.
Foster strong relationships with partners, suppliers, and customers.
Delegate effectively and develop diverse perspectives.
Drive change by translating strategy into clear goals and mindset.
Celebrate success and show appreciation.

The TWINSCAN Factory (TF) is responsible for the production of ASML lithography systems including planning and logistics. A place where we strive to be the role model Flow Factory where quality comes first but where safety goes before all.

Introduction to the job
Hollow-core photonic crystal fibers are critical components for ASML’s advanced light sources, which power our metrology systems. Producing these fibers requires state-of-the-art glass manufacturing technologies, highly specialized cleanroom facilities, and a strong focus on quality control, safety and detail-oriented work. The technical challenges are diverse, ranging from controlling hydrodynamic effects during fiber drawing to machine conditioning, process stability, glass craftsmanship and advanced qualification. At the same time, the role offers a unique opportunity to contribute in a small, highly specialized team working at the interface of academic know-how and industrial high-tech manufacturing.
Role and responsibilities
As a Fiber Drawing Technician, you work in a cleanroom-based, high-tech fiber manufacturing facility where you take responsibility in the operational drawing and qualification of ASML’s specialized optical fibers. You participate across the full fiber drawing process: from raw material characterization and preform assembly to fiber drawing, qualification, documentation and preparation for shipment.
You identify opportunities to improve yield, quality and way of working, and you share these with senior engineers and management. You bring craftsmanship, attention to detail and a hands-on mindset to help realize fiber material that meets unique technical and quality requirements.
You work closely with a specialized team of fiber drawing experts, engineers and a technology partner in an international high-tech environment.
You report within the local team and interact with stakeholders in Erlangen and Veldhoven.
Key deliverables include providing sufficient high-quality fiber material on time, contributing to a safe and good working environment, and helping keep the facility, equipment and processes at a high standard.
Education and experience
You have a vocational education (German: Ausbildung), or a B.Sc. degree in Fine Optics, Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Glass Technology or a comparable technical field, combined with 1–3 years of relevant work experience.
Candidates with a higher degree or a different technical background are also encouraged to apply if they bring relevant hands-on skills, curiosity and motivation to learn.
Affinity with fine mechanical work, precision handling and craftsmanship with glass or delicate technical components is essential.
Skills
Hands-on experience with optical fibers, specialty fibers, hollow-core fibers, glass processing or comparable precision manufacturing.
Experience with qualification techniques such as SEM, optical microscopy, dimensional inspection or optical transmission testbeds.
Experience with raw material inspection, quality control, or documentation in a technical environment.
After onboarding and training, you are able to work independently, follow agreed procedures and escalate deviations or risks in a timely and structured way.
Affinity with stock management, basic data analysis, statistical thinking and logistics to support reliable fiber delivery to different ASML locations.
Experience with maintenance, troubleshooting in a production or laboratory environment.
Hand-on experience in technical problem solving to bring a delicate process back in control. You are comfortable working in cleanroom areas and high-tech facilities, and you understand the importance of discipline, safety and quality in such environments.
You have a strong motivation to secure reliable fiber output and contribute to continuous improvement of equipment, processes and ways of working.
You embrace ASML’s international and diverse working environment, communicate clearly, and stay focused on quality and continuous improvement. You are eager to learn, expand your technical skills and contribute to a small, remote team with a strong sense of ownership. Fluency in English is required; German language skills are a big plus. You are comfortable working in a small, remote team.
If you are motivated by hands-on precision work, high-tech manufacturing and continuous learning, we encourage you to apply.
Other information
You report to a team leader, delivery team lead or location manager. The primary work location is Erlangen, Germany. Occasional business trips to ASML headquarters in the Netherlands are required (especially at the beginning of your journey at ASML).

Introduction
ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
Role and responsibilities
ASML is seeking a Test & Measurement Lead Engineer with multidiscipline competencies (mechanical, electronics, test software, integration, troubleshooting, testing) to join the Wilton, Connecticut Development Location. We are seeking an individual with a very strong background in test design, test execution and data quality.
The Test & Measurement Lead Engineer masters the Test & Measurement Facilities (TMF) WoW and at least one or more TMF disciplines. Understands the ASML Development & Engineering WoW (Way of Work) and how this relates to TMF. Suggests product and process improvements to prevent reoccurring errors or failures.

You will work closely with Legal & Compliance and Government & External Affairs to translate trade compliance regulations and geopolitical developments into clear direction for Sourcing, Supply Chain and Procurement, ensuring the organization remains resilient and future-proof.
Role and responsibilities
The SS&P Trade Compliance & Geopolitical Manager establishes and drives the strategic Trade Compliance and Geopolitical Risk agenda within Sourcing, Supply Chain and Procurement. The role combines subject matter expertise, stakeholder influence and capability development to ensure trade compliance, proactively manage geopolitical risks, and embed these considerations into supplier strategies, category management and business decision-making.
By connecting external developments with internal execution, the role enables SS&P to operate compliantly, resiliently and competitively in an increasingly dynamic global environment.

Act as the SS&P focal point for Trade Compliance and Geopolitical topics, leveraging expertise from Legal & Compliance subject matter experts where required.

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Supply Chain, International Business or a related field.

Introduction to the role
Over the past decades, ASML has grown exponentially, and as we rely heavily on our supply chain, so has our supply chain ecosystem. In the coming years, we expect further growth that will require a transformation of large parts of our Supply Chain. In order to tackle this strategic challenge and help shape & drive the transformation in our supply chain, we created the "Supply Chain Transformation" department within Strategic Sourcing & Procurement. Within this department, a team of professionals in Supply Chain management disciplines will drive engagements/change programs in our supply chain and be supported with specific competencies from across ASML.
Strategic Sourcing & Procurement collaborates closely with our supply chain partners to enhance their operational performance across the QLTCS domains—Quality, Logistics, Technology, Cost, and Sustainability. The day-to-day operational activities are managed within the framework of supplier clusters. To drive transformation, the Supply Chain Transformation team leads initiatives that focus on evolving the business. This includes maintaining continuous and transparent communication channels, providing constructive behavioral feedback to team members and peers, and supporting their development. The team also plays a pivotal role in inspiring, engaging, and guiding cross-sector and project team members to achieve shared goals.
As a Supply Chain Transfer Manager, you will lead cross-functional teams responsible for managing critical supply chain transfers. Your goal is to ensure the timely and reliable availability of materials, working closely with stakeholders across technical and operational disciplines. You’ll drive project progress, safeguard supply continuity, and play a key role in managing transitions in our supply chain.
Role and responsibilities
The Supply Transfer Manger is responsible for:
Manage and lead multi-disciplinary technical orientated cross-sector transfer team
Establish clear project governance and align with internal and external stakeholders on goals and plans
Collaborating with stakeholders and cross-sector teams to create and maintain the transfer portfolio
Supporting resource planning to ensure successful transfer execution
Developing a comprehensive product phase-out and transfer strategy that includes:
- Capacity alignment across the entire n-tier supply chain to ensure readiness and continuity
Logistics risk mitigation, incorporating buffer strategies and last-buy decisions to safeguard supply
Definition and execution of technical release procedures for each product category in collaboration with the transfer team
Providing robust input for phase-out negotiations to support the Sourcing team with clear, data-driven recommendations
Proactively conducting supply chain risk assessments and implementing mitigation strategies to ensure material availability throughout all program phases. This includes verifying quality standards both pre- and post-shipment, and securing on-time delivery across the project lifecycle.
Managing escalations within transfers to solve bottlenecks in supply chain and avoid re-occurrence
Education and experience
A Bachelors degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.

postings.description:
Transport Materials Manager Projects & Excellence
In a nutshell

Eindhoven, Netherlands

Other technical backgrounds, Other non-technical backgrounds
