Introduction to the job
As Manager Projects & Excellence Transport Materials, you lead the transformation and continuous improvement agenda for ASML’s global transport materials domain. You improve the end-to-end performance of reusable transport materials across suppliers, factories, logistics partners and customer-facing flows. You report to the Manager Transport Materials and operate within the Planning & Delivery (P&D) sector.
You enter a complex and evolving environment in which transport material flows are not yet consistently efficient, transparent or scalable. Your mission is to create the structure, capabilities and governance required to support ASML’s growth, while safeguarding day-to-day material availability.
You professionalize and scale the transport materials supply chain by establishing clear ownership, robust planning processes, effective governance and data-driven decision-making. This includes optimizing pool sizes from a cost, availability and sustainability perspective; securing availability at the point of use; managing external maintenance and repair partners; and driving strategic improvements that reduce waste, increase reuse and strengthen operational control.
The scope is global. Success requires alignment of roles, responsibilities and ways of working across ASML entities, sectors and external partners, while connecting strategic direction to practical execution.
Role and responsibilities
The Manager Projects & Excellence Transport Materials leads the Projects & Excellence team and drives the following key areas of responsibility for the global Transport Materials organization:
Lead the operational performance, quality and continuous improvement of transport material maintenance, repair and reconditioning processes in close collaboration with external partners and internal stakeholders.
Develop, maintain and deploy the Transport Materials Excellence roadmap, including a portfolio of cross-sector improvement initiatives, Business Capability Improvement projects, data and IT-enabled improvements, standardization and governance required to achieve agreed performance targets.
Translate strategic priorities into an integrated project portfolio with clear scope, ownership, milestones, dependencies, business impact and decision requirements.
Own the Return4Reuse application and related budget, ensuring stable performance, effective deployment and continuous improvement across relevant factories and locations.
Drive the global expansion of transport material registration, track-and-trace and return processes, including deployment around Veldhoven and local factories.
Improve availability and pool-size calculation methods to enable better planning, control, standardization and scalability.
Establish meaningful operational management through clear KPIs, dashboards, data ownership and transparent performance reviews, including measures for secure transport material availability.
Create a holistic view of future transport material flows and define which activities should be performed where and by whom, supported by robust strategies and fact-based business cases.
Connect ongoing projects with capability development, ensuring that improvements are embedded in the standing organization and translated into sustainable ways of working.
Contribute to ASML’s ESG and sustainable packaging roadmap by accelerating return and reuse flows, reducing waste and CO2 impact, and embedding circular supply chain principles in daily operations.
Lead, coach and develop team members and project leads, strengthening both subject-matter expertise and project management capability.
Act as a senior stakeholder and change leader across P&D, other ASML sectors, factories, suppliers and logistics service providers.
Education and experience
8-10 years of experience in supply chain, logistics, warehousing, planning, operational excellence and/or business transformation in a complex high-tech environment.
Demonstrated managerial experience in leading teams, programs and cross-sector stakeholder fields with end-to-end improvement responsibility.
Proven experience in developing and delivering transformation roadmaps and project portfolios with measurable business outcomes.
Hands-on operational experience in transport materials, return and reuse flows, packaging, logistics operations, supplier collaboration and supply chain capability development.
Experience with maintenance, repair, reconditioning and external service-provider management is strongly preferred.
Experience in the semiconductor industry and/or high-tech equipment industry.
Experience with data-driven performance management, KPI development, dashboards, process ownership and IT-enabled improvement.
Experienced in applying Lean, Agile, BPI, operational excellence and structured problem-solving methods to improve process performance and embed sustainable change.
Fluent in English, both verbal and written.
Skills
You combine strategic thinking with hands-on delivery. You are comfortable creating direction in an environment with complex dependencies and incomplete structures, and you translate ambiguity into clear priorities, ownership and action.
Result-driven: able to act under pressure, maintain focus and mobilize stakeholders with a pragmatic, can-do mentality.
Self-propelling: demonstrates ownership, curiosity, a learning mindset and a strong drive for continuous improvement.
Structured and analytical: able to create transparency, identify root causes and turn data into decisions and scalable solutions.
Collaborative: works effectively across organizational levels and professional disciplines with an open attitude and willingness to learn and share.
Influential: excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to persuade and align senior stakeholders, experts and external partners.
Change-oriented: able to manage change, overcome resistance and persist in achieving the mission while embedding sustainable ways of working.
Strong communicator: listens carefully, communicates clearly and presents complex information effectively in both verbal and written form.
Courageous and connecting: speaks up, holds constructive conversations and connects people and initiatives to the bigger picture.
Leadership-focused: able to coach professionals, develop capabilities and balance team development with delivery commitments.
Other information
Planning & Delivery (P&D) is part of the Operations organization, together with Customer Service, Manufacturing and the supporting functions Corporate Real Estate and Environment, Health & Safety. Within P&D, the Delivery department is responsible for Freight & Customs, Warehousing and Goods Flow Management. This position is part of the Global Warehousing organization.
Transport materials are critical to uninterrupted supplier, factory and customer flows. The domain is characterized by global dependencies, multiple ownership models, external service providers and growing operational complexity. Increasing business volumes and changes in the ASML footprint require scalable processes, global standards and stronger end-to-end control.
The Projects & Excellence team connects strategy, project execution and capability improvement. It provides the structure needed to coordinate related initiatives, strengthen project management capacity and ensure that improvements are sustained across the global transport materials network.

Job Description
As a Upgrade Install and Relocation (UIR) engineer, you will be responsible for the end-to-end installations, upgrades and relocations adjustments, calibrations, qualification of ASML lithography tools, and customer communication. This role requires a multidisciplinary engineering background and hands-on experience with complex semiconductor equipment in cleanroom environments.
Key Responsibilities
Execute installation and qualification of ASML lithography systems including mechanical, electrical, and software integration.
Perform system troubleshooting, diagnostics, and root cause analysis to resolve installation issues.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams worldwide including project coordinators, system owners, technical support teams and customer representatives to ensure timely and successful system delivery.
Support continuous improvement initiatives for effective installation from preparation through execution to wrap-up including tooling.
Required Qualifications
English – Fluent or Native level
Japanese – Intermediate or above
Technical school, Bachelor’s degree or above in Mechanical, Electrical, Optical, or Software Engineering or equivalent technical discipline. However, we welcome applicants who completed other majors.

Trustworthiness

Strong communication and documentation abilities in both English and Japanese.
Proactive, professional behavior and curiosity to grow
Flexibility to travel and work in a dynamic, high-tech environment.
Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.

You will work at any customer site across Japan and possibly the world. Business trip to other sites can occur 50-90% of your life.

各種手当や制度、充実した福利厚生を整えています。
※市場動向、職場環境、そして社員一人ひとりの多様なニーズを考慮し、内容を定期的に見直し・更新しています。
1 資産形成サポート・手当
社員の将来設計から日々の生活まで、安心して働き続けられるよう、資産形成と生活支援の両面をサポートする制度を充実させています。
-確定拠出年金：月額基本給×8%を会社が拠出し老後資産の形成を支援
-従業員持株制度：給与天引きで株式購入が可能（上限あり）1年間保有で購入金額の20%プレミアム付与
-フレキシブル・ベネフィット：年に一回ポイントが付与され、旅行・レストラン・日用品など幅広いサービスに利用可能
-食事手当：食費を補填するための金額を毎月支給
-寒冷地手当：積雪地帯等で必要となるコスト等の負担を軽減するための手当を支給
2 転居サポート制度
ご入社にあたり転居が必要な方へ、当社規定に基づき各種サポートをご提供します。※当社規定による
-物件探しサポート：本人・配偶者の下見1回分の交通費と最大5泊の宿泊費を会社が負担※宿泊費の上限あり
-引越費用サポート：家財運搬などの引越費用を会社が負担
-物件契約費用サポート：物件契約時の礼金・仲介手数料・保証委託料・火災保険料を会社負担
3 キャリア支援
社員一人ひとりが自分らしいキャリアを描き継続的に成長していけるよう、多様な学習機会や挑戦の場を提供し意欲あるキャリア形成を力強くサポートしています。
-学習・研修制度：語学・技術・ソフトスキル・リーダーシップ等、多種多様なトレーニングを提供
-社内メンター制度：社員がキャリアやスキル開発を目的に社内の経験豊富なメンターとつながれる機会を提供
-社内公募制度：日本国内だけでなく海外拠点を含むASMLのポジションへ応募でき、自身のキャリア志向に沿った成長機会を追求できます
4 健康・医療サポート
社員が心身ともに健やかに働けるよう、日々の健康管理からメンタルケアまで、安心して利用できる医療・相談サポート体制を整えています。
-定期健康診断：年1回会社負担で健康診断を実施し、社員の健康維持を支援
-ストレスチェック：年1回のストレスチェックでメンタルヘルス状態を把握
-従業員相談窓口：24時間利用可能な専門窓口で、メンタル・健康・法律・家庭問題などについて相談可能
5 保険・補償制度
万一のケガや病気、長期離脱といった不測の事態にも、社員とそのご家族が安心して生活を続けられるよう、包括的な保険・補償制度を整えています。
-団体傷害保険（GPA）：業務内外のケガに対する治療費・入院費等を広く補償
-団体定期生命保険（GTLI）：万一の場合、年収の2倍（上限1億円）を補償
-団体長期障害補償（GLTD）：90日以上の長期離脱時に、給与の最大60%を補償
6 休暇・働き方
多様な働き方やライフイベントに柔軟に対応し、社員が自分らしいペースで働けるよう、充実した休暇制度と働き方の選択肢を整えています。
-特別休暇：通常の有給休暇に加え、夏季休暇・パーソナル記念日休暇など、働きやすい休暇制度を整備
-慶弔休暇：結婚・出産・ご家族の弔事に利用可能な特別有給休暇
-フレックスタイム制度（コアタイムなし※一部職種は不可）：柔軟な勤務時間の選択で多様な働き方を支援
-在宅勤務制度：対象の職種については所属チームや上長と相談の上、在宅勤務が可能
7 育児・介護サポート
社員ご自身はもちろん、ご家族のライフステージにも寄り添い安心して働き続けられるように育児・介護に関わるさまざまな休暇・サポート制度を整えています。
-産前産後休業制度
-育児休業制度
-子供の看護休暇
-短時間勤務制度
-介護休暇

The Customer Support (CS) organization is responsible for the installations, qualification, repair and maintenance of the ASML systems at customer sites and is responsible for the necessary transfer of know-how to the customer. Local site Customer Support branches perform these tasks for the customer within the specific region.
Executes system Upgrade & Installations and Relocations activities that are well-defined and works under close supervision; provides technical support for other CS activities when needed.

Requires flexibilty and openess to accommodate various work settings, locations and interactions/collaborations with different colleagues.

Problem analysis and approach
Gather all information relevant for the problem, analyze using defined means, gather additional diagnostic info if needed, execute initial approach to solve problem determined by senior engineers and with close guidance from others.

Installation

Upgrade

Based on arranged customer machine time window to arrange for all (possible) parts, tools, equipment and information / knowledge to be available at start of procedure, execute procedure under the guidance from experienced team members.

Introduction to the Job
ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography systems that are critical to producing faster, more powerful and energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service advanced systems that enable the world's leading chipmakers to create smaller, more capable semiconductor devices that power the technologies people use every day. Headquartered in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, ASML operates globally with 18 office locations across the United States, including major sites in Chandler, Arizona; San Jose and San Diego, California; Wilton, Connecticut; and Hillsboro, Oregon.
As an Upgrade Install and Relocation (UIR) Engineer, you will play a key role in bringing ASML's advanced lithography systems into production at customer sites. You will install, upgrade, relocate, qualify, and optimize highly complex semiconductor manufacturing equipment that helps customers achieve world-class performance and productivity.
Working within ASML's Customer Support organization, you will collaborate with customers, engineers, and technical experts to deliver safe, high-quality installations and upgrades. In this hands-on role, you will contribute directly to technology innovation while building trusted partnerships and helping customers maximize system performance and operational success.
Role and Responsibilities
As an Upgrade Install and Relocation Engineer, you will work closely with customers, engineers, and technical experts to install, relocate, upgrade, and optimize advanced lithography equipment. You will combine technical expertise, problem-solving skills, and teamwork to ensure systems are delivered safely, accurately, and on schedule.
You will:
Install, relocate, de-install, assemble, and qualify lithography systems and subsystems in cleanroom environments.
Execute system upgrades, modifications, and recovery activities according to established procedures and technical specifications.
Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve mechanical, electrical, and system-level issues to ensure optimal performance.
Collaborate with customers and cross-functional teams to identify and resolve technical challenges.
Analyze system performance and verify compliance with engineering, safety, and quality requirements.
Complete technical documentation, service reports, work orders, and project handovers accurately and on time.
Support continuous improvement initiatives and provide guidance to less experienced team members when appropriate.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, mechatronics, physics, electronics, or a related technical field, or two years of practical experience.
Associate degree, technical degree, military technical training, or two years of experience may be considered with relevant industry experience.
Minimum one year experience in field service, semiconductor manufacturing, equipment installation, high-technology manufacturing, aerospace, automotive, or a similar technical environment.
Minimum one year experience assembling, installing, troubleshooting, and repairing complex electromechanical equipment.
Minimum one year experience using data analysis tools, spreadsheet software, and technical reporting applications.
Minimum one year experience reading technical documentation, engineering drawings, procedures, and specifications.
Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing, vacuum systems, pneumatics, hydraulics, precision alignment, or related technologies is preferred.
Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You’ll have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems.
To thrive in this job, you’ll need the following skills:
Apply strong analytical thinking to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues.
Communicate clearly and professionally with customers, colleagues, and stakeholders.
Collaborate effectively across teams to achieve shared objectives.
Adapt quickly to changing priorities, schedules, and customer requirements.
Demonstrate ownership, accountability, and attention to detail.
Follow technical procedures while maintaining a strong commitment to safety and quality.
Learn new technologies, systems, and processes efficiently.
Build positive and professional relationships with customers and team members.
Identify improvement opportunities that increase safety, efficiency, and performance.
Work independently while maintaining alignment with team goals.
Other Information
This position is based in Austin, Texas, with on-site presence required.
This position requires 80% travel, primarily within the United States, with occasional international travel based on business and customer needs.
This position may require day, night, rotating, or on-call schedules, including weekend work and extended hours based on business and customer needs.
This position requires the ability to work in a cleanroom environment for extended periods while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses, and gloves.
The position requires sitting, walking, standing, reaching, bending, kneeling, crouching, climbing ladders, working in confined spaces, and moving throughout customer or campus locations as needed.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
Valid driver's license required.
Position works under the direction of a Manager, Supervisor, Team Lead, or Senior Engineer.

Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members.
The Company offers employees and their families, medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance. Employees are able to participate in the Company’s 401k plan. Employees will also receive eight (8) hours of vacation leave every month and (13) paid holidays throughout the calendar year. As a General Installation Coordinator (GIC) within the Upgrade, Install and Relocation (UIR) organization, you will coordinate the logistical, material, site-readiness, and administrative activities that enable safe and predictable ASML system installations, upgrades, and relocations at customer sites in Japan.
The role focuses on project preparation, both SAP-based and non-SAP material coordination, badging and site access, safety training readiness, stakeholder communication, and installation close-out. You will work closely with project teams, customer representatives, our partner TRUMPF, supply chain management (CSCM), global operation center (GOC), In Fab Logistics, EHS, local planners, IT, service coordinators, and other internal and external functional teams to keep installation execution moving smoothly.

A successful GIC brings ownership, clear communication, careful documentation, and the ability to connect people, systems, and processes across local and global teams.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare laptops for ASML and TRUMPF, and arrange badging or site access for project team members before and during installation execution.
Check ASML and customer safety training validity, including Japan full harness, and coordinate required training with local planners and the EHS team.

Manage SOs together with other coordinators and technically complete (TECO) material return after the installation is completed.
Drive continuous improvement by localizing and structuring ways of working, improving handover quality, and supporting effective customer communication.

Introduction
ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our main headquarters are located in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we also have 18 office locations around the United States- including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ, San Jose, CA and San Diego, CA.
Customer Supply Chain is responsible for all customer supply chain activities (machines deliveries, upgrades at customer sites, spare parts management), inbound and outbound flows to and from the factories.
Role and Responsibilities
The CSCM Team Leader is responsible for leading and coordinating supply chain activities to ensure the efficient flow of materials, products, and information from suppliers through delivery to customers. This role oversees daily operations, drives performance improvements, manages team execution, and serves as a key liaison between customers, suppliers, logistics providers, and internal stakeholders.
The Team Leader is accountable for meeting operational objectives, maintaining service levels, resolving escalations, and supporting strategic initiatives that improve supply chain performance, cost efficiency, and customer satisfaction.
Other responsibilities will include:
Lead, coach, and develop supply chain team members to achieve business objectives.
Manage daily supply chain operations, including planning, procurement, logistics, inventory, warehousing, and customer deliveries.

Deep understanding of supply chain and logistics processes.
Proven track record in process improvement and implementation.
Working knowledge of MRP systems.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint.
Knowledge of ASML logistics processes is a plus.
Personal Skills
Working at the cutting edge of tech, you’ll always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You won’t work in a silo. Instead, you’ll be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you’ll collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. Communication and Leadership Presence.

postings.title: Vaccum Systems Engineer
postings.description:
Vaccum Systems Engineer
In a nutshell
Location
Wilton, CT, US
Team
Design Engineering and Architecture
Work experience
10-15 years
Educational background
Physics
Chemical Engineering
Materials Science
Other technical backgrounds
Technical field
Heat and Mass Transfer
Travel
10%
Workplace type
On-Site
Fulltime/parttime
Full time
Introduction
ASML is seeking a Vacuum Systems Engineer to join our Wilton, Connecticut location in the Defectivity Module Delivery Unit (MDU). Within ASML, the Development and Engineering (D&E) sector is responsible for the specification and design of ASML products throughout a product lifecycle. The Defectivity MDU department is responsible for creating and maintaining the critical environment, including molecular and particle cleanliness, within the vacuum reticle modules inside cutting-edge Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. As a Vacuum Systems Engineer, you will play a key role in enabling next-generation EUV lithography by creating contamination-free vacuum environments for some of the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing systems.
In this role, you will help model and design gas flow from atmosphere to deep vacuum, select appropriate materials, and design cleanliness processes that support vacuum-grade performance in scanner and test-rig environments. The solutions developed in this role directly impact wafer yield, machine availability, and customer productivity.
Scope / Level of Impact
Takes full technical ownership for complex vacuum systems or gas-flow architectures, manages system impacts and cross-functional dependencies, drives resolution through technical uncertainty, and contributes standards, procedures, and evidence-based recommendations across ASML units. Identifies and mitigates risks that could impact customer performance and reliability. Serves as a recognized subject matter expert who influences vacuum and gas-flow strategy across projects, products, and ASML sites.
Role and Responsibilities
As a Vacuum Systems Engineer in the Defectivity group, you will work closely with Veldhoven machine conditioning architects, Defectivity MDU architects and leadership to specify vacuum systems and gas flows in scanners and test rigs. Partner with hardware project teams and lead designers to ensure vacuum and gas-flow requirements are successfully integrated throughout the product development lifecycle. Lead the ASML Wilton Engineer guild for machine conditioning architecture and vacuum systems competence onsite.
Translate the overall system design into a gas-flow and vacuum architecture that meets system requirements.
Specify vacuum system components, standards, and procedures and ensure they are properly recorded in Technical Product Documentation (TPD).
Define, model, and execute qualification tests to verify that the architecture or subsystem performs all specified functions and meets all performance and design requirements.
Support resolution of particle contamination issues through analysis and specification of flushing and venting procedures.
Specify pump-down and vent procedures that ensure common flow performance.
Participate in design reviews for test rigs and support functional integration of architectures or subsystems.
Execute design of experiments for degassing chambers and components on product and process levels.
Provide surface particulate and vacuum-grade cleanliness support, hands on troubleshoot escalations, and contribute practical recommendations from analysis.
Transfer vacuum systems knowledge between ASML units and frequently interact with D&E Delivery Teams, functions, competences, customer support, and research.
Perform analyses and calculations to predict flow architecture or subsystem functionality, including pressure-drop budgeting, flow budgeting, humidification, and gas purity.
Take direction from ASML System Architects and principal engineering mentors leading critical large-capital-equipment development efforts.
Follow EHS policies and proactively identify, communicate, and mitigate safety risks.
Education and Experience
Minimum education and experience expectations vary by job grade. A bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical field is required; a master’s degree or PhD is preferred depending on role scope, technical depth, and business need.
JG09: BS degree in a technical field and 9+ years of substantial experience; MS or PhD preferred. Education above a BS can compensate for years of experience depending on the candidate.
Solid theoretical and practical experience with vacuum and gas-flow phenomena and applications, preferably in the semiconductor industry will be given priority for hire.
Internal candidates familiar with Twinscan and vacuum systems ADT, vacuum systems hands-on architecture knowledge, or ASML vacuum system flow modeling will be given priority for hire.
Skills
Technical and Functional Skills
Vacuum systems and gas-flow architecture: Ability to specify vacuum systems, gas flows, pump-down and vent procedures, and architecture requirements for scanner and test-rig environments.
Cleanliness, materials, and contamination control: Knowledge of molecular and particle cleanliness, surface particulate behavior, vacuum-grade cleanliness, materials compatibility, desorption issues, and contamination troubleshooting.
Analysis, modeling, and testing: Ability to plan and execute tests and DOEs, analyze measurement results, perform pressure-drop and flow budgeting, and use evidence to make practical recommendations.
Documentation and technical communication: Ability to document standards, procedures, requirements, test evidence, and component specifications in Technical Product Documentation and present findings to varied technical audiences.
Preferred technical skills: Experience with particle transport in flows, rarefied gas flow, plasma physics, electrostatics, surface science, RGA or other vacuum measurement techniques, and calculations or simulations for gas-flow and particle transport.
Experience using modeling or simulation tools: to predict gas flow, vacuum performance, contamination transport, or thermal-fluid behavior is highly desirable.
Demonstrate: strong technical writing and communication skills.
Behavioral and Leadership Skills
Drives results: Translates technical goals into clear priorities and delivers committed outcomes with quality and ownership.
Collaborates and communicates effectively: Works across disciplines, suppliers, and stakeholders to align expectations, resolve issues, and transfer knowledge between ASML units.
Demonstrates self-awareness: Seeks and applies feedback, adapts approach, and improves collaboration in complex or ambiguous environments.
Values differences: Respects and integrates diverse perspectives to strengthen decision quality and inclusive execution.
Builds effective teams: Establishes clear goals, roles, accountability, and ways of working while coaching others as applicable.
Drives vision and purpose: Connects technical direction to business priorities and helps teams stay focused through ambiguity and change.
Ownership and adaptability: Demonstrates high energy, self-motivation, quick learning, flexibility, and the ability to handle multiple projects and tasks concurrently with minimal guidance.
Why Join ASML?
Work on technology that enables the world’s leading semiconductor manufacturers.
Solve highly complex multidisciplinary engineering challenges.
Collaborate with globally recognized experts in vacuum technology, contamination control, and lithography.
Influence future EUV and High-NA technology platforms.

Introduction to the Job
ASML is seeking a Vacuum Systems Engineer to join our Wilton, Connecticut location in the Defectivity Module Delivery Unit (MDU). Within ASML, the Development and Engineering (D&E) sector is responsible for the specification and design of ASML products throughout a product lifecycle. The Defectivity MDU department is responsible for creating and maintaining the critical environment, including molecular and particle cleanliness, within the vacuum reticle modules inside cutting-edge Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. As a Vacuum Systems Engineer, you will play a key role in enabling next-generation EUV lithography by creating contamination-free vacuum environments for some of the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing systems.
In this role, you will help model and design gas flow from atmosphere to deep vacuum, select appropriate materials, and design cleanliness processes that support vacuum-grade performance in scanner and test-rig environments. The solutions developed in this role directly impact wafer yield, machine availability, and customer productivity.
Scope / Level of Impact
JG08
Leads technically complex vacuum and gas-flow work packages, supports hardware projects and lead designers, owns defined architecture or subsystem deliverables, and drives cross-functional alignment with architects, projects, competences, customer support, and research partners. Focuses on ownership of subsystem-level vacuum and gas-flow solutions while developing broader architecture expertise across the Defectivity domain.
JG09
Takes full technical ownership for complex vacuum systems or gas-flow architectures, manages system impacts and cross-functional dependencies, drives resolution through technical uncertainty, and contributes standards, procedures, and evidence-based recommendations across ASML units. Identifies and mitigates risks that could impact customer performance and reliability. Serves as a recognized subject matter expert who influences vacuum and gas-flow strategy across projects, products, and ASML sites.
Role and Responsibilities
As a Vacuum Systems Engineer in the Defectivity group, you will work closely with Veldhoven machine conditioning architects, Defectivity MDU architects and leadership to specify vacuum systems and gas flows in scanners and test rigs. Partner with hardware project teams and lead designers to ensure vacuum and gas-flow requirements are successfully integrated throughout the product development lifecycle. Lead the ASML Wilton Engineer guild for machine conditioning architecture and vacuum systems competence onsite.
Translate the overall system design into a gas-flow and vacuum architecture that meets system requirements.
Specify vacuum system components, standards, and procedures and ensure they are properly recorded in Technical Product Documentation (TPD).
Define, model, and execute qualification tests to verify that the architecture or subsystem performs all specified functions and meets all performance and design requirements.
Support resolution of particle contamination issues through analysis and specification of flushing and venting procedures.
Specify pump-down and vent procedures that ensure common flow performance.
Participate in design reviews for test rigs and support functional integration of architectures or subsystems.
Execute design of experiments for degassing chambers and components on product and process levels.
Provide surface particulate and vacuum-grade cleanliness support, hands on troubleshoot escalations, and contribute practical recommendations from analysis.
Transfer vacuum systems knowledge between ASML units and frequently interact with D&E Delivery Teams, functions, competences, customer support, and research.
Perform analyses and calculations to predict flow architecture or subsystem functionality, including pressure-drop budgeting, flow budgeting, humidification, and gas purity.
Take direction from ASML System Architects and principal engineering mentors leading critical large-capital-equipment development efforts.
Follow EHS policies and proactively identify, communicate, and mitigate safety risks.
Education and Experience
Minimum education and experience expectations vary by job grade. A bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical field is required; a master’s degree or PhD is preferred depending on role scope, technical depth, and business need.
JG08: BS degree in a technical field and 5+ years of thorough experience; MS or PhD preferred. Education above a BS can compensate for years of experience depending on the candidate.
JG09: BS degree in a technical field and 9+ years of substantial experience; MS or PhD preferred. Education above a BS can compensate for years of experience depending on the candidate.
Solid theoretical and practical experience with vacuum and gas-flow phenomena and applications, preferably in the semiconductor industry will be given priority for hire.
Internal candidates familiar with Twinscan and vacuum systems ADT, vacuum systems hands-on architecture knowledge, or ASML vacuum system flow modeling will be given priority for hire.
Skills
Technical and Functional Skills
Vacuum systems and gas-flow architecture: Ability to specify vacuum systems, gas flows, pump-down and vent procedures, and architecture requirements for scanner and test-rig environments.
Cleanliness, materials, and contamination control: Knowledge of molecular and particle cleanliness, surface particulate behavior, vacuum-grade cleanliness, materials compatibility, desorption issues, and contamination troubleshooting.
Analysis, modeling, and testing: Ability to plan and execute tests and DOEs, analyze measurement results, perform pressure-drop and flow budgeting, and use evidence to make practical recommendations.
Documentation and technical communication: Ability to document standards, procedures, requirements, test evidence, and component specifications in Technical Product Documentation and present findings to varied technical audiences.
Preferred technical skills: Experience with particle transport in flows, rarefied gas flow, plasma physics, electrostatics, surface science, RGA or other vacuum measurement techniques, and calculations or simulations for gas-flow and particle transport.
Experience using modeling or simulation tools: to predict gas flow, vacuum performance, contamination transport, or thermal-fluid behavior is highly desirable.
Demonstrate: strong technical writing and communication skills.
Behavioral and Leadership Skills

postings.description:
Warehousing Services Manager
In a nutshell
Location
Eindhoven, Netherlands
Team
Sourcing and Supply Chain Management
Work experience
4-9 years, 10-15 years
Educational background
Other technical backgrounds
Travel
25%
Workplace type
Hybrid
Fulltime/parttime
Full time
To support our factory, ASML keeps parts, tools and packaging in Warehouses close to our factory and customers. These are outsourced to suppliers or Logistics Service Suppliers (3PL’s).
The Replenishment Hub is tasked to make sure these warehouses and suppliers are ready to support our factory in the most efficient way, which means that all facilities are fit for purpose, there is enough space and sufficient manpower and that activities are performed in line with the agreed SLA’s and budgets. Facilities in our warehouses include Clean Technology Infrastructure (such as clean rooms) to clean tooling, to make sure we supply our suppliers and factories with tools in the right quality.
Job mission
You manage specific Supplier warehouses and service centers in your assigned responsibility on:
- Budget, cost control and cost saving initiatives
- Performance and performance improvement initiatives Ensure these are operated flawlessly by the supplier by auditing on adherence of the right procedures and systems by putting proper controls in place. The growing number of produced ASML machines requires us to setup new locations or expand or relocate existing locations. It will be your responsibility to translate the business requirements into warehouse requirements and manage the infrastructure projects successfully to completion. Time, money, and (internal) customer satisfaction will be your main drivers. You will need to collaborate with a multitude stakeholders within ASML to be able to run projects, operations and process changes.
Job description
Plan and manage the budget for the suppliers in the assigned responsibility
Manage the supplier on performance through periodical business reviews (weekly / monthly)
Ensure locations stay fit for purpose at all time by driving infrastructural changes: translate parts, tools and packaging handling and storage requirements into the logistics facilities needed.
Manage the assigned budget for operations and projects
Build relationships with wide range of internal and external stakeholders, for example: Procurement, Suppliers, factory logistics etc.
Define, drive and deliver optimization projects in this domain to drive cost down, material availability up and/or performance up.
Act as a subject matter expert in your field
Education
MSc. or Bachelor in Supply Chain Management
Experience
5+ years experience in a Supply Chain or Logistics position
Experience with Project Management
Experience with Service Logistics and/or managing 3PL’s
Process standardization
LEAN
Personal skills
Self-starter and finisher
Dive into details where required, while keeping the overview and prioritizing
Able to build rapports and communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders
Travel
Up to 20% within Eindhoven region
Context of the Position
A flawless distribution network is key for a smooth supply chain. Fast and flexible transportation networks, differentiated warehousing solutions and complex value-added services are some characteristics of our landscape. Different requirements towards our supply-chain due to development of our systems, the number of upgrades of systems on customer sites and the need for differentiated service level agreements drive the need for a flexible 3PL network. Hence the Global Warehousing Services department is responsible for managing and developing the supply chain / distribution infrastructure in line with business requirements and against aligned norms. A team of highly educated professionals drives the supply chain infrastructure towards 2030, focused on the rapid developments, based on market intelligence, innovations, business needs, 3PL performance and process analytics.
Other information
ASML Planning & Delivery (P&D) is an industry-leading supply-chain management organization, responsible for ensuring material availability to ASML’s factories and customers. Our DNA contains customer focus, concurrent engineering, virtual integration plus the ability to thrive in a volatile market, accelerate the supply chain and deliver creative solutions. P&D plans up to four years ahead while customer requirements and system bill of materials can change at any time. Any break in material availability can have an unacceptable impact for our customers. So, with over 700 highly educated and motivated people, P&D must proactively identify and solve potential issues by working closely together with our technical departments and customers while actively managing an extensive supplier base.

Optical Fabrication Technician
Shift: Back End Days 6am – 6pm (Thursday, Friday, Saturday, alternate Wednesday)
Introduction to the role:
You will fabricate some of the world’s most advanced optical components used in the most advanced semiconductor photolithography machines. Through your attention to detail, results orientation, and commitment to task, you will produce high precision quality optics per production schedule. You will maintain the safety and workplace organization of your processing area. You will value adherence to standards while applying your experience and perspective to contribute to continuous improvement in our processing methods. You will enjoy success generated through your individual desire to learn and through teamwork with your colleagues.
We are looking for individuals like you to work in one of our processing competencies. These include: machining glass materials into final configuration using CNC milling equipment; grinding and polishing surfaces of optical components to rigorous dimensional and surface quality specifications; loading material into and operating deposition chambers to coat optics; precisely align and assemble glass parts with a high degree of accuracy in order to produce high quality optical assemblies; measuring optical characteristics of components using advanced metrology equipment for in process material processing feedback and final quality inspection.
Role & Responsibilities:
Back End Days 6am – 6pm (Thursday, Friday, Saturday, alternate Wednesday)
“Must be willing to work a compressed work week schedule- twelve-hour long shift and rotating from three to four days a week.”

Handle delicate optical components and visually identify any abnormal characteristics.

Identify and escalate any unsafe conditions.
Identify and escalate any product or process quality concerns in a timely manner.
Perform assigned work content to support area and factory schedule execution.

Learn and apply skills to tackle progressively more challenging products.
Identify and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives in how your work is defined and performed, and more broadly within your area, to improve safety, quality, output, and cycle time.

Clean optical surfaces of all particles and contaminants.
Accurately record time and attendance.
Assist with training new and existing employees
Education & Experience:
High school diploma or GED required.
Associate degree in a vocational trade preferred.
Previous experience working in a manufacturing facility or completion of a vocational certification preferable.

Constructively challenge the status quo in search of a better way.

Self-motivated learner.
Dexterity to handle optical components with care.

ASML brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers – to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Wilton, CT, Chandler, AZ and San Jose, CA. This position will be in Wilton, CT.
Job Mission
You will effectively lead the Compressed Work Week Front End Night ( Sunday-Tuesday, alternate Saturday 6pm-6am) Optics manufacturing for Milling, Grinding, and Polishing operations. You will have managerial responsibilities for 15+ optical technicians spread across several work centers. You will ensure safe, on-time delivery of high quality product to your customers while leading improvements in process and operational effectivity and efficiency. You will continuously seek out, foster, and spearhead improvements to all aspects of your operational area. You will engage in adoption and industrialization of new products and new processes through a strong partnership with Production and Development Engineers. You love being a team player that enjoys the success of team members as much as you enjoy personal success.

Maintaining alignment of individual, team, and area goals to department and Company objectives.
